political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Marilena Raouna, President-in-Office of the Council.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: President-in-Office of the Council

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner, artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded into our economies, as well as our security infrastructure. And advanced AI systems are transforming many sectors of our economy, from healthcare to transportation, finance, energy, education and defence.

When it comes to cybersecurity, the new generation of advanced AI systems are powerful assets and, at the same time, pose significant risks. That is to say, they can help us detect vulnerabilities and build up our defences, but in the wrong hands, whether used by cybercriminals or hostile-state actors, they can also endanger our systems.

We already see this happening. AI is capable of identifying software vulnerabilities, automating sophisticated phishing attacks, and generating highly convincing disinformation. And there is no doubt that foreign malicious actors will make use of all tools at their disposal. In this regard, the European Union needs to be prepared and anticipate such threats.

Therefore, I welcome this important and timely debate. It is vital that the European Union does not fall behind. To better monitor the deployment of advanced AI models and to address our potential security concerns, we need to be involved at an early stage. Cooperation with industry is key, not only to understand technological trends, but also to shape them in line with our values and security.

The Council is following all developments closely. Regular discussions are taking place at technical level, ensuring that Member States remain both aligned and informed. The adoption of the Cyber Resilience Act was a key step in strengthening our cybersecurity. Its security-by-design approach will help reduce the number of software and hardware vulnerabilities, and it will also improve our reaction when vulnerabilities are only detected after a product has been released.

We also welcome the proposal for a new cybersecurity package that the Commission put forward at the end of January this year. As a presidency, we are fully committed to continue advancing the discussions on the new cybersecurity act which is part of this package and on which discussions have significantly advanced during the Cypriot Presidency.

The presidency also plans a dedicated discussion on advanced AI systems and cybersecurity at a meeting of the Horizontal Working Party on Cyber Issues on 1 June. We are convinced that this proposed legislation will significantly contribute to strengthening our cybersecurity.

Moreover, with the Artificial Intelligence Act, we already have a solid legislative framework that will allow us to monitor the most powerful AI models that pose systemic risks. From August this year, we will be able to enforce transparency, documentation and risk mitigation requirements, marking an important phase in the act's implementation.

But we also know that regulation alone is not enough. We must also strengthen our technological autonomy. Today, Europe remains highly dependent on external actors for critical cloud infrastructure, semiconductor supply chains, advanced computing resources or cybersecurity tools. This dependency is occurring in the context of an increasingly strategic global competition around advanced AI capability.
In this context, we look forward to the upcoming tech sovereignty package announced by the Commission. This will be an integral part of our overall strategic autonomy.

interventions.speaker_label: Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Executive Vice-President of the Commission

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you for this opportunity, for this very timely debate. Artificial intelligence can be used for good and for bad, and this applies also in cybersecurity. AI can equip cyber-defenders with powerful tools to protect our critical infrastructure. At the same time, it poses grave risks when exploited by malicious actors, and this has now expanded to a new level and pace.

These new frontier AI models possess high capabilities. They operate at a speed and level of automation that outpaces traditional defensive cycles, at the same time also lowering significantly the barrier to entry for sophisticated attacks.

The new concern is that vulnerabilities can now be identified at an unprecedented speed, reducing what would normally take months to hours, outpacing any human expertise in this field. We cannot be certain that this will be the same for fixing these vulnerabilities, and this is the risk we need to be prepared to address.

In recent weeks, we have had the launch of such models for cybersecurity by two of the most advanced AI players from the US, and it is clear that we will see more and more that kind of model entering the market also from other parts of the world.

In the face of these challenges to cybersecurity, we need to do two things. First, we need to make sure that the EU's robust legal framework is applied. And, second, see if there are remaining issues that need to be addressed.

First, under our AI Act, providers of the most advanced AI models must notify the Commission when they know they have such a model. They must also assess and mitigate systemic risks, including those arising from potential cyber‑misuse.

Second, the NIS 2 Directive requires critical infrastructure operators to take state‑of‑the‑art measures to counter all cybersecurity risks, including those stemming from the malicious use of frontier AI.

Third, the Cyber Resilience Act mandates manufacturers of hardware and software to test their products for vulnerabilities before placing them on the market and throughout their lifecycle. It also requires timely fixing of any vulnerabilities discovered. The emergence of frontier AI models makes the swift transportation and implementation of this legal framework a key priority.

The Commission will ensure that these frameworks are implemented as quickly as possible, and we will also make sure that their implementation fully addresses both the risks and the potential of AI. We have also in place a cyber‑emergency mechanism which can support preparedness testing and scanning, and we will see how to deploy the EU Cyber‑Reserve for the purpose of preparedness as a matter of priority. We are working very closely with ENISA, our EU agency for cybersecurity and national cybersecurity authorities in the Member States on this matter.

We have not waited for these models to appear to anticipate future cybersecurity capabilities. As part of the upcoming technological sovereignty package, we will focus on ensuring the maintenance, security and integrity of our open source digital infrastructures that are coming under increased cybersecurity pressure resulting from the weaponisation of AI. Our proposal for a revised Cybersecurity Act is designed precisely to equip ENISA and the Commission with the resources, powers, and clarity of mandate that this new threat picture is requiring.

ENISA is still a very small agency, compared both with the national cybersecurity agencies, but also with other security‑related Union agencies. We are also now proposing measures to ensure that information flows faster to those who need to act on it, through early alerts, and also collaboration on vulnerabilities.

To ramp up our preparedness in the face of emerging AI threats, I will also present a list of actions in the coming weeks, bringing together the best EU expertise in AI and cybersecurity, and in doing so, we will work with like‑minded partners.

Should more need to be done, we are certainly open to considering this, and this is where the European Parliament can play a very decisive role in the negotiations on the Cybersecurity Act, which we presented last January. Our proposal is a horizontal framework where we can anticipate these issues and where we need to give the EU Agency for Cybersecurity, ENISA, the powers and the scope of the mandate they need to help our Member States face these challenges.

So we count on the European Parliament's support in this respect. The Commission has been engaging closely with the providers of the recently launched advanced AI models from the very start to better understand and also anticipate their cybersecurity capabilities and how these companies plan to address associated risks.

In the current geopolitical context, where even the smallest vulnerability in our ICT supply chains can be exploited by malicious actors, AI‑powered cyber‑defences are essential to safeguarding our critical infrastructure. An essential first step in this is the rapid adoption of already‑available advanced cyber‑tools by public and private European organisations for their own cyber‑defence.

There is no reason to wait, and this is crucial for preparing for the upcoming risks, but we do not want to remain dependent on others' cyber‑defence tools. We must do more to nurture our European cybersecurity ecosystem. We have already European cybersecurity companies who boast impressive vulnerability discovery capabilities on par with the big US models. But these companies are still very small, and this is why Europe must invest in our own frontier AI and cybersecurity capabilities.

We need to encourage and support European companies to develop advanced AI models, including open‑weight models, so that in Europe we have the right conditions for sustainable cybersecurity business models to meet the challenges of today and tomorrow.

interventions.speaker_label: Michał Wawrykiewicz, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Madam Minister, Madam Vice-President, colleagues, banking systems, rail transport, cloud services and even water treatment facilities – all these services rely on digital systems that may be protected, might be tested or attacked by AI.

As we could hear today from the Commission and from the Council, AI is a double-edged sword. On one hand, it can strengthen our defences. It can detect patterns and weaknesses faster than any human operator.

But the effectiveness of any tool depends on who uses it and our enemies and our opponents are learning very fast. A cyberattack today can stop production lines, paralyse transport, disrupt hospitals, expose personal data, and weaken citizens' trust in public institutions. Cybersecurity is a strategic economic and security priority, as AI makes attacks faster, larger and more autonomous.

Advanced AI models can identify and exploit hidden software vulnerabilities and therefore mark a turning point for European cybersecurity. At stake are public safety, economic stability and democratic resilience.

Europe must act pragmatically. We need a dedicated EU strategy for AI-driven cyberthreats. Critical infrastructure and sensitive public data must not be excessively dependent on non-European clouds and AI systems.

This is not a call for isolation at all. Europe must remain open and innovative because this has always been our strategic strength, but openness without resilience would be considered as weakness. Technological sovereignty means that when it comes to the security of our citizens, Europe must be able to protect itself.

interventions.speaker_label: Ana Catarina Mendes, em nome do Grupo S&D.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: em nome do Grupo S&D

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Ministra, Senhora Comissária, caros colegas, eu julgo que o desafio maior que a União Europeia tem hoje é de saber como adaptar as nossas sociedades à inteligência artificial, como ter a inteligência artificial ao serviço das nossas democracias, reduzir as nossas dependências externas e apostar numa estratégia industrial digital europeia.

Isto implica — do meu ponto de vista e do ponto de vista do S&D —, ação, visão e estratégia. Ação, visão e estratégia porque estamos a falar de segurança económica, de defesa digital, de soberania tecnológica na União Europeia.

A inteligência artificial e as ameaças estão a transformar profundamente as nossas sociedades, a segurança, a economia, o funcionamento das nossas democracias. E os ataques já não são apenas às infraestruturas críticas, são também, mas são aos nossos sistemas eleitorais, ao espaço público europeu, e — do meu ponto de vista — isso cria uma desconfiança sobre as instituições, o que é, aliás, o objetivo de quem promove estes ataques.

É por isso que é preciso transformar a inteligência artificial numa parceira do nosso desenvolvimento e da nossa democracia, porque cibersegurança europeia é uma questão de democracia, de segurança, de proteção de dados, mas é também uma questão de competitividade.

Por isso é que é preciso que esta estratégia tenha investimento em capacidades europeias próprias, em cibersegurança, inteligência artificial confiável, semicondutores, computação de alto desempenho, cloud europeia e proteção de infraestruturas críticas, absolutamente essencial para proteger consumidores, para proteger a nossa economia, para proteger as nossas democracias.

E volto a este ponto: soberania digital significa uma estratégia industrial digital europeia que combine regulação, gestão de risco, proteção dos direitos fundamentais, reforço da resiliência cibernética e coordenação institucional.
Do que estamos a falar, Senhoras e Senhores Deputados, é mesmo de valorizar a nossa democracia e defender uma autonomia estratégica digital no espaço europeu.

interventions.speaker_label: Jaroslava Pokorná Jermanová, za skupinu PfE.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: za skupinu PfE

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, vážení kolegové, kybernetické útoky, dezinformace a zneužívání umělé inteligence už nejsou hrozbou budoucnosti, ale realitou dneška. Proto se musíme posunout od samotných regulací k reálné připravenosti a odolnosti našich států a regionů. Skutečná bezpečnost se ukáže až ve chvíli, kdy útok skutečně přijde.

Jako bývalá hejtmanka největšího kraje v České republice jsem viděla, jak ničivý může být kybernetický útok. Útok na krajskou nemocnici vyřadil zdravotnický systém téměř na rok. Nešlo jen o počítače. Dotklo se to péče o pacienty, fungování záchranného systému i každodenního života občanů.

Podobně zranitelné jsou nejen nemocnice, ale i energetické sítě, doprava nebo třeba vodohospodářská infrastruktura po celé Evropě. Jediný útok může během několika hodin ochromit chod celého státu. Za mého působení jsme například testovali scénáře blackoutů. Bylo to nákladné, ale právě taková cvičení ukazují, zda a jak jsou stát, regiony i podnikatelská sféra skutečně schopny fungovat v krizové situaci.

Evropa se musí zaměřit na připravenost a odolnost. Evropské prostředky by měly směřovat do ochrany kritické infrastruktury, testování kybernetické bezpečnosti a praktických krizových cvičení. Musí směřovat hlavně do regionů, které jsou nejzranitelnější a v těchto oblastech zaostávají. Bezpečnost dnes není jen otázkou obrany ve válce. Je to schopnost společnosti fungovat i během kybernetických útoků, blackoutů a výpadků infrastruktury. A na tuto realitu Evropa bohužel stále ještě není dostatečně připravena.

Paní předsedající, vážení kolegové, kybernetické útoky, dezinformace a zneužívání umělé inteligence už nejsou hrozbou budoucnosti, ale realitou dneška. Proto se musíme posunout od samotných regulací k reálné připravenosti a odolnosti našich států a regionů. Skutečná bezpečnost se ukáže až ve chvíli, kdy útok skutečně přijde.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, oggi parliamo di un tema di sicurezza nazionale ed europea che è il tema della cibersicurezza, sempre più forte nei confronti dei cittadini, dei singoli, delle imprese, ma anche dei settori fondamentali e strategici delle nostre nazioni.
Dico questo perché non è una semplice voce digitale, non è una semplice voce informatica: si tratta di un tema fondamentale per tutelare tutti noi e le nostre nazioni.

È infatti notizia di poco più di un anno fa un attacco hacker a uno dei server della Regione Emilia‑Romagna che si occupa di tutti i dati sanitari di quella parte dell'Italia, delle persone e dei cittadini. Provate a immaginarvi quale danno potrebbe essere creato se un server che gestisce tutti i dati sanitari dei nostri cittadini europei dovesse rimanere bloccato per diversi giorni.
È o non è una situazione di sicurezza nazionale? È o non è una situazione di sicurezza europea?

È il motivo per il quale chiediamo a gran voce, di fronte a chi dice investiamo nei cannoni, noi diciamo investiamo soprattutto nella cibersicurezza, investiamo per salvare tutte quelle persone che magari stanno aspettando una visita specialistica, un esame privato; hanno bisogno di essere tutelate e dobbiamo renderci conto che la sicurezza nazionale è, e passa, ad oggi, attraverso le piattaforme digitali.

interventions.speaker_label: Bart Groothuis, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, we stand at the brink of a potential cyber bloodbath. AI models can now hack any system on a large scale and with the speed of light. Criminals, nation states, will use these AI models against our banks, our supermarkets, and all of our society will be tested.

The good news is that these same AI models can also protect any system at scale and at the speed of light. So we have the choice between a cyber bloodbath, or to use AI as a catalyst for better cybersecurity, but there is very limited time to build resilience – months at best.

So I ask, dear Commissioner, to transform the cybersecurity agency ENISA into a dedicated AI cybersecurity task force – not in a year, not in six months, but next week. Immediately implement mandatory AI red teaming, develop and host AI powered defences, establish a certification scheme for AI cybersecurity tools so businesses know what to trust.
The choice is ours. The time to act is now.

interventions.speaker_label: Markéta Gregorová, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, the danger of what we have learned from Mythos research and the Glasswing arrangement is that AI-assisted cyber operations may compress months of expert vulnerability research into days.

For us Europeans, the new risk is not only technical; it is a strategic dependency. If the most capable defensive models and early warnings sit mainly with non-EU partners and their selected private collaborators, Europe may learn about vulnerabilities in its own critical infrastructure too late and on terms set by others. Would you keep your wealth and assets in such a jurisdiction?
The right response to a Mythos-class threat is not to be first to write new legislation; it is to use the instruments Europe already has with far more urgency.

I ask the presidency, do we have reliable access to frontier AI models? If Europe lacks trusted defensive access to Mythos-class tools, we must pool our market power, regulatory power and security intelligence to obtain it at all costs ASAP.

I also ask the presidency to activate the integrated political crisis response for AI-driven cyber threats. This should get the Union to be ready when the next mass incident hits our hospitals or schools. That is what the framework was built for. Let us use it.
And colleagues, the single market is not yet a single cyber market. Let's harmonise ambitiously. Let's lay the foundations for European cyber security.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: au nom du groupe The Left

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, vous vous rappelez cette nouvelle du Financial Times, il y a quelques semaines, où Israël avait hacké, pris le contrôle, des caméras de surveillance de la circulation à Téhéran pour ensuite organiser les tueries sur place? Cela m'a stressé parce que je vois qu'il y a beaucoup de communes et de villes en Europe qui utilisent des caméras de surveillance et des technologies de surveillance israéliennes. Jusqu'à quel point peut-on dire qu'on est en sécurité si des entreprises basées dans cet État accusé de génocide nous surveillent au quotidien?

La même chose avec des logiciels d'espionnage. L'Union européenne a financé directement, indirectement, des entreprises comme NSO, avec Pegasus ou Paragon, qui sont des entreprises qui développent des logiciels d'espionnage israéliens qui sont utilisés ensuite contre nos journalistes, contre nos infrastructures. C'est quand même incroyable qu'on finance cela. Cela ne vous inquiète pas un tout petit peu quand même?

Et aujourd'hui, on voit qu'en France, il y a la justice française qui enquête sur un scandale potentiel d'ingérence à partir d'une entreprise israélienne dans les élections communales – municipales – françaises. Alors moi, ça, c'est la première chose qui me stresse, parce que c'est ce qu'il y a déjà sur le territoire européen.

Et je pourrais parler aussi, si on veut aller un peu plus loin, de Palantir. Palantir, cette entreprise qui appartient à un grand milliardaire américain, qui nous expliquait dans un manifeste qu'il y a des cultures régressives, inférieures, et des cultures supérieures, qu'en fait les services publics, les hôpitaux, les enseignants, ce n'est pas si important. Il faut surtout lui donner tout notre fric.

Et qu'est-ce qu'on fait? Les armées européennes, l'OTAN, Europol font des contrats avec ces entreprises-là. Comment est-ce que vous voulez être un minimum crédibles dans la lutte pour la sécurité digitale, numérique, si vous avez ce genre d'acteurs sur votre territoire? Juste parce que ce sont des Américains, ce sont des Israéliens, du coup, on ne trouve pas ça grave. Il n'y a aucune crédibilité là-dedans, Madame la Commissaire.

paragraphs.text: Vážená pani predsedajúca, kolegovia. Čína vyprodukuje každý rok okolo päť miliónov inžinierov techniky. Európska únia len okolo 600 tisíc. Kým oni tam vyvíjajú AI smartfóny a humanoidných robotov, tak v Európe pretláčate na univerzitách genderové štúdie a náš priemysel bohužiaľ likvidujete nezmyselným Green dealom. A teraz nás tu chcú európski byrokrati poučovať o kybernetickej bezpečnosti. Prepáčte, ale veď tú vašu aplikáciu, slávnu európsku aplikáciu na overovanie veku na sociálnych sieťach, hackli za dve minúty.

A ja si nechcem ani predstaviť, aké katastrofálne následky by malo napríklad hacknutie tej digitálnej peňaženky s digitálnymi eurami, ktoré sa snažíte ľuďom natlačiť. Ľudia by za sekundu mohli prísť o všetky peniaze, o všetky úspory a, bohužiaľ, vy by ste neboli tomu schopní zabrániť. Pretože vidíme, že Európu vediete dole cestou. Európa technologicky začína zaostávať za Čínou, za Spojenými štátmi americkými a toto je dôsledok vašej politiky. A my to chceme zmeniť a investovať do IT, do európskych firiem, aby sa naštartovali a začali byť konečne konkurencieschopné svetu.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the debate over EU access to advanced AI is part of a deeper problem: our systemic dependence on non-EU hardware and software. There is clearly a lot of product hype in AI right now, but one thing should be clear to us: European tech sovereignty cannot only be a long-term aspiration – it needs clear action now.

Sovereignty does not mean isolation. We must engage with like-minded international partners to make a genuine global consensus on advanced AI. We clearly need an alliance of values to start with, yet we cannot lead globally if we bring nothing to the table. Building our own capabilities is a matter of survival and resilience, as well as security and competitiveness.

This House has high expectations on the tech sovereignty package coming later this month, as well as the public procurement initiative coming in July. It must deliver at least three concrete actions: first, new procurement rules that prioritise European sovereign tech solutions; second, easing smartly our regulatory burden for scaling critical technologies; third, a focus on concrete actions, on harmonisation of our single market and, of course, on our capital markets union.

Let's stop reacting in panic and only acting when a crisis hits us, and focus on concrete actions – spelling out the fact that we need to put our European companies first, and make sure that we only do business with US tech companies based on reciprocity, not on dangerous dependencies.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, qualche settimana fa il gruppo Femwar02 ha paralizzato l'Università La Sapienza di Roma: 400 server bloccati, centinaia di migliaia di studenti senza servizi, dati personali sul dark web.

Nel 2024 il gruppo russo Black Basta aveva pubblicato i referti medici di milioni di italiani nel sistema Synlab. E non è un problema solo per l'Italia: questi attacchi non sono scenari futuribili, sono il presente in tutta Europa e stanno per diventare sempre più pericolosi.

Ad aprile, infatti, Anthropic ha annunciato Mythos, un modello AI in grado di trovare autonomamente migliaia di vulnerabilità critiche in ogni sistema informatico, così pericoloso da non poterlo mettere sul mercato. L'azienda francese Mistral sostiene di avere capacità oggi equivalenti.

Per questo serve dotare subito l'AI Office europeo di più risorse, di più personale tecnico qualificato e di un mandato politico più forte per affrontare subito le nostre vulnerabilità. Non c'è più tempo da perdere.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, affirmer que celui qui domine l’intelligence artificielle sera demain le maître du monde, c’est s’avancer un peu trop vite. En revanche, il est certain que celui qui ne maîtrise pas l’intelligence artificielle sera dominé par ceux qui en maîtriseront toute la chaîne et qui nous inonderont de leurs services. Le débat du jour est placé sous le signe d’une forme de panique liée aux failles que le modèle Mythos d'Anthropic, entre autres, pourrait révéler dans nos propres systèmes.

Il y a pourtant dans l’actualité une source encore plus grande d’inquiétude quant à l’avenir de l’intelligence artificielle en Europe. Nous découvrons que le nucléaire ainsi que l’hydroélectricité pourraient être exclus du label de durabilité concernant le déploiement de centres de données dans le cadre du règlement européen sur le développement du cloud et de l’IA; seules les énergies dites renouvelables seraient retenues. C'est une définition très idéologique et partisane de la durabilité, puisque l’électricité d’origine nucléaire a, on le sait, un impact carbone extrêmement faible.

Pour répondre aux besoins de développement de l’IA en Europe, nous devons fabriquer 400 gigawatts supplémentaires d’électricité. Il faut produire massivement. Le nucléaire est un formidable atout pour générer du surplus d’électricité que nous pourrons consacrer au déploiement de centres de données et à l’IA. À ce titre, nous nous réjouissons d’observer le retour en grâce du nucléaire à travers le continent, comme en Italie et en Belgique récemment, où des relances vont avoir lieu.

La Commission européenne doit reculer, s’avouer vaincue dans sa lutte historique contre le nucléaire. Ses réflexes idéologiques font le bonheur des groupes américains qui savent que les quelques années qui sont devant nous seront décisives et qu’il n’y aura plus de possibilité de rattraper le retard accumulé. Si l’Europe veut faire partie du club des puissances dotées en matière de maîtrise de l’IA, il est temps de cesser cette guérilla permanente qui est faite au nucléaire.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Pani Komisarz! Unia Europejska popełniła wiele błędów, wprowadzając zbyt wiele regulacji, które sparaliżowały gospodarkę i przemysł europejski. I dzisiaj jesteśmy świadkami tego, że jesteśmy coraz mniej konkurencyjni. Niemniej jednak trzeba wyciągać wnioski z tego, co się wydarzyło i nie można w tej chwili doprowadzić do takiej sytuacji, że w tym wyścigu do rozwoju sztucznej inteligencji Unia Europejska jest outsiderem.

W związku z tym powinniśmy przede wszystkim doprowadzić do takiej sytuacji, że rzeczywiście jesteśmy konkurencyjni, mamy pomysł na to, w jaki sposób ten sektor rozwijać tutaj, u nas, w Europie. Ale z drugiej strony to jest oczywiście ogromne zagrożenie. Jesteśmy świadkami praktycznie codziennie cyberataków i w związku z tym konieczne jest wprowadzenie takich zasad i takich regulacji, które ochronią obywateli europejskich i gospodarkę europejską przed tym zagrożeniem. Niemniej jednak jeszcze pamiętajmy o jednej kwestii, że granica pomiędzy wolnością słowa a pomiędzy doprowadzeniem do tego, że ta regulacja sparaliżuje wszystkich, jest bardzo cienka.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister, Commissioner, first, we are urgently debating cybersecurity and preparedness in the EU today, because we became suddenly aware that several new AI systems are especially good at detecting and exploiting system vulnerabilities like they were superhackers on steroids.

But the real threat is – and has been for some time – less sophisticated and far more dangerous. The threat is not that AI now has superhacking capabilities; the real danger is the automation of cyberattacks on an unprecedented scale. By exploiting basic vulnerabilities and scaling them through automation, malicious actors – be they criminal or state actors – can now attack our infrastructure 24/7 at virtually zero cost. It is a cheap, automated assembly line of disruption.

And, dear colleagues, we know that our usual regulations, bureaucratic checklists will not defend us from this automatic cyber warfare. We need to have our own automated collective defence, and here's how to do it: first, we must enforce real time cross-border threat-sharing across the Union, and then we must adequately fund ENISA to be an AI-driven, continuously vulnerability-patching institution. In other words, we must fight automated scaled attacks with automated resistance in real time. And we need this tomorrow.

But perhaps, most importantly, we must be able to be the adults in the room and state clearly that those who treat AI development as an arms race are foolish, dangerous and may lead to drastic consequences for humanity. The only sensible thing to do, as in the previous dangerous arms race, is to agree internationally on how to oversee the development of AI.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, both the Commission and the Council are missing the point. And the point is: a new arms race has begun – not with tanks, not with missiles, with algorithms.

If real, Mythos is an algorithm of mass destruction, and it is unfolding now. The line between civilian innovation and instrument of war is disappearing before our eyes. The same AI system that helps you to have algorithms to book your travels in the morning can attack hospitals, power grids and military systems in the evening.

EU must initiate a global AI governance regime to address the topic. Let's be frank: in cybersecurity, defence alone is not enough. Deterrence matters. The capability to strike back matters. The capability to make adversaries fear consequences matters.

Frankly, the fact that you, Madam Vice-President, are not the Commissioner for defence and that the Commissioner for defence is not you is one of the greatest tragedies of our institutions, because Europe still thinks in silos while the threats against us are converging.

We need a European Defence Union also for digital, a strategic command centre for Europe, also for digital, a European Security Council ready to act. We need European AI defence troops and a European AI defence shield – built in Europe, powered by European technologies like Mistral, controlled by democracies. Because a continent that cannot defend itself and its borders – its digital borders – will not control its fate. The time to act is now.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, «o hard power deste século será construído em software.» A frase é do manifesto da Palantir, empresa criada pela CIA em 2003 que se registou na Comissão Europeia como de literacia em inteligência artificial e que tanto guia bombardeamentos no Irão, como serve para a polícia alemã rastrear pessoas.

No mês passado, duas Big Techs dos Estados Unidos lançaram sistemas sofisticados de inteligência artificial que provaram ser capazes de detetar e atacar pontos de vulnerabilidade sem qualquer intervenção humana. A cibersegurança de sistemas de hospitais, redes elétricas e outras infraestruturas está em risco.

Empresas por toda a Europa usam o argumento da IA para despedir trabalhadores, ainda que muitas vezes depois voltem a contratá-los, mas mais precários e por menos salário. Está, aliás, por provar que a IA tenha gerado ganhos de produtividade na economia. Até ver, é uma gigantesca bolha financeira e, sim, guerra.

Este não é, portanto, o momento de desregular ou de simplificar, como lhe chama a Comissão. Precisamos, sim, de modelos éticos e desenvolvidos na Europa, de entidades de investigação e desenvolvimento a participar na construção de ferramentas tão centrais no mundo de hoje. Precisamos de reguladores eficazes com mais meios para inspecionar e licenciar.

No momento em que se fala de maior recurso à IA na área da saúde, com estes sistemas será possível utilizar os dados para treinar sistemas médicos e reconstruí-los. Estamos a falar de dados genéticos ou clínicos altamente sensíveis e privados dos cidadãos.
Senhora Comissária, a escolha é urgente: segurança, liberdade, democracia.

paragraphs.text: Elnök Asszony! A kibertérben Európa sebezhető, mert fejlesztés helyett szabályoz. Saját kibervédelmi iparra van szükség, chipgyártással, felhővel és mesterséges intelligenciával. Amíg kritikus adatainkat amerikai felhőszolgáltatók tárolják, amíg a túlszabályozás okozta megfelelési költségeket a kkv-szektor nem tudja megfizetni, amíg a big tech a törvények fölött áll, és nem elszámoltatható, Európa törpe marad és kiszolgáltatott. Szoros együttműködés kell a tagállamok között, de birodalmi felügyelet nélkül. A kibervédelem nemzetbiztonsági kérdés, amely tagállami hatáskör. A Bizottság túlterjeszkedése megengedhetetlen.

Ráadásul a Bizottság kibervédelemre hivatkozva ideológiai hadviselést folytat a véleménynyilvánítás szabadsága ellen. Függetlennek hazudott tényellenőrök hálózatát finanszírozza, de hogyan lenne bárki független a finanszírozójától? A fősodortól eltérő, hazafias, globalizációkritikus, családbarát, életvédő, konzervatív véleményeket az ellenőrök gyakran dezinformációnak vagy szélsőséges tartalomnak minősítik, így csökken az elérhetőségük a digitális térben. Ez politikai befolyásolás, a demokrácia meghekkelése. Ahelyett, hogy a kibervédelmet politikai fegyverként használnák és virtuális cordon sanitaire-eket állítanának fel, fókuszáljanak inkább a saját digitális infrastruktúránk megteremtésére, különben a versenyképességnek végképp befellegzett.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Künstliche Intelligenz hat viele Potenziale, vor allem das Potenzial, uns zu verdummen: Die Algorithmen von Tech-Milliardären steuern zunehmend unser Denken, unser Fühlen und auch die Politik; sie machen Kinder zu digitalen Zombies.

In den USA droht die Blase bei künstlicher Intelligenz zu platzen, weil angesichts hoher Energiepreise Kapazität für Betrieb und Kühlung der Computerfarmen fehlt. Eine große Gefahr von KI sind automatisierte Waffensysteme. Die europäische Hochrüstung macht uns dabei übrigens nicht unabhängiger von den USA. Das Oberkommando der NATO-Streitkräfte in Europa hat gerade KI von Palantir eingekauft – ein US-Konzern, der offen sagt, dass er eine Diktatur von US-Milliardären errichten will. Übrigens auch unter Beifall der rechten Seite des Hauses, denen hier die nationale Souveränität völlig egal ist.
Die kritische KI-Infrastruktur und Cyberabwehr gehören in öffentliche Hand; US-Konzerne wie Palantir gehören ausgesperrt! Sonst werden wir in einer Tech-Apokalypse aufwachen.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, a inteligência artificial está a transformar profundamente a forma como vivemos, trabalhamos e comunicamos, mas está também a alterar o panorama das ameaças à segurança da União Europeia.

Hoje, os riscos já não se limitam aos ciberataques tradicionais. Sistemas de IA podem ser utilizados para automatizar ataques em larga escala, manipular informação, criar deepfakes altamente credíveis e explorar vulnerabilidades críticas com uma rapidez sem precedentes.

Perante esta realidade, a Europa não pode ser ingénua. A cibersegurança passou a ser uma questão de soberania. Mas a resposta não deve ser o medo da inovação — há que fomentar a capacidade de construir uma inovação segura, responsável e assente nos nossos valores democráticos. É precisamente isso que a União Europeia procura fazer através do Regulamento da Inteligência Artificial, do Regulamento da Ciber-Resiliência e da Convenção sobre a Inteligência Artificial.

Precisamos agora de ir mais longe e investir em capacidades europeias de ciberdefesa, reforçar a cooperação entre Estados-Membros e garantir que a Europa não fique dependente de potências externas em tecnologias críticas. E precisamos também de olhar para o impacto humano destas ameaças, sobretudo junto dos mais jovens, cada vez mais expostos à manipulação algorítmica, à fraude digital e à exploração online.

A inteligência artificial será, inevitavelmente, parte do futuro da segurança europeia. A questão é se queremos reagir aos riscos ou preparar a Europa para liderar esta transformação com responsabilidade, inovação e confiança. Está aqui a chave do futuro.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria Virkkunen, cuando este Parlamento aprobó el Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial e incluso cuando aprobó el ómnibus para simplificarlo, hemos sido conscientes de que estamos ante una revolución tecnológica imparable y vertiginosa que nos abisma ahora a la llamada «inteligencia artificial de frontera»: Mythos, Anthropic, OpenAI...

El principio de precaución que practican las instituciones y el Parlamento Europeo no puede conducirnos al miedo, pero la colaboración con esas nuevas empresas de vanguardia tampoco puede llevarnos a acentuar la dependencia. Por el contrario, afirmar nuestra soberanía estratégica significa reafirmar también nuestros valores: control democrático institucional, transparencia, respeto de los derechos fundamentales... es decir: supervisión humana, en definitiva.

Se trata de encontrar un equilibrio que sea coherente con los principios que inspiraron la legislación europea de inteligencia artificial y, al mismo tiempo, acentuar la preparación de la Unión Europea para defenderse también ante la propensión al armamento y a la guerra, así como ante la capacidad de la inteligencia artificial de explotar las vulnerabilidades de las sociedades abiertas.

Se trata de encontrar un equilibrio que sea coherente con los principios que inspiraron la legislación europea de inteligencia artificial y, al mismo tiempo, acentuar la preparación de la Unión Europea para defenderse también ante la propensión al armamento y a la guerra, así como ante la capacidad de la inteligencia artificial de explotar las vulnerabilidades de las sociedades abiertas.

paragraphs.text: Elnök Asszony! Az Európai Unió a digitális gyarmatosítás útján halad, de nem mi gyarmatosítunk másokat, hanem mások gyarmatosítanak minket, és ennek komoly gazdasági és biztonsági oldala is van. Az Európai Unió nagyon büszke arra, hogy a világ első mesterségesintelligencia-szabályozását alkotta meg. Ezzel szemben digitális téren nem Európa az első innovációban, kódolásban és minden releváns technikai feltétel megteremtésében sem. A világ legnagyobb techcégei között alig van európai, a digitális innováció így nem Európából jön. Legjobb esetben is utólag másoljuk azokat a szolgáltatásokat, amelyekre nekünk is szükségünk van, de még azok sem európai hardveren futnak.

Évtizedek óta lemaradásban vagyunk, és ez egyre inkább látszik az adatközpontokon és a mesterségesintelligencia-modelleken is. Ezek pedig tovább csökkentik digitális szuverenitásunkat. Az idő szűke miatt csak egy példát említenék. Európában 3400 adatközpont van, az Egyesült Államokban 5400. Az adatközpontok pedig zabálják az energiát. Az Európai Unió villamoshálózat-korlátai miatt 7-től 10 évet kell várni arra, hogy egy új adatközpontot rákapcsoljanak a villamosenergia hálózatra. A villamosenergia-hálózat mellett akadály maga a villamosenergia ára is. Amerikában fele annyiba kerül, mint Európában, Kínában még olcsóbb. Az elhibázott, ideológiai alapú energiapolitika újabb és újabb korlátokat okoz, és károkat okoz az európaiaknak. Megélhetés, versenyképesség és egyre inkább a kiberbiztonság terén is, olcsó energia nélkül Európa egyre jobban le fog maradni.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, il tema della prontezza, della preparazione alle crisi tocca certamente il tema della sicurezza nel più ampio spettro, c'è quello della difesa, c'è quello dell'economia, c'è quello della sicurezza personale.
E oggi è tutto sicurezza cibernetica. Di fronte a questo contesto, sempre più complesso e di natura ibrida, è importante lavorare su quale capacità l'Europa deve darsi.

È di questi giorni il dato per cui gli Stati Uniti stanno aumentando – raddoppiando – la propria capacità produttiva grazie all'intelligenza artificiale. E qui, oggi, noi ci troviamo ancora una volta a dire il vuoto che passa tra la capacità dell'Europa e quella del resto del mondo.

Io voglio sottolineare un aspetto significativo, quello dell'indipendenza, della capacità di gestire dati, di controllare il sistema della sicurezza dal punto di vista cibernetico: l'Europa è troppo dipendente, soprattutto dalla Cina.
In quest'Aula ho sentito, ridondante, l'accusa verso Israele. Nessuno si interroga su quanto la Cina, oggi, ci stia controllando e questo sembra preoccupare solo noi.

paragraphs.text: Fru Formand, kommissær, minister! Det er jo ikke nogen nyhed, at Europa længe har befundet sig i en hybridkrig. Det nye er til gengæld, at AI er blevet krigens helt afgørende våben. Hver eneste dag forsøger autoritære regimer at undergrave vores demokratier gennem cyberangreb, desinformation og angreb på kritisk infrastruktur. Hvad der før tog en flok talentfulde hackere en måned, tager nu kun ganske få minutter. Så vi er nødt til at gøre noget, og vi er nødt til at gøre det hurtigt.

Europa, kommissær, er fortsat for uforberedt. Vi skal styrke vores fælles cyberforsvar markant. Vi skal selvfølgelig styrke ENISA, vores agentur, men vi skal også have et fælles cyberforsvar. Vi har kort sagt brug for en egentlig cyberbrigade, en europæisk brigade, der kan gøre noget ved det her med det samme i realtid. En kampklar enhed af specialister, der kan hjælpe medlemslandene med at opdage, afværge og reagere på hybride trusler med det samme. For hvis autoritære stater samarbejder på tværs af grænser, så skal vi selvfølgelig også gøre det, og vi skal gøre det nu. Og frem for alt: Vi skal indse, at hvis vi skal bekæmpe den her AI-trussel og bruge AI offensivt, så er vi nødt til at gøre det sammen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, if it is true what Anthropic claims – Mythos being able to detect all cyber security vulnerabilities – then it could pose a major risk if this AI system falls into the wrong hands. Even if half is true, it opens the door to major cyberattacks at scale. Think of banks being hacked, our transport systems being disrupted, and hospitals blacking out. And if we understand the experts correctly, Mythos is just the first model, but many will follow soon.

With a US Government that does not believe in regulating AI, we are apparently in the hands of Anthropic to decide whether they think the EU is a trustworthy partner, like Google. Anthropic only putting red lines for their systems being used against American citizens doesn't give me much hope. And to be honest, just saying that we have the right systems in place also doesn't. Systems are only useful and only work if you use them, act swiftly and with urgency.

So, Commission, maybe the urgency you feel to deregulate and postpone tech rules you could also channel towards the safety of our citizens and businesses, and also towards supporting the development of European AI, with cybersecurity capabilities that is created in line with democratic values. If we don't want our reliance on our cybersecurity in foreign hands and to be turned against us, we need to take bold decisions – there steering the type of innovation we want in Europe – and make sure the money we are investing in European AI goes to benefit all Europeans and not another AI puppy video generator.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, des hôpitaux paralysés par une cyberattaque, des opérations chirurgicales annulées, des soignants privés d'ordinateurs, de téléphones, de dossiers médicaux. Ce n'est pas de la science-fiction. Cela arrive déjà, comme à Besançon, à Anvers ou à Paris ces derniers mois.

Avec les capacités offensives des nouveaux modèles d'intelligence artificielle, comme Claude Mythos ou GPT 5.5, cela peut devenir demain notre quotidien et notre législation actuelle ne suffira pas. D'ici un an, ce sont des dizaines de modèles open source qui rendront accessibles ces capacités partout, à bas coûts, sans aucun garde-fou. Du pain béni pour les pirates et pour les ingérences étrangères.

Mais l'IA, elle peut aussi servir à nous défendre en détectant les failles avant même que les hackers frappent. À condition que cette IA soit au service de notre souveraineté. Car des questions fondamentales se posent. Doit-on confier les données de nos armées et de nos systèmes les plus sensibles à des entreprises américaines soumises au bon vouloir de Donald Trump? Souhaitons-nous remplacer une vulnérabilité par une vassalité?

Je crois que nous devons au contraire nous appuyer sur nos entreprises, comme Mistral par exemple, qui développe actuellement les solutions pour une cyberdéfense souveraine. Nous avons les moyens de les financer grâce à nos marchés publics, par exemple. Mais n'attendons plus, car demain il sera trop tard.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, on a piraté votre vie. Regardez ce que nous, Européens, avons subi en à peine six mois. En France, le fisc s’est fait pirater vos déclarations d’impôts. L’URSSAF aussi, avec les adresses, les noms de vos enfants et de leur nourrice. Le ministère de l’intérieur aussi, avec le fichier des antécédents judiciaires de 16 millions de Français. Un adolescent de 15 ans a piraté l’État et offert 11 millions de cartes d’identité, de passeports et de permis de conduire à la criminalité.

Et ici même, dans cette enceinte du Parlement européen qui prétend tout réglementer pour notre bien, les contrats de mariage, les fiches de paie et les données médicales des collaborateurs sont désormais en vente libre sur Internet. Le comble, c’est qu’il y a quelques semaines, Ursula von der Leyen présentait fièrement l’application européenne de vérification d’âge sur les réseaux sociaux; 24 heures plus tard, un simple consultant la faisait tomber. Le résultat est tragique: usurpation d’identité, comptes vidés, cambriolages. La France est devenue championne du monde d’un nouveau crime: l’enlèvement pour crypto-monnaie.

Vos parents peuvent se faire séquestrer parce que vous possédez du bitcoin. Pourquoi? Parce que l’État vous a imposé de tout lui déclarer, vos noms et vos patrimoines, et il a laissé fuiter ces données. En France, c’est l’État qui donne l’adresse des victimes à leurs bourreaux. Pendant ce temps, ici, vous continuez d’exiger toujours plus de déclarations, toujours plus de contrôles.

Mes chers collègues, la surréglementation numérique n’a pas seulement échoué à nous protéger, elle a chassé nos innovateurs, asphyxié nos entrepreneurs et nourri un mirage de sécurité qui nous a tous mis en danger. Aujourd’hui, l’Europe doit choisir: le contrôle ou la liberté. Nous choisissons la liberté.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Guten Tag. Dass die Überwachungsbefürworter, die meist auch Regel-unnötig-Finder sind, sich nun für Cybersicherheit der EU angesichts fortschreitender KI-Systeme, so der Tagesordnungspunkt, begeistern, ist rührend und passiert in dem Moment, da die US-Firma Anthropic mit ihrer neuen Software in Sekundenschnelle Software-Sicherheitslücken aufdecken können soll – in jeder Software, auch in europäischer.

Weshalb ich Sie heute aber nicht im Kreise der Sicherheitsbefürworter begrüßen darf, liegt an der Tatsache, dass es Ihnen nicht um die Cybersicherheit der Bürger geht. Gewollte backdoors in Software sind für Sie kein Problem, wenn Polizei und Geheimdienste sie nutzen, um Bürgerinnen auszuspionieren. Sicherheitslücken heißen ja Sicherheitslücken, weil Sicherheitsbehörden da zur Sicherheit reinlücken – Spaß. Hintertüren, die nur die Guten (räuspert sich) nutzen können, sind eine Illusion. Also, Tür zu, alle glücklich – naja fast.

paragraphs.text: Nett, dass Sie mir eine eigenständige Persönlichkeit zubilligen, dass ich nicht der Fuß von Herrn Sonneborn bin, danke dafür.

Wir können einiges tun, um die Sicherheit der Menschen zu gewährleisten. Zum Beispiel könnten wir europäische Software fördern, was wir so nicht tun. Wir könnten peer-to-peer chats ermöglichen, was wir so nicht tun. Wir könnten absolute Verschlüsselung gewährleisten, was wir nicht tun wollen, weil, wie ich sagte, Sicherheitslücken, die jetzt so furchtbar in Krankenhäusern – und was noch genannt wurde – entstehen können, um Amerikanern die Spionage zu gewährleisten – fordern wir ja gerade, für zum Beispiel Chatkontrolle, zum zehnten Mal.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Madam Commissioner, I think everyone agrees here that AI's transformation and disruption potential is absolutely total. It is changing the way we wage war, and it will be decisive on how we actually live in peace in the coming, let's say, 50 years.

The Commission, therefore, has this generational task to lay the foundations of what is our European life, but in this digital world on steroids that we're all confronted with. It has to safeguard our democracies and our economies to protect against the destructive forces and to harness the potential which also all of us can recognise.

But Europe's voice is crucial, between the godlike AI from the US and the Chinese totalitarian alternatives that we will be confronted with. The question is not whether we do something, it's whether we are ready to provide an alternative that is actually being able to be that alternative. This means scaling, building and buying European. It's very clear.

It also means thinking about the data we need to train our models. We are mass exporting our data to the US, and very soon also – and many of the younger people in Europe with their Temu apps – they're doing that to China.

So if the Commission is still looking for new own resources, maybe an export tariff on our data is a good alternative to make the others pay for something that they really need, because I'm convinced that our data is the most valuable asset we have in Europe. It represents the value of our economy and of our values itself. It is something we need to monetise, if you want to say it in a very Gen Z way.

It also means thinking about the data we need to train our models. We are mass exporting our data to the US, and very soon also – and many of the younger people in Europe with their Temu apps – they're doing that to China.

So if the Commission is still looking for new own resources, maybe an export tariff on our data is a good alternative to make the others pay for something that they really need, because I'm convinced that our data is the most valuable asset we have in Europe. It represents the value of our economy and of our values itself. It is something we need to monetise, if you want to say it in a very Gen Z way.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Commissioner, I think it's not exaggeration to say that we are living historical times. AI is affecting our societies in so many ways, including the nature of cyber warfare. Attacks are becoming faster, more autonomous, more precise and harder to detect. But our infrastructure, our network, our weapon systems are vulnerable. This is not science fiction; this is reality we're living in. Russia, China, Iran, North Korea are using our weaknesses daily and attacking us and harming us, so Europe needs to step up, including in this House.

So, dear colleagues, I have a suggestion. I believe that it is time that we establish a permanent committee on AI dedicated to monitoring developments, assessing risks, strengthening our preparedness and ensuring Europe can act strategically instead of reactively. Many countries around the world have already done that and I think it's time we do so also.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Vice-présidente, Madame la Ministre, vous venez dénoncer les risques de Mythos d'Anthropic et de ChatGPT 5 d'OpenAI, deux entreprises américaines. Oui, dès son lancement en avril 2026, Mythos a montré sa puissance. Oui, certains ont même craint qu'il échappe au contrôle de ses créateurs. Mais ce modèle n'est pas accessible au public, je dirais, un peu comme les SMS d'Ursula avec Pfizer. Le premier est caché pour protéger les citoyens, les seconds l'ont été pour protéger Bruxelles des citoyens.

Alors plutôt que de commenter les avancées américaines ou chinoises, il faudrait, enfin, investir massivement dans l'intelligence artificielle ici en Europe. Arthur Mensch, le fondateur de Mistral, expliquait la semaine dernière à l'Assemblée nationale vouloir investir 1 milliard d'euros en recherche et développement. En novembre 2025, OpenAI avait déjà dépassé les 14 milliards de dollars d'investissements. Le vrai danger, ce ne sont pas seulement ces modèles; le vrai danger, c'est la dépendance que Bruxelles organise. C'est la dépendance effectivement que Bruxelles organise, mais je ne parle même plus de la surréglementation qui domine toujours, malgré des discours officiels sur la simplification. La bureaucratie tient bon.

Et je terminerai sur cet exemple que vous connaissez très bien, mesdames, qui serait comique si ce n'était pas si tragique. J'étais rapporteure pour les Patriotes sur l'omnibus «AI». Pendant six heures, nous avons débattu pour savoir ce qu'était un «nudificateur» et à partir de quel pourcentage de fesses une image devenait illégale. Certains se sont même demandé si un tee-shirt mouillé pouvait devenir un «nudificateur». En fait, l'Europe n'aura pas la révolution de l'intelligence artificielle. Elle l'évite sciemment, elle regarde ailleurs.
Et pour réaliser la force de la Chine et des États-Unis, il suffit de regarder le nombre de brevets déposés en 2024.
(L'oratrice montre un graphique)

La Chine en a déposé près de 50 %, les États-Unis, 16 %, et l'Europe, 5,4 %. Alors, si on n'est pas à table, c'est qu'on est au menu. Je terminerai par cette phrase, même si je ne la partage pas aux États-Unis, mais je la partage ici, c'est: Make Europe great again.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, la inteligencia artificial avanza hoy a velocidad de misil y, mientras, en Europa seguimos regulando a velocidad de máquina de escribir.

Ese es el problema, porque mientras los ciberataques se automatizan, aprenden y evolucionan en segundos, nuestras empresas siguen perdiendo tiempo, recursos y competitividad navegando entre burocracia. Y precisamente ahí está uno de los grandes riesgos que afrontamos en el Reglamento sobre la Ciberseguridad, porque la ciberseguridad real no se mide por el número de formularios rellenados ni por la cantidad de obligaciones administrativas que imponemos, se mide por algo muchísimo más simple: la capacidad real para defender sistemas críticos, infraestructuras, empresas y ciudadanos. Y eso requiere talento, requiere tecnología, inversión, capacidad industrial y capacidad operativa real, no más complejidad regulatoria. Porque si Europa obliga a sus empresas a gastar más energía en cumplir burocracia que en proteger sus sistemas, estaremos debilitando nuestra propia soberanía tecnológica.

Necesitamos un enfoque basado en riesgo real, basado en proporcionalidad y evidencia técnica, un marco que proteja nuestra seguridad digital sin destruir innovación, competitividad ni inversión. Porque la revolución de la inteligencia artificial ya no es el futuro, está ocurriendo ahora, en este momento. Y Europa tiene que decidir si quiere liderar esa transformación o limitarse a regular como otros lideran el mundo.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, Minister, artificial intelligence is no longer a distant possibility. It is already reshaping our economies, our democracies and our security, and powerful systems like Anthropic's Mythos or OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber demonstrate both the extraordinary promise and the serious risks of frontier AI.

This is urgent, dear colleagues. We have to equip ENISA with the tools necessary, and this is where we really need a dedicated AI cybersecurity strategy to counter those threats that are really threatening all aspects of our lives.

AI models capable of advanced cyber operations should undergo mandatory safety testing, but before development, companies developing frontier AI must prove that their systems are secure, transparent and resistant to misuse. Certification schemes are necessary here.
Second, the EU should establish strict safeguards for high-risk AI. Models with offensive cyber capabilities must not be freely accessible without oversight.

And last but not least, Europe must invest in its own AI ecosystem. If we really entirely depend on foreign technology giants, we are risking losing our economic competitiveness and digital sovereignty.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Wen hat Anthropic über die potenziellen Gefahren von Mythos eigentlich informiert? Die US-Regierung, über 50 US-amerikanische Unternehmen und am 7. April dann endlich die Welt mit einer öffentlichen Ankündigung. Aber von der potenziellen Bedrohung durch Mythos sind nicht nur amerikanische Unternehmen und Bürgerinnen und Bürger betroffen, sondern auch wir in Europa. Aber die Europäische Union? Fehlanzeige! Sie hat bis heute keinen Zugang zu dem Modell, um zu prüfen, wie gefährlich es tatsächlich ist und zu sehen, wie sie europäische Bürgerinnen und Bürger schützen kann.

Und das zeigt zwei Dinge. Erstens, wie fatal es war, die Anwendung der KI-Verordnung weiter durch den Omnibus hinauszuzögern. Wer glaubt, dass diese Unternehmen uns in Europa ernst nehmen, wenn wir ihren Deregulierungsfantasien nachgeben, der wird gerade eines Besseren belehrt. Und zweitens: Wir brauchen dringend starke Cybersicherheitskapazitäten in Europa. Technologische Souveränität ist dringender denn je. Lassen Sie uns endlich daran arbeiten und dafür die nötigen Maßnahmen und das nötige Kapital bereitstellen, wie es viele Kolleginnen und Kollegen hier gefordert haben. Bald kommt das Sicherheitspaket, dann können wir das umsetzen.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση βρίσκεται μπροστά σε μια εποχή κυβερνοαπειλών. Σήμερα, συστήματα τεχνητής νοημοσύνης μπορούν σε ελάχιστο χρόνο να εντοπίζουν και να εκμεταλλεύονται κενά λογισμικών σε πρωτοφανή κλίμακα. Όμως, η Ευρώπη δεν είναι επαρκώς προετοιμασμένη για να αντιμετωπίσει αυτή τη νέα πραγματικότητα. Δημόσιες υπηρεσίες, κρίσιμες υποδομές, πολίτες αλλά και οι δημοκρατικοί θεσμοί απειλούνται. Η ευρωπαϊκή κυβερνοασφάλεια εξακολουθεί να εξαρτάται από τεχνολογίες και εταιρείες τρίτων χωρών, γεγονός που περιορίζει τον ευρωπαϊκό έλεγχο και τη στρατηγική αυτονομία.

Γι αυτό, απαιτείται άμεσα ενιαία ευρωπαϊκή στρατηγική που θα διασφαλίζει την ευρωπαϊκή ψηφιακή κυριαρχία και την έγκαιρη πρόσβαση σε κρίσιμα συστήματα τεχνητής νοημοσύνης, ώστε να αξιολογεί τους κινδύνους και να σχεδιάζει αποτελεσματικά μέτρα για την αντιμετώπισή τους. Είναι άμεση ανάγκη να υιοθετηθούν κατευθυντήριες γραμμές για τη στήριξη του δημόσιου και του ιδιωτικού τομέα για την άμεση αντικατάσταση των παλαιωμένων λογισμικών· να επιταχυνθεί η εφαρμογή της πράξης για την κυβερνοανθεκτικότητα· να καλυφθούν διαπιστωμένα ρυθμιστικά κενά ασφάλειας στο πλαίσιο της αναθεώρησης της πράξης για την κυβερνοασφάλεια· να επανεξεταστεί το ευρωπαϊκό ρυθμιστικό πλαίσιο για συστήματα τεχνητής νοημοσύνης ανοικτού κώδικα με προηγμένες επιθετικές δυνατότητες· να ενισχυθεί ο ΕNISA με περισσότερους πόρους. Η Ευρώπη πρέπει να επενδύσει περισσότερα για να αποκτήσει αυτονομία στην ψηφιακή τεχνολογία, ώστε να έχει τις δικές της δυνατότητες κυβερνοάμυνας.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Moderne KI braucht Forschung auf Spitzenniveau. Wir aber misstrauen der Exzellenz und erklären sozialdemokratisches Mittelmaß zur politischen Tugend.
KI braucht ein starkes Zusammenspiel von Universitäten, Kapital, Start-ups und Großindustrie. Wir aber ersticken Unternehmergeist in Regularien und Berichtspflichten.
KI braucht Spitzenpersonal und attraktive Bedingungen. Wir aber schrecken die besten Köpfe ab und öffnen lieber die Pforten unserer Sozialsysteme.
KI braucht viel und bezahlbare Energie. Wir aber zerstören lustvoll die Grundlage unserer Energiesicherheit und vertreiben die KI über die Stromrechnung.

Technologische Plattformen sind die Grundlage von Souveränität. Wer KI-Resilienz will, muss das Weltsozialamt EU schließen, Energiesouveränität wiederherstellen und das Bürokratiemonster der Kommission dort halten, wo es hingehört: Draußen vor der Tür.

paragraphs.text: Cienītā sēdes vadītāja! Kolēģi! Pajautājot mākslīgā intelekta tērzēšanas robotam par Krievijas agresiju Ukrainā, tā atbildes bieži atkārto Kremļa mantras par nacismu Ukrainā, par slepenajām ASV bioieroču laboratorijām, par Rietumu militārās palīdzības zagšanu.

Saskaņā ar NewsGuard veikto pētījumu, kurā tika pārbaudīti desmit vadošie tērzēšanas roboti, tie sistemātiski atkārto nepatiesības, nepatiesus stāstus par Ukrainu, kuru izcelsme ir meklējama Krievijā.
Tā nav ideoloģiska vai tehniska kļūda – tās ir Krievijas apzinātas manipulācijas ar mākslīgā intelekta modeļiem, tos mērķtiecīgi saindējot ar nepatiesu informāciju.
Šī Kremļa taktika ir neticami rentabla. Informācijas hibrīdkaram pietiek ar vienu miljardu dolāru gadā, kamēr militārais budžets prasa 190 miljardus dolāru.
Krievijas manipulācijas nav tikai kiberdrošības jautājums. Tās apdraud Eiropas demokrātiju, mūsu informācijas telpu un eiropiešu sirdis un prātus.

Lai aizsargātu mūsu iedzīvotājus, informācijas drošība ir jāpadara par pamatprasību. Eiropai ir jāstiprina mākslīgā intelekta apmācības datu pārredzamības standarti un jāatbalsta mākslīgā intelekta izstrādes neatkarīga pārraudzība.

Tā nav ideoloģiska vai tehniska kļūda – tās ir Krievijas apzinātas manipulācijas ar mākslīgā intelekta modeļiem, tos mērķtiecīgi saindējot ar nepatiesu informāciju.

Šī Kremļa taktika ir neticami rentabla. Informācijas hibrīdkaram pietiek ar vienu miljardu dolāru gadā, kamēr militārais budžets prasa 190 miljardus dolāru.

Krievijas manipulācijas nav tikai kiberdrošības jautājums. Tās apdraud Eiropas demokrātiju, mūsu informācijas telpu un eiropiešu sirdis un prātus.

Lai aizsargātu mūsu iedzīvotājus, informācijas drošība ir jāpadara par pamatprasību. Eiropai ir jāstiprina mākslīgā intelekta apmācības datu pārredzamības standarti un jāatbalsta mākslīgā intelekta izstrādes neatkarīga pārraudzība.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, artificial intelligence is transforming our economies, our security environment and our democratic societies in an unprecedented speed. Europe must lead not only in innovation, but also in responsibility and resilience.

The AI Act is an important step because it puts fundamental rights, transparency, human oversight and cybersecurity at the centre of advanced AI systems. But frontier AI systems can become tools for cyberattacks, disinformation and attacks against critical infrastructure. Europe, therefore, needs stronger preparedness, closer coordination between cyber security authorities, industry and researchers, and greater investment in trusted European AI capabilities and digital sovereignty.

We must also strengthen cooperation with like-minded partners to improve cyber resilience and respond to AI-enabled threats. At the same time, the EU should take the lead globally in shaping international rules and principles for trustworthy and secure AI.

And finally, if we are serious about enforcement, the AI office must evolve into a fully fledged European agency with the resources and expertise needed to monitor, assess, support and control the development of advanced AI systems.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, je suis content qu’on ait ce débat parce que, dans mon pays, en France, j’ai l’impression que d’habitude tout le monde s’en fout, alors que c’est un sujet majeur. Madame Keller, ne soyez pas désagréable. Ça va vous changer. Souriez, souriez. Il fait beau aujourd’hui. En plus, les agriculteurs sont devant.

Et donc on va parler d’un sujet intéressant qui concerne près d’un million de personnes sur les deux dernières années, qui ont été victimes finalement du vol de leurs données, des fuites de données sur les réseaux. Et je ne sais pas si vous connaissez breach3d, dans mon pays, en France, c'est l’histoire d’un mineur de 14 ans qui, dès l’âge de 14 ans, aujourd’hui 15 ans, a piraté l’Agence nationale des titres sécurisés, c’est-à-dire l’agence qui fait les permis de conduire, qui fait les passeports, qui fait les cartes d’identité. Et donc il a été interpellé grâce au courage et à l’excellent service de la police judiciaire française. Et aujourd’hui, il a des comptes à rendre à la justice. Donc on voit bien que ce n’était pas un érudit et un spécialiste de l’informatique, mais il a réussi à pirater l’un des premiers sites que les Français utilisent pour faire leurs documents d’identité. Pareil pour la plateforme de formation de la police. Elle a été piratée dans un cadre où les policiers sont des cibles. Ils ont été légitimement inquiets. Donc on voit bien que les sites officiels aujourd’hui ne sont pas ou mal protégés. Et c’est bien qu’on ait un plan qui soit non seulement national, mais européen pour protéger ces données.

Ensuite, pareil, des tireurs sportifs ont vu leur base de données dans laquelle ils sont référencés, volée. Donc il y a eu des vols à domicile de leurs armes à feu, et pareil également pour des usurpations ou des fausses qualités utilisées grâce à la récolte des données, par la falsification et par l’intrusion dans des données informatiques qui touchent de nombreux Françaises et Français, mais aussi au niveau de l’Union européenne. Donc, par exemple, l’authentification multifacteur permettrait de lutter contre ces intrusions informatiques. Et je pense qu’il faut aujourd’hui se doter d’une réelle politique informatique et de sûreté et de sécurité pour pouvoir enfin être à la hauteur du XXIᵉ siècle. Merci pour votre sourire, Madame Keller, ça vous change, vraiment.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, Uniunea Europeană este dependentă de tehnologia online dezvoltată în statele non-UE. Viitorul securității europene nu se mai decide doar la granițe, ci și în centrele de date și în laboratoarele AI.

Dar accesul la tehnologie și finanțare este limitat și inegal distribuit între statele membre. Se resimte deja o Europă cu două viteze în tehnologie și inteligență artificială, iar această fractură va determina o pulverizare în materie de apărare și securitate. Reziliența europeană nu poate fi limitată la câteva state membre, restul fiind blocat ca piață de consum și furnizori de forță de muncă.

România este victimă a unui paradox european: produce și încă mai concentrează inteligență umană orientată spre tehnologie, dar este determinată să o exporte masiv. Suntem foarte buni la a dezvolta tehnologii pentru alții, dar nu suficient de buni pentru a conta ca pol tehnologic. Nu e din cauza dizidenților din cordonul sanitar, ci a liderilor incompetenți și lipsiți de viziune ai Uniunii Europene.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Wir sehen gerade, wie schnell hochleistungsfähige KI Cybersicherheit verändert. Systeme wie Mythos zeigen doch, dass technologischer Fortschritt sich eben nicht wegregulieren lässt. Denn nur weil Europa etwas verbietet, heißt es nicht, dass autoritäre Regime oder feindliche Akteure es nicht trotzdem entwickeln und dann auch gegen uns einsetzen.

Deswegen braucht Europa endlich einen Kurswechsel: weg von angstgetriebener Regulierung, hin zu wertebasierter Regulierung, die Innovation, Investition und technologische Souveränität ermöglicht. Wir dürfen im globalen KI-Wettlauf nicht länger Zuschauer sein, während die USA und China das Spielfeld bestimmen!

Denn Cybersicherheit bedeutet auch Verteidigungsfähigkeit. Unsere kritische Infrastruktur besonders muss mit den besten Technologien geschützt sein. Wir dürfen nicht abhängig sein von autoritären Staaten. Dafür müssen wir endlich die Bremse lösen: weniger Bürokratie, günstigere Energie, digitaler Binnenmarkt, eine Kapitalmarktunion für große Investitionen, für KI und Cybersicherheit. Denn Europa kann hier vorne mitspielen, wenn wir aufhören, Innovation zuerst als Risiko zu begreifen und es endlich als Chance sehen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, so a girl posts a beach photo of herself on Insta, and weeks later she's receiving naked pictures of herself – AI generated. This happened to 20 girls in Spain and it happened to Steffi Mercie in Belgium multiple times. Dear colleagues, it happened to 1 million children in 2025 alone. That is one child in every classroom.

So, across Europe, people are waking up to find their voice and their body weaponised by AI without their consent. Luckily, Europe is finally banning these apps in December. But we had to fight for it because some wanted loopholes. Some thought that the profits of big tech were more important than protecting our children.

That's what terrifies me, because we are about to make the exact same mistake when it comes to our cybersecurity. The advanced AI models that were released in April can discover vulnerabilities that have gone undetected for 15 years. They can enable attacks at a scale that we've never seen. So if the hesitation on banning deepfakes is actually leaving our women and children not protected and exposed, well then the hesitation on cybersecurity leaves everybody exposed.
So, colleagues, let's not make that same mistake again.

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, a chairde, as advanced AI evolves at breakneck speed, Europe faces a defining test: innovation must strengthen our security, not undermine it.
We see the massive benefits of AI every day in Ireland, driving our tech sector and transforming healthcare. But we cannot afford to be blind to the unprecedented cybersecurity risks.
Sophisticated AI is already being weaponized. It accelerates cyberattacks and scams, automates disinformation, and targets critical infrastructure with unimaginable speed.

For Ireland, as a primary digital and data hub for Europe, the stakes could not be higher. A threat to our networks is a threat to the entire European single market. While the EU has led the way with the Artificial Intelligence Act and new cyber regulations, laws alone are not a shield.

We need concrete action. That means deep cross-border intelligence sharing, heavy investment in our cyber defence capabilities and ironclad protection for vital sectors like energy, finance and hospitals.
Artificial intelligence is the single biggest opportunity, but also the single biggest challenge of our lifetimes.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, la verdad es que hablar de la inteligencia artificial hoy se está convirtiendo claramente en la definición de lo que es ya un arma de guerra, y Europa está en guerra, no lo podemos obviar. La verdad es que analizar la última cumbre que ha habido entre los Estados Unidos y China, con el señor Xi Jinping hablando de la trampa de Tucídides, tiene mucho que ver con analizar la realidad mundial y global y con lo poco o nada que pinta en este momento Europa.

No se trata de hablar de modelos, no se trata de hablar de Anthropic —que, por cierto, es una empresa que sobre la base de sus códigos éticos ha sido apartada del sistema de defensa norteamericano—. Se trata fundamentalmente de diseñar un gran modelo de soberanía europea y, desde mi punto de vista, basado en cuatro pilares fundamentales. El primer pilar es el energético; las gigafactorías van a necesitar cantidades ingentes de energía. El segundo es la capacidad de cómputo —sin eso no vamos a llegar a ningún lado—. El tercero es la gestión de datos, y el cuarto, los modelos de los que estamos hablando. Anthropic es un ejemplo, pero podríamos hablar de OpenAI, la realidad norteamericana u occidental... ¿Dónde están los modelos chinos que también tenemos que controlar y supervisar?

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, paní komisařko, dnes diskutujeme o kybernetické bezpečnosti v době pokročilé umělé inteligence. A je to samozřejmě správně, že tuto debatu vedeme. Protože umělá inteligence už dnes není jen ekonomický nástroj, ale je to nástroj geopolitiky, obrany i hybridních hrozeb.

Ale řekněme si jednu nepříjemnou pravdu. Evropská unie je v této oblasti často pozadu. Když zavádíme nové systémy, trvá to roky. Když přijde nová hrozba, odpovídáme strategií, akčním plánem nebo vytvářením další pracovní skupiny. Jenže protivníci Evropy nečekají na implementační lhůty. Kybernetické útoky s použitím umělé inteligence se vyvíjí v řádu týdnů, nikoliv legislativních období. A právě zde si musíme vzít několik ponaučení.

Za prvé, centralizace sama o sobě bezpečnost nezaručí. Členské státy často reagují rychleji než Brusel, protože mají vlastní zkušenosti a mají vlastní kapacity a znají lépe své hrozby. Musíme jim dát větší pravomoci a flexibilitu a neřídit všechno z jednoho centra.

Za druhé, nestačí regulovat. Evropa vytváří pravidla, ale nástroje na jejich implementaci často chybí. Potřebujeme nejdříve navýšit personální kapacity a investice do obranných technologií stejně tak jako sdílení dat mezi příslušnými orgány.

A za třetí, musíme podporovat inovace. Pokud naše firmy zatížíme byrokracií natolik, že vývoj umělé inteligence bude probíhat mimo Evropu, oslabíme tím sami sebe. Bez technologické konkurenceschopnosti nezajistíme naši bezpečnost. Evropa potřebuje více akceschopnosti, protože v éře umělé inteligence nebude rozhodovat ten, kdo napíše nejdelší regulaci, ale rozhodovat bude ten, kdo dokáže nejrychleji zareagovat.

Za prvé, centralizace sama o sobě bezpečnost nezaručí. Členské státy často reagují rychleji než Brusel, protože mají vlastní zkušenosti a mají vlastní kapacity a znají lépe své hrozby. Musíme jim dát větší pravomoci a flexibilitu a neřídit všechno z jednoho centra.

Za druhé, nestačí regulovat. Evropa vytváří pravidla, ale nástroje na jejich implementaci často chybí. Potřebujeme nejdříve navýšit personální kapacity a investice do obranných technologií stejně tak jako sdílení dat mezi příslušnými orgány.

A za třetí, musíme podporovat inovace. Pokud naše firmy zatížíme byrokracií natolik, že vývoj umělé inteligence bude probíhat mimo Evropu, oslabíme tím sami sebe. Bez technologické konkurenceschopnosti nezajistíme naši bezpečnost. Evropa potřebuje více akceschopnosti, protože v éře umělé inteligence nebude rozhodovat ten, kdo napíše nejdelší regulaci, ale rozhodovat bude ten, kdo dokáže nejrychleji zareagovat.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowni Państwo! Tak, potrzebujemy cyberbezpieczeństwa. Tak, potrzebujemy zmierzyć się z wyzwaniami przyszłości, ponieważ świat, który na naszych oczach się zmienia, staje się coraz bardziej chaotyczny i pełen zagrożeń. Ale żałuję, że ponad połowa tej sali nie dostrzega groteskowości tej debaty. Prawie połowa z was chciałaby iść na wojnę, na walkę ze Stanami, z Chinami, rywalizować z nimi, z Elonem Muskiem. Tylko nie dostrzegacie, że wasza legislacja, tony papieru, które tutaj wyprodukowaliście, powodują brak konkurencyjności, brak najnowocześniejszych technologii w Unii Europejskiej.

Szanowni państwo dyskutują o cyberbezpieczeństwie, a przecież w Brukseli czasem nie jesteśmy w stanie głosować, bo przyciski w sali nie działają. Popatrzcie na systemy informatyczne w Parlamencie Europejskim. W jaki sposób one skutecznie działają na co dzień? To jest po prostu groteska i żart. Nie jesteście w stanie zapewnić cyberbezpieczeństwa w Europie.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Frau Exekutiv-Vizepräsidentin der Kommission! Wir sind uns einig: Die künstliche Intelligenz wird unsere Welt neu ordnen und wir müssen mehr dafür tun, damit wir nicht ins Hintertreffen geraten.

Die gute Nachricht hat die Frau Kommissarin kürzlich gesagt: 45 000 Start-ups gibt es in Europa, 8 000 beschäftigen sich mit künstlicher Intelligenz. Aber wir brauchen eine Kapitalmarktunion, und wir müssen bitte wirklich talent aus den USA holen. Viele Forscherinnen und Forscher sind in dieser Trump-Welt ohnehin nicht mehr glücklich. Bitte holen wir sie her, sie können in Europa wunderbar arbeiten.

Denn die Gefahren müssen wir auch sehen: Cyberangriffe können unsere Kraftwerke lahmlegen, der hybride Krieg Russlands gegen uns wird in vielen Bereichen, gerade auch mit der künstlichen Intelligenz, noch verstärkt, gerade auch im Bereich Desinformation, was wir ja in einem eigenen Ausschuss auch behandeln. Eine Gefahr besteht auch für unsere Infrastruktur. Deswegen gibt es nur eines: unabhängig werden!

Und – Entschuldigung – den größten Unsinn habe ich wieder von Rechtsaußen gehört: Da ist von nationaler Souveränität die Rede. Ja, wie soll denn das funktionieren? Es kann nur eine europäische Souveränität geben und daran müssen wir arbeiten, bitte, gemeinsam für unser Europa. Wir schaffen das!

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, the newest AI model from Anthropic, Mythos, is so effective at finding weaknesses in software that they decided to only give access to a few companies from the US. In the wrong hands, it can be used to exploit digital vulnerabilities, like attacking bank accounts or health records at a speed and skill never seen before. Another wake-up call for Europe!

Anyone who believes the best AI will always be available to us is making a dangerous assumption. As soon as AI models become strategic assets for cybersecurity, defence or economic power, access will become selective. If we do not have AI made in Europe, if we do not control our own digital infrastructure, we cannot control our own future.

The next AI model might not be kept under lock and key. It might be pointed at us! So I ask you, Commissioner, to act quickly and build EU-owned infrastructure, data centres, cloud and compute on European soil. Invest in research and development of purpose-built AI, cybersecurity and open source standards. If we act quickly, we will still have a future made in Europe.
