paragraphs.text: Gerbiama Pirmininke, gerbiami kolegos. Ekspertai sako, kad po keleto metų socialiniai tinklai, kuriais dabar naudojamės, bus istorija. Juos pakeis dirbtinis intelektas su daugeliui dar sunkiai suprantamomis technologijomis. Saugumo ekspertai taip pat perspėja, kad netrukus ateis laikas, kai dirbtinis intelektas mums rodys pasaulį. Tie, kas kontroliuos dirbtinį intelektą, tas valdys ir žmonių veiksmus. Deja, bet kiekvienas pažangos elementas gali būti panaudojamas piktam. Todėl turime pasiruošti dirbtinio intelekto instrumentalizacijai. Kolegos kalbėjo apie duomenų panaudojimą, tačiau ekspertai perspėja apie duomenų užnuodijimą. Labai džiaugiamės ChatGPT pagalba, tačiau turime būti pasiruošę manipuliacijoms ir duomenų panaudojimui piktam.

Visa tai greitai bus svarbiausias saugumo klausimas. Tačiau būtų klaida pažangą stabdyti draudimais. Reikia kuo skubiau investuoti į savarankišką Europos Sąjungos dirbtinio intelekto infrastruktūrą. Būtina efektyvi gyventojų švietimo dėl dirbtinio intelekto sistema. Struktūriškai einame teisingu keliu. Dabartinėje Komisijoje Hennos Virkkunen portfelis jau aiškiau konsoliduoja dirbtinio intelekto klausimus vienoje politinėje atsakomybėje. Linkiu Jums sėkmės, Henna. Laiko neturime daug.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, o seu telemóvel acaba de vibrar. Lá, encontra uma mensagem com um número desconhecido: é o seu filho com um áudio claro. Ficou sem bateria, está a caminho de casa, mas não tem como pagar o comboio. Voluntariamente, envia para este contacto o montante equivalente ao bilhete de regresso. Só que este não era o seu filho — era um agente sofisticado de inteligência artificial que acabava de servir os propósitos de uma equipa de burlões.

Hoje, os ataques cibernéticos não atacam apenas os mais velhos. São cada vez mais eficazes entre o público digitalmente preparado. No último ano, na União Europeia, o sucesso do cibercrime por phishing subiu de 12 % para 54 %, quando comparamos ataques tradicionais com ataques auxiliados por inteligência artificial. Na indústria, o custo médio de cada um destes ataques situa-se nos 5 milhões de euros. No total, são mais 22 % de ataques face ao ano anterior.

Por isso, não, não basta regular. É urgente termos soberania digital europeia, termos empresas europeias, mas controlarmos o código que aqui também se faz. E, para isso, Senhora Comissária, é hora de aumentar o investimento na capacidade operacional para garantir que a regulação é mesmo sinónimo de proteção.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, Minister and dear colleagues, I would not repeat here all the threats created by artificial intelligence, nor all the opportunities it offers.

But I would invite us to think about something else. Why is it that every time we discuss a critically important sector, we discover that Europe is dependent – dependent in energy, dependent in defence, dependent in critical technologies?

An interesting thing is that every time I meet with industries from the countries on which we depend in the field of technology, they all say the same thing – you are excellent at regulating. We are learning from you. It is kind of inspiring. But the question is, do they truly admire our regulatory approach or do they simply understand that Europe's tendency to overregulate everything that moves often becomes their advantage?

If we want to remain secure and competitive in the age of artificial intelligence, Europe must learn not only how to regulate, but also how to create, develop and protect its own technologies. That's the only way out of dependencies.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, hace unos años, pensábamos que las mayores amenazas para nuestra seguridad eran físicas y hoy sabemos que lo son también digitales; que la inteligencia artificial, además de servir para avanzar y para innovar, también sirve para atacar infraestructuras críticas, para arrojar información sensible y para desestabilizar servicios públicos. Y el desarrollo de sistemas avanzados de inteligencia artificial como Mythos ha marcado un punto de inflexión para la seguridad europea, que no puede depender de otros países en tecnologías clave como el almacenamiento de datos, como los microchips o como la propia inteligencia artificial.

Tenemos capacidades y está en nuestras manos reforzar de verdad la protección digital de nuestras empresas, de nuestras instituciones y de nuestros servicios esenciales. Hay que crear también una estrategia europea específica para hacer frente a las amenazas de la IA e invertir más en tecnología europea para reducir dependencias externas y para fortalecer nuestra capacidad industrial y tecnológica.

Esto realmente es una oportunidad para Euskadi y para Europa, porque sin seguridad sabemos que no hay libertad y porque proteger nuestras infraestructuras críticas y nuestros datos sensibles no es cerrar Europa al mundo, es garantizar nuestra seguridad, nuestra resiliencia y nuestra autonomía en un contexto global cada vez más competitivo y más inestable.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, le cyberespace est devenu un terrain de confrontation permanent. Les cyberattaques frappent nos hôpitaux, nos réseaux d'énergie, nos institutions démocratiques. Elles touchent chaque jour la vie concrète de nos citoyens, leurs données, leurs économies, leurs services essentiels. Et depuis que l'intelligence artificielle est entrée dans l'équation, leur sophistication a franchi un seuil nouveau.

Dans le domaine de la défense, c'est particulièrement alarmant. Des acteurs étatiques utilisent désormais des modèles avancés pour identifier des vulnérabilités dans nos systèmes militaires, perturber nos communications et mener des opérations de désinformation à une échelle industrielle.

L'Europe n'est pas restée les bras croisés. Le paquet cybersécurité de janvier 2026, le renforcement de l'ENISA, les exigences du règlement de l'IA, tout cela constitue une base sérieuse. Nous avons construit un cadre et c'est un réel acquis.

Mais ce cadre ne suffira pas si nous dépendons de technologies que nous ne maîtrisons pas. L'autonomie stratégique de l'Europe n'est pas une option. Elle est une nécessité vitale, car nos adversaires ne se donnent pas les mêmes limites. Nos normes sont une force, elles ne doivent jamais devenir une faiblesse. Nous devons investir massivement dans notre expertise, dans nos capacités propres, dans notre souveraineté numérique. Légiférer aujourd'hui ne suffit pas, il faut anticiper et agir.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Alltså att komma ikapp någon är väl inte någon riktig vision egentligen. Särskilt när denna någon knappast är ett föredöme. Den vulgära och onaturliga rikedom som nu staplas hos de amerikanska techoligarkerna äventyrar ju vår demokrati och vår säkerhet. Vi behöver våra egna alternativ i Europa.

Men Europa ska inte skapa sina egna techmoguler. Den nya tekniken ska användas för människans väl. Inte för att några få ska tälja guld med soppslev, medan vi andra betalar med att förpesta vår mentala och emotionella kapacitet genom att scrolla reklam från morgon till kväll.

Visionen måste ju handla om mer fritid, mer trygghet, mer glädje i människors vardag, om teknik som frigör snarare än skapar nya bojor. Vårt jobb, det är att se till att vi kommer ur den här teknikrevolutionen som ett rättvisare, bättre samhälle för alla.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, the Mythos affair showed what we already knew: that sadly, the EU lives in the stone age of AI. Very embarrassing.

Our mindset is that of bureaucracy and of isolationism that we confuse with sovereignty. We fail to invest in energy innovation. We struggle to reduce bureaucracy. There is no vision. We act as if advanced AI is the enemy, but it is not – criminals are; EU paralysis is.

As Mistral founder Arthur Mensch said recently, Europe does not have many strengths, heavy regulation is a burden and the market takes shape too slowly. Therefore, those who can invest are Americans – not only because they have a market, but also because they believe in the future, whereas we have a fixed mindset about technology, our AI Office is understaffed, underpowered and already lagging behind the technology it's supposed to face.

Meanwhile, the Commission is busy drafting safeguards for the future, as if AI is a sci-fi promise instead of the tool already patching our security breaches today. That's not leadership. That's like building a smoke detector in a burning house. Yes, AI is a double-edged sword. Let's cut bureaucracy so that we can use the right edge.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire Virkkunen, Madame la Ministre, chers collègues, je me réjouis de ce débat sur la cybersécurité et la préparation de l’Union européenne face aux systèmes d’intelligence artificielle avancée, un enjeu crucial pour notre sécurité et notre souveraineté. L’IA, c’est à la fois une formidable opportunité et un défi majeur en matière de cybersécurité. Si nous voulons protéger nos infrastructures, nos institutions et nos citoyens, l’Europe doit se doter d’un cadre solide et ambitieux.

Car dans le même temps, alors même que l’AI Act n’est pas encore mis en œuvre, la Commission souhaite déjà déréguler et revenir sur certains standards via l’omnibus «IA». Ce n’est pas la bonne direction. Lorsque nous avions adopté l’AI Act, nous étions fiers d’être pionniers d’un cadre clair et éthique, conciliant innovation et sécurité. Aujourd’hui, nous risquons d’affaiblir cette ambition sous la pression de certains lobbies qui privilégient les intérêts de court terme.

Je me réjouis néanmoins de certaines avancées dans l’accord omnibus – je pense à l’interdiction des nudifiers –, mais cela ne peut justifier l’affaiblissement d’un cadre que nous avons voulu protecteur. Nous devons, Madame la Commissaire, rester exigeants. Oui à l’innovation, oui à une Europe forte technologiquement, mais jamais au prix de la sécurité de nos concitoyens.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisară, securitatea cibernetică și inteligența artificială devin noul front strategic al Europei. Atacurile digitale nu vizează doar rețele informatice, afectează infrastructuri critice, instituții publice, procese democratice și chiar mințile concetățenilor noștri.
În același timp, sistemele avansate de IA accelerează manipularea informațională și războiul hibrid contra Europei. De aceea, trebuie să trecem la capacitate strategică reală.

Avem nevoie de cel puțin trei măsuri concrete. Prima este crearea unui mecanism european de răspuns rapid la atacuri cibernetice majore asupra infrastructurilor critice. A doua: investiții comune într-o infrastructură europeană de IA și calcul avansat pentru a reduce dependențele tehnologice externe. Și, în fine, un lucru foarte important, un audit european obligatoriu pentru sistemele de amplificare algoritmică ale marilor platforme digitale, deoarece manipularea algoritmică devine o problemă de securitate democratică.
În acest moment reglementăm doar conținutul. Doamnă comisară, avem nevoie de un program SAFE pentru cybersecurity.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, we all see benefits from digitalisation in different sectors. Health is no exception. We enjoy speed, comfort and efficiency, and research possibilities that digitalisation brings to our lives.

But at the same time, we became dependent on technologies that are vulnerable in many ways. Automated cyberattacks, data exploitation, manipulation and bias, possible weaponisation of artificial intelligence: these are just a few examples that demonstrate the possible spectrum of the security problems we are already facing or will face in a close future.

Therefore, there is a strong need for preparedness in cybersecurity, robust security frameworks, regular testing and validation, data privacy and protection, collaboration and information sharing, adaptive response plans, research and innovation in this field. As AI systems become more advanced, the landscape of cybersecurity risks expands, requiring proactive, adaptive and comprehensive preparedness strategies.

paragraphs.text: Gospa predsednica! Če danes nekdo lahko z enim samim algoritmom ohromi bolnišnico, izbriše zaupanje v volitve ali sproži paniko med milijoni, potem kibernetska varnost ni več samo tehnološka tema, kajne?

Kdo bo v prihodnosti postavljal pravila: demokratične institucije ali netransparentni sistemi brez odgovornosti? Ko je en heker z javno dostopno umetno inteligenco vdrl v več mehiških vladnih agencij in ukradel občutljive podatke, bi to moral biti alarm za vse nas. In od takrat se grožnje samo še stopnjujejo. Napredni sistemi umetne inteligence so orodje in kot vsako orodje lahko ali ščitijo ali uničujejo. Ne moremo si več privoščiti naivnosti. Seveda je evropska zakonodaja pomembna, ampak sama po sebi nas ne bo zaščitila. Potrebujemo več evropskih zmogljivosti, več vlaganja v kibernetsko odpornost in manj odvisnosti od tujih tehnoloških gigantov.

Talent imamo, podjetja imamo. Zdaj je čas, da evropske tehnologije nehamo samo subvencionirati, ampak jih začnemo uporabljati. Ker če bo tehnologija napredovala hitreje, kot bomo sposobni zaščititi našo demokracijo, potem vprašanje ne bo več, kaj vse zmore umetna inteligenca. Vprašanje bo, ali bomo še vedno odločali mi o njej ali pa bo ona odločala o nas.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, Minister, dear colleagues, today we are facing a completely new reality in cybersecurity. The new AI model Mythos was considered so powerful and potentially dangerous that its developers decided not to release it publicly. What makes this especially alarming is the speed and precision with which this system can operate. AI is now capable of detecting and combining hidden software vulnerabilities at a pace that the human eye and human mind simply cannot follow.

Europe must be prepared for this new reality. We need stronger cooperation between our Member States and faster sharing of cybersecurity information. We also need clear European rules for the use of AI in critical sectors such as energy, transport, healthcare and digital infrastructure.

For industry, especially in smaller and highly digitalised countries like Estonia, cybersecurity is essential. A single AI-driven cyberattack can stop production, damage supply chains or expose sensitive data. Public services must also be protected. Hospitals, schools, emergency services and public administration cannot afford the long interruption of cyberattacks against sensitive systems.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, Minister, colleagues, it is obvious that the European Union must remain resilient, secure and prepared in the face of rapidly advancing AI technologies.

Our democratic institutions, critical infrastructure, healthcare systems and citizens must be protected against new risks and challenges emerging from increasingly sophisticated AI systems. We must strengthen Europe's cyber-resilience against the misuse of advanced AI systems, including disinformation campaigns, automated surveillance, threats targeting critical infrastructure and democratic processes, health threats posed by AI, cyberattacks against hospitals.
We must strengthen ENISA, turning it into a fully functioning agency. We must establish a comprehensive cyberdefence shield and infrastructure.

But democratic and parliamentary oversight, human accountability, transparency and robust safeguards must remain central to any deployment of AI in security-related contexts. The use of AI in cybersecurity and defence does not undermine fundamental rights, social rights and democratic controls.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, non dobbiamo temere il progresso, ma dobbiamo governarlo, affinché la tecnologia resti al servizio dell'uomo e non sfugga al controllo della società.

I rischi dell'intelligenza artificiale sono sotto gli occhi di tutti: dai deep fake fino a minacce ancora più gravi, cyberattacchi, vulnerabilità individuate su larga scala, attacchi contro infrastrutture critiche e servizi essenziali.

Non parliamo soltanto di sicurezza digitale, parliamo di sicurezza nazionale e guerra ibrida: colpire uno Stato senza muovere un carro armato, paralizzando reti e manipolando le informazioni. Implementare i nostri strumenti normativi è necessario, ma le norme, da sole, non bastano.

Il punto politico è questo: l'Europa non può diventare il continente che regola tecnologie prodotte, addestrate e aggiornate da altri. I nostri competitor globali corrono, sviluppano modelli sempre più innovativi, mentre noi siamo in tremendo ritardo. E il futuro non ci aspetta: abbiamo bisogno di modelli europei avanzati di intelligenza artificiale, cloud sicuri, capacità di calcolo e cybersicurezza.

È questo il nuovo fronte dell'indipendenza geopolitica, perché governare l'IA significa riaffermare il primato della politica sulla tecnica: non per frenare il futuro, ma per evitare che siano altri a scriverlo per noi.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Vice-présidente de la Commission européenne Virkunnen, chers collègues, le physicien Stephen Hawking nous avait prévenus: l’IA pourrait être la meilleure ou la pire chose qu'il arrivera à l’humanité. Aujourd’hui, nous faisons face à une déferlante de cyberattaques toujours plus sophistiquées, plus rapides et plus autonomes. Et le cyber-risque n’a aucune frontière. Avec Anthropic et son modèle américain Mythos, certains parlent déjà d’une bombe atomique numérique, car ce modèle d’IA, le plus puissant au monde, est capable d’infiltrer et d’orchestrer des cyberattaques massives dans des infrastructures essentielles comme les hôpitaux, les banques, les transports. La boîte de Pandore est ouverte et d’autres modèles encore plus puissants suivront, comparables à des cyber-armes.

Dans ce contexte, l’Europe ne peut pas se satisfaire d’être une colonie numérique. Pendant que les menaces s’accélèrent, des États hostiles et des groupes criminels se préparent. Alors, quand allons-nous bâtir une vraie IA européenne souveraine? Car dans cette guerre numérique, la cybersécurité est un enjeu de souveraineté. Madame la Vice-présidente de la Commission européenne, l’Europe doit urgemment reconnaître les IA avancées comme des infrastructures stratégiques critiques, au même titre que les télécommunications ou l’énergie, et on doit construire une capacité européenne autonome de cybersécurité pilotée par l’IA pour réduire nos dépendances technologiques.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, liebe Frau Exekutiv-Vizepräsidentin Henna Virkkunen, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Österreichs ehemaliger Bundeskanzler Wolfgang Schüssel, der dieser Tage in den Europäischen Verdienstorden aufgenommen wird, hat gestern hier im Europäischen Parlament darauf hingewiesen, dass fast täglich irgendwo in Europa Behörden auf verschiedenen Ebenen – lokal, regional, selbstverständlich auch auf staatlicher Ebene und europäisch – von Cyberangriffen betroffen sind. Wir müssen es ernst nehmen, dass unsere europäische Art der Zivilisation, der Freiheit und der Menschenwürde angegriffen wird – und in Zeiten wie diesen selbstverständlich auch mit digitalen Mitteln und jetzt und ab jetzt ganz besonders auch mit Mitteln der künstlichen Intelligenz.

Wir sind leider zum Kontinent des Konsums geworden im Bereich der Digitalisierung und auch im Bereich der künstlichen Intelligenz. Europa muss aber der Kontinent der Innovation und der Produktion sein, und dafür ist vieles zu tun. Nicht, weil wir uns abschotten wollen von anderen Teilen der Welt. Ganz im Gegenteil: Wir wollen kooperieren, aber auf einer festen, eigenen, selbstständigen und auch selbstbewussten Basis.

Dafür ist eine Fülle von Maßnahmen zu treffen. Das beginnt bei Investitionen, die wir lockermachen müssen durch einen Kapitalbinnenmarkt. Das beginnt auch bei der Ausbildung junger Menschen. Das beginnt dabei, auch Mädchen und Frauen für naturwissenschaftliche Fächer und technologische Berufe zu interessieren, damit wir das Potenzial, das in Europa ist, heben, für unsere Sicherheit und auch für unseren Wohlstand auf dem Weg Richtung Aufschwung.

paragraphs.text: Gospa predsednica! Evropska unija se sooča z vse bolj sofisticiranimi kibernetskimi grožnjami. Napadi na bolnišnice, energetska omrežja in javne inštitucije niso več izjema, ampak nova realnost.

Hkrati vidimo tudi uporabo umetne inteligence za ustvarjanje deep fake posnetkov, dezinformacij, napadov na politike, novinarje ter seveda civilno družbo. A razprava ni črno bela. Umetna inteligenca predstavlja resno tveganje za našo varnost. Obenem pa sodobni umetno-inteligenčni sistemi že danes odkrivajo kritične ranljivosti v digitalnih sistemih, ki jih tradicionalni varnostni pregledi niso zaznali. Umetna inteligenca je torej hkrati nevarnost in priložnost, zatorej Evropa potrebuje skupen in usklajen pristop h kibernetski varnosti. Grožnje ne poznajo meja držav članic, zato potrebujemo močnejše evropsko sodelovanje, hitrejšo izmenjavo informacij in večjo tehnološko suverenost. paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, Уважаема г-жо Комисар, уважаеми колеги, когато говорим за киберсигурност, вече не говорим само за защита на компютърни системи. Говорим за това дали ще функционира транспортната ни инфраструктура, дали електропреносните мрежи ще работят, дали ще бъдат защитени болниците ни, дали банките ще издържат на атака, дали демокрацията ще устои на манипулации.

Днес с алгоритъм могат да се причинят щети, за които преди бяха необходими армии. Пред очите ни се променя самата природа на заплахите. Новите технологии с изкуствен интелект са все по-мощни и по-автономни. Те могат да бъдат инструмент за защита от кибератаки, за по-бърза реакция при кризи. Но същите тези технологии могат да бъдат използвани и за злонамерени действия. Искаме Европа да бъде едновременно сигурна и конкурентоспособна.

Не трябва да избираме между иновации и защита. Трябва да постигнем и двете. Но нека е ясно: това не е въпрос само на технологии, а преди всичко на хора. Няма лидерство без инвестиции в бъдещи лидери. Нуждаем се от повече специалисти по киберсигурност и изкуствен интелект, от по-силни партньорства между университетите и индустрията. Нуждаем се от европейски капацитет, който да задава посока в ключовите високотехнологични области. Европа не бива да разчита на външни технологии в сфера, която е пряко свързана със сигурността и суверенитета. Защото технологичната зависимост носи стратегически риск.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, suveranitatea este o proprietate a celor puternici, care au tehnologie și cu ajutorul căreia văd mai multă realitate decât vedem noi și pot să facă lucruri pe care noi nu le putem face. Suveranitatea este capacitatea de a face singur lucrurile de care depinzi, de care depinde securitatea ta.

Poți fi oare suveran când nu ai propriile companii strategice de tehnologie? Tehnologia dezvoltată de oameni servește interesele acelor oameni și acelor companii. Noi nu apărem în poza asta, nu sunt companiile noastre. Mai ești oare suveran când informația care ajunge la cetățenii tăi și care le determină comportamentul este filtrată de algoritmii unor companii din afara granițelor?
Dacă nu înțelegem asta, companiile străine de tehnologie vor stabili ce se întâmplă la noi și cu noi, în timp ce noi vom decide ce facem cu dopurile de la sticlele noastre de plastic.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, the first and perhaps biggest challenge for European cybersecurity is that Europe is falling behind the United States and China in the development of advanced AI technologies.

Last year, 5 000 major cyber-incidents were recorded across Europe, and behind this activity we usually see Russia and China. This is not only a technological challenge, but rather security and defence.

Lithuania and other countries on the eastern border have experienced for years cyberattacks, disinformation and hybrid operations against our institutions and critical infrastructure. In Lithuania alone, authorities recorded nearly 4 000 cyber incidents last year – a 63 % increase compared to the previous years, amounting to more than 10 cyber incidents every single day.

Now, advanced AI systems are making these threats even more dangerous. At the same time, Europe still depends heavily on non-European AI technologies. We are strong in regulation, but not in capability. Legislation such as the European Chips Act should help Europe strengthen its own AI capacities.

We need European innovation, European computing capacity and European expertise in cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Our task is not only to regulate existing, but to boost creation of our own technologies, strengthening Europe's security and resilience.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi e colleghe, quando parliamo di sicurezza informatica e di intelligenza artificiale parliamo della libertà dell'Europa.

Non possiamo essere soltanto un mercato per tecnologie sviluppate altrove. Dobbiamo costruire infrastrutture europee capaci di proteggere i cittadini, i dati e l'economia. Per farlo, serve il coraggio di investire anche nei territori che possono diventare la nuova frontiera strategica del continente.

Nel Mezzogiorno d'Italia esistono università, centri di ricerca e competenze già protagonisti nei progetti sulla cibersicurezza e sull'innovazione. Il Sud ha energie e talenti giovani che l'Europa non può più continuare a perdere.
Investire nel Sud Italia, nel Sud Europa significa rafforzare l'autonomia strategica dell'intera Unione europea, significa costruire un'Europa meno dipendente, più sicura e più unita.

L'intelligenza artificiale non è solamente una sfida tecnologica: è una sfida prima di tutto politica, poi sociale e civile e l'Europa la vincerà, questa sfida, soltanto se saprà trasformare le sue periferie in nuovi centri di innovazione, di dignità e di futuro.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, recientemente han emergido —a estas alturas ya lo sabemos todos— desarrollos de inteligencia artificial avanzada con capacidades realmente extraordinarias. Se trata de sistemas que pueden identificar fallos en software de forma autónoma, pero a la vez generar mecanismos para utilizarlos con otros fines.

Estamos ante un salto cualitativo en el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial con una velocidad exponencial nunca conocida. Hasta ahora, el debate sobre la regulación de la inteligencia artificial se había centrado en cuestiones como la transparencia o los sesgos algorítmicos y cuestiones de esa naturaleza. Sin embargo, estos desarrollos introducen un nuevo contexto y nuevos factores y elementos. Entramos en el ámbito de las gestiones y la gestión de capacidades con potencial de uso dual, con implicaciones directas para la seguridad en general de los ciudadanos y de las empresas.

En este contexto, la IA se convierte en un recurso estratégico. Es el momento para que la Unión Europea defina su posición, que debe adaptarse a esta nueva realidad. Ante estas amenazas que trascienden fronteras, necesitamos respuestas a la escala adecuada, y esa escala es la europea.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Frau Exekutiv-Vizepräsidentin der Kommission! Dieser Krieg ist nicht vorbei, erklärte der Anwalt von Elon Musk, nachdem seine 114 Milliarden EUR schwere Klage gegenüber OpenAI abgewiesen wurde. Das zeigt, dass es bei künstlicher Intelligenz längst nicht mehr nur um Technologie und wirtschaftliche Interessen, sondern um viel mehr geht – um Macht, Informationssicherheit und Kontrolle. Fortschrittliche KI-Systeme erkennen Schwachstellen in Computersystemen, skalieren Cyberangriffe und gefährden kritische Infrastruktur – das stellt eine reale Bedrohung für Europa dar. Daher muss die Europäische Union cybersicher werden.

Europa war Vorreiter bei der KI-Entwicklung. Wir haben die Fähigkeit und das Know-how nach wie vor und brauchen KI nicht mit Angst zu begegnen. Schon deshalb nicht, weil wir bei den fortschrittlichsten KI-Systemen vollständig von intransparenten, außereuropäischen Akteuren unabhängig sein müssen.

Wir können auch nicht davon ausgehen, Rechtsstaatlichkeit gelte auch im digitalen Raum. Technologische Innovation darf niemals zu rechtsfreien Räumen führen und schon gar nicht demokratische Kontrolle ersetzen.
Setzen wir jetzt den AI Act, Datenschutz und cyber-resilience-Regeln konsequent um und durch.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, mes chers collègues, l'annonce de l'IA Mythos a révélé ce que nous refusions de voir: il existe désormais des modèles d'intelligence artificielle capables de briser en quelques heures les meilleures cyberdéfenses du monde. La planète cyber brûle et nous regardons ailleurs, alors que nous sommes déjà sous la menace permanente de la guerre hybride que la Russie nous mène.

Au moment où nous réarmons l'Europe avec ReArm Europe et SAFE, il est temps de sortir de la naïveté face au risque cyber. Le nouveau règlement sur la cybersécurité doit bannir d'urgence l'accès des États hostiles à nos infrastructures digitales stratégiques. Sans cela, ce texte ne sera que du bavardage.

Nos lois actuelles, comme la mobilité militaire ou le Space Act, traitent ce risque. Mais il nous faut désormais systématiser les stress tests à l'ensemble des infrastructures vulnérables. Après avoir raté le tournant de l'intelligence artificielle qui nous prive de la capacité à nous défendre contre cette menace, nous ne devons pas louper la prochaine étape, celle de la révolution quantique, qui représente l'avenir du chiffrement. Pour cela, nous devons prévoir les investissements à la hauteur, notamment par le Fonds de compétitivité.

Pripravnost više nije izbor, u vremenu umjetne inteligencije otpornost znači moć, a Europa mora biti spremna.

Moramo ulagati u europsku kibernetičku obranu, u vlastite tehnologije i tehnološki suverenitet.

Pripravnost više nije izbor, u vremenu umjetne inteligencije otpornost znači moć, a Europa mora biti spremna.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, artificial intelligence has changed our lives forever, in both good and bad.
Unfortunately, Europe has fallen behind its competitors, but this should not come as a surprise. Our unhinged obsession with regulation has brought us to this point.

Now, we are afraid of what others are creating. We are in a situation where American companies are able to produce models with supreme hacking abilities. We may not like it, but you cannot deny that it's an asset for them.

I agree that such models should face proper inspection and monitoring, but I cannot help thinking if without all the regulation, European companies could have created something that the rest of the world would be willing to inspect.
It's not the companies' fault, it's the EU decision-makers that have made Europe the loser.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, Europa es vulnerable. El avance de la inteligencia artificial provoca incertidumbre. Amenaza en mi país, por ejemplo, a 270 000 personas, un 10 % de la población, cuatro de cada diez puestos de trabajo, o sea, en total, un 38 % del empleo. Eso no es nuevo, la tecnología no es neutral. Hay que ver también esa dimensión social: se está produciendo en las empresas tecnológicas, con despidos masivos a nivel mundial, y por eso hay que realizar un análisis riguroso, regular y proteger también la ciberseguridad.

Debemos tener nosotros, en Europa, el control de la tecnología y no al revés. La IA tiene que ser considerada un servicio público —también la ciberseguridad— y debe ser regulada con programas públicos para trabajadores despedidos y deslocalizados.

Además, sabemos ya —según dice la ONU— que va a afectar más a las mujeres, infrarrepresentadas en empleos relacionados con la IA, ya que las estructuras sociales y económicas van a reproducir modelos de discriminación. Y sí, somos vulnerables: al uso malicioso de la IA, a la desinformación y al fraude.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiama Pirmininke. Žinot, klausydamas diskusijų aš nežinau, kur randuosi – Rusijos parlamente ar Europos Sąjungos Parlamente. Šiandien lyderis kovojant su dirbtiniu intelektu, taip pat su internetu yra Rusija. Ten uždraustos įvairios programėlės – Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram. Mes irgi tą patį darome. Europa vietoj to, kad vystytų dirbtinį intelektą savo, ji seka Rusijos keliu – bando kovoti su juo ir cenzūruoti dirbtinį intelektą.

Pasaulyje pirmauja dvi šalys, vystydamos dirbtinį intelektą, – Rusija ir Kinija. Gal mes nežiūrėkime į Rusiją, gal žiūrėkime geriau į Jungtines Amerikos Valstijas ir vystykime šitas technologijas. Vien tik kovodami ir eidami paskui Rusiją mes tikrai atsidursime tokioje situacijoje, kokioje yra dabar Rusijos piliečiai. Jie negali susikalbėti, atsiskaityti banko kortele, nusipirkti maisto. Taigi permąstykime savo vertybes.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, madame la Ministre, madame la Vice-Présidente, nous connaissons nos vulnérabilités, mais nous restons enfermés dans une logique de réglementation et de défense, alors qu'il est temps d'adopter une stratégie offensive. L'enjeu est clair: réduire notre dépendance aux pays tiers, notamment aux États-Unis, pour les solutions technologiques, les équipements de sécurité et l'hébergement des données dans le cloud. L'Europe doit investir massivement dans ces secteurs pour accélérer l'émergence de start-ups et de champions technologiques capables de rivaliser à l'échelle mondiale.

Mais la technologie seule ne suffira pas. Notre véritable richesse, ce sont les ingénieurs et les talents que nous formons. Trop d'entre eux quittent l'Europe pour renforcer les entreprises américaines. Que faisons-nous pour les retenir ou les faire revenir? Trop peu. Nous devons créer un environnement qui inspire l'ambition, la confiance et la fierté européenne. C'est en redonnant aux Européens la conviction que nous pouvons relever les grands défis technologiques et stratégiques que nous construirons notre souveraineté.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, kolegice i kolege, sasvim je razvidno da danas govorimo o drugoj strani medalje, kako modeli AI mijenjaju kibernetičke prijetnje.

Tu se zapravo po meni mijenja i omjer snaga jer kibernetički kriminal sve više počiva na krađi, trgovini i iskorištavanju podataka. Jasno je, iz svega toga da Europa mora postati digitalno i tehnološki suverenija kako bi mogla odgovoriti na sigurnosne rizike. Za sve one skeptike koji su danas sudjelovali u raspravi, ja bih rekla da vlastiti AI razvoj, superračunala i zajednički sigurnosni kapaciteti moraju počivati na koordinaciji država članica. Govorim zapravo o digitalnoj obrani, jer danas je AI u cyber prostoru ono što su, primjerice, raketni sustavi dugog dometa na bojištu - pogađaju kritičnu infrastrukturu bez ulaska u zemlju.

Dvije su riječi po meni ključne: spremnost i otpornost. Spremnost: imati planove, stručnjake, zaštitne sustave i bržu koordinaciju prije napada i otpornost: da infrastruktura može nastaviti funkcionirati i oporaviti se nakon napada.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister, honourable Members, thank you for this very active debate. It really shows that the topic is very timely and requires our attention, because in today's world, cybersecurity is a very crucial, core part of our overall security. And in an increasingly AI-driven world, cybersecurity advancements, but also threats, now unfold at machine speed. And the situation demands that we also match this pace in our preparedness and in our resilience.

Today, our legislation provides us with the legal framework and also the operational tools needed to confront these risks. But it now needs to be fully implemented. And at the same time, we have to continue to build our own European capabilities. The European Commission will deploy all relevant instruments in collaboration with our agencies, with our Member States, and of course, with our critical infrastructure companies.

The Commission remains fully committed to closely monitoring the evolving implications of frontier AI for the cybersecurity of our critical infrastructure and supply chains as well. And with the support of this House, also to advance the necessary work to address them.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Vice-President, thank you for this important and very active and engaging debate. I believe there is broad agreement on the need for all stakeholders, including EU institutions, Member States and the industry, to closely cooperate in the development, testing and use of advanced AI systems. While we all acknowledge the potential risks that these systems can bring, it is also absolutely necessary to explore their potential benefits for our cybersecurity.

The Cypriot Presidency is fully committed to continue advancing and strengthening cooperation on cybersecurity, protecting our critical infrastructure and reinforcing our collective resilience. In this regard, the Council and the Member States will continue to work closely with the European Parliament and with the Commission in this joint effort, as we build our technological sovereignty.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Vice-président, chers collègues, voulons-nous que l'Europe soit un terrain de jeu pour oligarques chinois et tycoons américains? Non. Alors, votons la réforme du filtrage des investissements étrangers. Après ce long travail au Parlement, puis en trilogue, je tiens à remercier chaleureusement les shadow rapporteurs pour leur approche constructive et leur solide soutien.

Avec ce texte, nous mettons fin à la légendaire naïveté européenne. Non, la Chine ne construit pas une usine assemblant des voitures électriques en Hongrie pour créer de l'emploi en Europe. Elle le fait pour contourner nos défenses commerciales, pour ratiboiser nos propres productions et assurer sa domination sur un secteur stratégique. Certains investissements étrangers visent à nous affaiblir et à nous asservir. Avec ce texte, nous protégeons nos marchés des prédateurs étrangers qui s'emparent de nos ports, de nos aéroports, de nos réseaux de communication.

Avec ce texte, les États membres seront désormais tenus de contrôler les investissements stratégiques et nous avons arraché au Conseil une liste de secteurs qu'il jugeait au départ inacceptables. Le mécanisme que nous mettons en place impose à chaque État de rendre des comptes aux autres. Car une faille dans un seul État membre peut mettre en danger nos productions sur tout le continent.

C'est un pas en avant, mais le combat pour défendre les productions européennes doit se poursuivre avec l'accélérateur industriel. Alors, chers collègues, adoptons ce texte à une large majorité et continuons à nous battre pour construire cette puissance européenne souveraine et indépendante qui sera la seule à nous permettre à toutes et à tous de vivre libres.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Vice‑President Šefčovič, dear colleagues, when citizens look at Europe today, many of them see two contradictory realities at the same time. On the one hand, they expect Europe to protect them. Protect them from war, from economic dependency, from geopolitical pressure, from insecurity in an increasingly unstable world. On the other hand, many people also feel that European decisions are becoming more distant from their own democratic influence. That Europe is often strong in producing rules, but too weak in making political responsibility visible.

It is precisely between these two expectations that the European debate now takes place because the real question is no longer: do we need Europe or do we not? The real question is: how do we organise European capacity to act in a way that remains democratically accepted? Because one thing is clear: the world around us has fundamentally changed. War has returned to Europe. For the first time in decades, Europeans again understand that peace, prosperity and security cannot be taken for granted.

Strategic dependencies are increasingly being weaponised and, in such a world, national capacity alone, colleagues, is no longer sufficient in many key areas. That is obvious. No Member State, colleagues – and I speak to this side, and I think you agree – on its own will be large enough to fully control geopolitical risks. Not in energy, not in technology, not in security.

But something else is equally true. European integration can only succeed in the long term if citizens continue to feel that political decisions remain understandable, accountable and, where necessary, correctable. That is why we are holding this debate today, because the experience of the past decades also shows something important: where Europe has created clear common decision‑making procedures and structures, Europe is capable of delivering. The single market, trade policy, competition policy, the common currency – in these areas, Europe carries international weight because decisions can be taken jointly and implemented effectively.

Where Europe remains institutionally fragmented, however, common strategic action becomes far more difficult. We see this in parts of foreign policy, security policy, energy policy. And yet, colleagues, we should be careful not to draw the wrong conclusions from this. Europe will not become a centralised unitary state and it does not need to become one.

The motto of the United States of America is 'E pluribus unum'. 'Out of many, one'. Europeans have not achieved that, nor do they want to. Our motto is 'United in diversity' and that is a significant difference. Europe's strength has always been its ability to build common solutions where common action is necessary while preserving political and national diversity where diversity matters. That is why we must now have a pragmatic and honest discussion about how the European Union can become more capable of acting without losing democratic acceptance.

In my view, this requires, above all, three things. First, European decisions need clear political responsibility. Citizens must be able to understand more clearly who prepares decisions, who supports them and who is politically accountable for them. The European Commission has evolved to a kind of government. It therefore needs to become both electable and removable, which is largely not the case today.

Second, the European Parliament must be strengthened wherever democratic oversight and political correctability are concerned because democratic systems remain stable only if they remain capable of learning and adapting.

And third, we should openly recognise that differentiated integration has always been part of the European project. Schengen did not begin with all Member States. Neither did the euro. Europe has often advanced precisely because some Member States were willing to move forward together in specific areas without undermining the unity of the Union as a whole.

So, the key question today is not whether Europe should act. The key question is how Europe can remain capable of acting while also remaining democratically legitimate and politically accountable. This, colleagues, is why we turn today to the Council and the Commission with several questions.

To conclude, the questions are: where do you see the greatest institutional limits to Europe's capacity to act within the current framework? Which reforms do you consider feasible with the existing Treaties? Where do you believe further institutional adaptation may become necessary? And how will you ensure that stronger European action always remains linked to democratic accountability, parliamentary oversight and a renewed trust of European citizens? Because, colleagues, Europe will only remain strong externally if it remains democratically trusted internally.

Europe's strength has always been its ability to build common solutions where common action is necessary while preserving political and national diversity where diversity matters. That is why we must now have a pragmatic and honest discussion about how the European Union can become more capable of acting without losing democratic acceptance.

In my view, this requires, above all, three things. First, European decisions need clear political responsibility. Citizens must be able to understand more clearly who prepares decisions, who supports them and who is politically accountable for them. The European Commission has evolved to a kind of government. It therefore needs to become both electable and removable, which is largely not the case today.

Second, the European Parliament must be strengthened wherever democratic oversight and political correctability are concerned because democratic systems remain stable only if they remain capable of learning and adapting.

And third, we should openly recognise that differentiated integration has always been part of the European project. Schengen did not begin with all Member States. Neither did the euro. Europe has often advanced precisely because some Member States were willing to move forward together in specific areas without undermining the unity of the Union as a whole.

So, the key question today is not whether Europe should act. The key question is how Europe can remain capable of acting while also remaining democratically legitimate and politically accountable. This, colleagues, is why we turn today to the Council and the Commission with several questions.

To conclude, the questions are: where do you see the greatest institutional limits to Europe's capacity to act within the current framework? Which reforms do you consider feasible with the existing Treaties? Where do you believe further institutional adaptation may become necessary? And how will you ensure that stronger European action always remains linked to democratic accountability, parliamentary oversight and a renewed trust of European citizens? Because, colleagues, Europe will only remain strong externally if it remains democratically trusted internally.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: President-in-Office of the Council

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, Commissioner, thank you to the honourable Member Sven Simon for this oral question on behalf of the Committee on Constitutional Affairs. As a Union, we are indeed faced with a new geopolitical reality, a changed security landscape and an increasingly complex multitude of challenges, both on the internal and the external front. This context renders it essential to work together for a safer, more resilient and more united Union, a Union cooperating, open to the world as a predictable, reliable and credible partner from a point of internal unity and strength. It is also now more vital than ever that the Union speaks with one voice to defend its values and interests and promote multilateral solutions.

Following the recent war in Iran, the Union demonstrated its reliability, predictability, and credibility in response to this challenging environment as well as its economic repercussions. In fact, in the face of recent crises and challenges, the Union has demonstrated time and again its ability to act in a timely, efficient and effective manner, as we have done in the past four years to support Ukraine. We have also taken bold decisions to ramp up Europe's defence readiness, notably with the adoption of the SAFE instrument, as well as to strengthen our competitiveness. That is, of course, not to say that it is not at times very challenging to build consensus among our 27 Member States, and, as we have experienced on many occasions, effort and time are needed to achieve this consensus, to achieve unity, which is, in essence, our greatest strength.

Honourable Members, our Union is a project that has constantly evolved not despite crises, but because of them, in many cases, because those are the moments that have driven deeper integration of the European Union. Enlargement is an indispensable commitment of this evolution. Our most successful foreign policy tool, a strategic investment in the future of our Union – enlargement was at the heart of the informal ministerial meeting of Europe ministers that was held a couple of weeks ago in Nicosia with the participation of our enlargement partners. In that discussion, we focused on the fundamentals, the backbone of enlargement, the rule of law, democratic institutions, economic criteria. Discussions highlighted that geopolitical urgency does not lower the bar for accession. Quite the contrary, enlargement partners are expected to deliver sustained and measurable results, while the Union must ensure clarity, predictability and fairness, and the Cyprus Presidency has diligently worked and has delivered concrete progress on enlargement despite the challenges, while upholding the credibility of the established methodology and its merit‑based character.

Mr President, honourable Members, the EU also needs to be ready at the time of accession. In parallel to the enlargement process, the Union needs to lay the necessary internal groundwork for reform and address key questions related to its priorities and its policies, as well as its capacity to act. In its June 2024 roadmap for future work on internal reforms, and more recently, in December, the European Parliament invited the Commission to present these reviews containing operational elements on the four strands of work: values, policies, budget and governance. On EU governance, the presidency has taken good note of the European Parliament's work, in particular recent resolutions on the institutional consequences of the enlargement process and the institutional aspects of the Draghi report.

I wish to conclude by saying that the response to global challenges is not limited to governance issues. Our recently agreed 'One Europe, One Market' roadmap, signed in Nicosia in April, represents a concrete and ambitious step to enhance our strategic autonomy by strengthening our competitiveness, completing our single market and making it simpler for people and businesses. This is an urgent, shared responsibility on which we are acting decisively, and we are working together for a true energy union on solutions to ensure affordable energy and achieve the energy transition. At the same time, to be more strategically autonomous, we must have the means to do it. Advancing the work on the next MFF is therefore key to match our ambitions with the necessary resources.

As Council presidency, we have driven the European agenda forward in an inclusive manner, with a very clear objective for a Union that is more strategically autonomous. This work is an investment in the future of our Union.

interventions.speaker_label: Maroš Šefčovič, Member of the Commission.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Member of the Commission

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, Madam Minister, President of the Council, first and foremost, I would like to thank you and especially esteemed chairman of the AFCO Committee, Mr Simon, for having the opportunity to discuss the important question of EU governance in the context of the global challenges facing the Union. I am fully aware of how important this topic is for this House and especially for the Committee on Constitutional Affairs in particular. I would like to thank the members of the AFCO Committee for the excellent debate we had under the structured dialogue on these topics just three weeks ago.

As laid out in President von der Leyen's political guidelines, it is clear that we must pursue an ambitious reform agenda to ensure that our Union functions effectively, both as it grows and in order to keep up with a new geopolitical reality. Our decision-making processes must evolve if we are to retain the ability to act swiftly and decisively, both at home and on the world stage.

The Commission is ready to engage in this reflection, working hand in hand with Parliament and the Member States. We should approach these discussions with an open mind, whether the solutions lie within the existing Treaties or require deeper reform. Parliament's resolution of November 2023 has already set in motion the Treaty revision process. The ball is now in the Council's court, and the Commission stands ready to fulfil its institutional role, including by providing our opinion if and when consulted by the Council.

But we do not need to wait for Treaty change to act. We must use the existing tools to their full potential. For example, the passerelle clauses provide a pathway to shift from unanimity to qualified majority voting in key areas, including on foreign and security policy. The Commission has long advocated moving in this direction, including through our proposal in 2018 for the common foreign and security policy. We must also explore other mechanisms, such as the enhanced cooperation mechanism, in situations where progress is blocked by the lack of unanimity. This instrument has already proven its worth in several cases, most recently in delivering the EUR 90 billion support loan to Ukraine.

We must be ready for enlargement and to this end, the Commission has been gradually strengthening its methodology for preparing and admitting new Member States. We must be ready to face systemic geopolitical and economic shifts, which requires a strong and forward looking response. For the next multiannual financial framework, the Commission has therefore proposed a fundamental overhaul of the EU budget that will be more streamlined, flexible and impactful. In particular, the proposal on Global Europe provides predictable support, while at the same time increasing the margin of flexibility to respond to rising geopolitical challenges, crises and opportunities.

Honourable Members, whether through Treaty reform, passerelle clauses or enhanced cooperation, the Commission is committed to working with this House to build a Union that is swifter, stronger and more united.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Przestrzegam przed sytuacją, w której konieczne zmiany instytucjonalne w Unii Europejskiej spowodują, że będzie jedna ofiara tych zmian, a mianowicie jednomyślność. Europa się mierzy z wieloma wyzwaniami zewnętrznymi. Mamy wojny u naszych granic, destabilizację w kategoriach globalnych, ale nie możemy zamykać oczu na kryzys wewnętrzny. Nie ma dziś państwa, które byłoby całkowicie wolne od ataków rosyjskich, antyunijnych. To zjawisko ma charakter systemowy. To nie jest moment, by zagłębiać się w zmiany sposobu podejmowania decyzji instytucjonalnych.

Widzimy to zresztą wyraźnie w Parlamencie Europejskim, gdzie apele o zmianę zapadają często minimalną większością głosów, co pokazuje skalę podziałów. Unia opiera się na równowadze między dużymi i małymi państwami. Jednomyślność zapewnia trwałość, zaufanie i jedność. Zaufanie i jedność jest naszą bronią zarówno w kryzysie wewnętrznym, jak i zewnętrznym.
Oczywiście Unia musi się rozwijać. Reformy są zawsze możliwe, jeśli istnieje szeroki konsensus i wyraźna potrzeba, a przede wszystkim odpowiedni moment. To nie jest ten moment.

interventions.speaker_label: Juan Fernando López Aguilar, en nombre del Grupo S&D.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: en nombre del Grupo S&D

paragraphs.text: Presidente, comisario Šefčovič, «La gobernanza de la Unión bajo presión» es el título de este debate en un desorden global, entre turbulencias geopolíticas que desafían como nunca antes la razón de ser de Europa, fundada, regida y limitada por su propio ordenamiento, es decir, por el Derecho.
Y, en paralelo, una Europa con una legalidad internacional, aprendiendo de las lecciones de la devastación de la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

Europa se desmorona ante nuestros ojos bajo la presión de quienes reivindican el unilateralismo y la ley del más fuerte. Es imprescindible que la Unión Europea tenga así una voz digna de ser escuchada —ojalá respetada, pero sobre todo una Europa con algo que decir—.

Y esto no es posible bajo las actuales reglas de la unanimidad. Si no es posible con los 27 Estados miembros actuales, menos aún lo será ante la perspectiva de la ampliación, con diez Estados en la lista de espera. Por eso, es imprescindible que reformemos los Tratados, que es lo que pidió el Parlamento Europeo en 2023.

Se trata de realizar una reforma institucional que supere la regla disfuncional de la unanimidad e imponga —por fin— mayorías cualificadas, no solamente para dotar a la Unión Europea de sus propios recursos y recursos propios, sino para utilizar el endeudamiento que financie las nuevas ambiciones sin desmoronar lo que ha sido la razón de ser de Europa —que son su solidaridad, política regional y política de cohesión—.

Pero, sobre todo, una reforma institucional que además refuerce al Parlamento Europeo —por fin— con una iniciativa legislativa propia en sus poderes de investigación, de control de la Comisión, turno de preguntas, control parlamentario. Se trata, por tanto, de regular un relanzamiento en toda regla del Parlamento Europeo.

La conclusión está al alcance de cualquiera: nunca como ahora la Unión Europea ha estado tan sola y al mismo tiempo ha sido tan dependiente de sí misma en la globalización; de sí misma y de los Estados miembros, que no pueden ser solamente una coalición o una Unión dentro de la Unión, como se ha propuesto últimamente, sino que tiene que ser la voluntad política de ser la Europa de los Estados miembros y de quienes aspiran a serlo.
De eso depende, ahora más que nunca, el futuro de la UE.

interventions.speaker_label: Marieke Ehlers, on behalf of the PfE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PfE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, today, every disagreement has become an argument against unanimity and an excuse for centralising more power in Brussels. But Europe is not weak because of vetoes. Europe is weak because, for far too long, we have lacked political courage and strong national leadership.

Our leaders hide behind institutions and procedures instead of taking political responsibility. They have forgotten the art of statesmanship. The statesmen who built Europe understood that European cooperation cannot be imposed. It must be built through persuasion, vision, compromise and mutual respect. They did not seek to erase nations, but to reconcile them.

This lack of leadership will not be resolved by abolishing the national veto, especially not in foreign policy. Foreign policy is not a technical exercise to be reduced to majority arithmetic. It is the highest expression of national sovereignty – and Europe is not a state.

Our national histories, cultures, economic interests, geopolitical realities and democratic choices are not identical – and they never will be. Pretending otherwise will result in paralysis instead of progress.
The Treaties already provide for enhanced cooperation amongst willing Member States to move forward together, without forcing political integration upon those who do not consent to it.
That is the Europe we must defend: a Europe of sovereign states cooperating where necessary, acting together where possible, but always accountable first and foremost to their own citizens.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Unia Europejska potrzebuje zmiany. Tylko nie takiej zmiany, o której państwo tutaj dyskutujecie. Dotarliśmy do niesłychanego momentu, momentu, w którym obserwujemy fiasko ostatnich dekad polityki projektowanej w tym budynku i w Komisji Europejskiej. Coraz więcej Europejczyków jest sceptycznie nastawionych do Unii Europejskiej z powodu braku transparentności, nadregulacji, wzrostu kosztów życia, imigracji, wszelkich polityk tworzonych na poziomie europejskim, w oderwaniu od woli ludu.

Co symptomatyczne, podmiot, który najczęściej łamie traktaty i łamie prawo w Unii Europejskiej, to jest Komisja Europejska, która jest de facto przez nikogo nie kontrolowana. I tak potrzebujemy reformy, potrzebujemy powrotu do naszych wartości, o których tak często mówicie. Tylko że Unia Europejska nie jest ich kustoszem. Ich kustoszem są narody europejskie. Najlepszą drogą będzie ograniczenie władzy Komisji Europejskiej bądź jej całkowita likwidacja.

interventions.speaker_label: Sandro Gozi, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Europe must become independent. To achieve this, a true European defence is no longer a choice; it is an emergency.

But arms alone will not secure Europe's future. Without political and democratic unity, there can be no European power. That is why new European governance and also Treaty revisions are now indispensable. We need a new transnational coalition, cross-party, across institutions, uniting leaders, pro-European forces and citizens across the continent. So my question is whether the Commissioner and the Minister are ready to join this coalition.

We stand for a Europe of political freedom, a Europe where those ready to move forward are no longer held hostage by national vetoes. Without flexibility, we would still be waiting for the single currency. The moment has come to build up a new political union within the current Union. A Union finally fit for the global challenges. History will not wait. Europe must choose: power, unity and action – or decline. There is no more time for hesitation.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, there is a man living in a cave. He has a piece of paper saying this is his cave and that he has sovereignty. But what will he do when people enter his cave and threaten to kick him out? Europeans don't want a sovereign cave. They understand real sovereignty is only achieved when you can actually shape your surroundings.

This debate is about the EU's institutional response to global challenges. That's the understatement of the year! Europe is under attack and the institutional response is zero. No Treaty change, no extra democracy, and we remain paralysed. Meanwhile, Trump, Putin, Xi and the tech oligarchs have one thing in common: they are all afraid of a united Europe, so they are trying to destroy us. And the far right nationalists in this parliament are helping them do it.

But what do we want? Nine out of ten Europeans want a more united Europe. How? Decide faster without vetoes. Defend ourselves with a European army. Elect a European Government that answers to all Europeans. The European moment is now. National leaders: losers have excuses, winners have a plan. So climb out of your caves and make a plan. If you care so much about sovereignty, make us sovereign. The only way to do it is together. From Portugal to Ukraine, let's create the United States of Europe!

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, Monsieur le Commissaire, l’Europe est confrontée à un environnement géopolitique de plus en plus brutal. Dans ce contexte, débattre des capacités d’action de l’Union dans le cadre institutionnel est important. Mais ce débat ne doit pas être confisqué par les technocrates. C’est la première chose. Parce qu’il ne s’agit pas seulement de savoir comment l’Union peut décider plus vite, mais de savoir ce qu’elle décide, pour qui elle le décide et au service de quel projet politique. Et disons-le clairement, votre Europe, Monsieur le Commissaire, vous qui n’écoutez pas, celle de la concurrence libre et non faussée, celle du marché au service des industriels, celle des droits sociaux considérés comme des obstacles, est aux antipodes de notre Europe, celle du partage des richesses, des droits fondamentaux, de la justice sociale.

Pas de faux débat entre nous. Oui, l’Union doit pouvoir agir plus vite face aux crises internationales, aux ingérences étrangères, aux menaces contre la démocratie, mais pas au prix d’un affaiblissement du contrôle démocratique des droits fondamentaux et de l'imposition de plus en plus de politiques libérales.

Si la majorité qualifiée peut permettre d’obtenir des avancées sociales, alors débattons-en. Mais permettez-moi, dans la configuration actuelle de l’Union, d’en douter fortement. En attendant, nous ne voulons pas d’une remise en cause générale de l’unanimité sur tous les sujets. Les choix les plus sensibles, par exemple en matière de politique étrangère, doivent rester politiquement assumés par les États et démocratiquement contrôlés par les peuples.

La même exigence vaut pour l’élargissement, qui ne sera un succès qu’en étant au service des peuples, de l’amélioration des conditions de vie de toutes et tous, pas pour devenir un outil de concurrence généralisée, de dumping social ou de révision à la baisse des standards européens. Cela veut dire pas d’élargissement à n’importe quel prix, pas d’élargissement qui organise l’exploitation des travailleurs, qui affaiblisse les droits syndicaux, la négociation collective, la santé et la sécurité au travail ou les services publics. L’accueil de nouveaux États ne doit se faire qu’autour d’un socle social ambitieux. En un mot: pas de puissance européenne sans justice sociale, pas d’élargissement sans projet social ambitieux, pas d’Europe forte sans droits fondamentaux.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, history teaches us something important: political systems tend to become more bureaucratic when confidence in their political leadership dwindles. Once democratic trust declines, institutions attempt to compensate through procedures, frameworks and mechanisms. Bureaucracy, however, must not ever replace legitimacy. As Hannah Arendt warned, bureaucracy easily becomes the rule of nobody, a system in which decisions are made everywhere, while responsibility is nowhere to be found.

An EU without the veto right of Member States would slide down a very dangerous slippery slope, which we are actually seeing already. A Union that struggles to build democratic consent falls back on permanent crisis, government governance and an ever-increasing institutional expansion, while gradually hacking away at the very roots on which it rests – the sovereignty of its Member States.

But Europe does not need a permanent machinery of governance, nor does it need a foreign policy detached from its nations and peoples. It needs democratic legitimacy, and it needs accountability, and it needs leaders capable of building consensus between sovereign nations. Because once unanimity disappears, the EU ceases to be a union of equal nations, cooperating freely. It becomes something fundamentally different, a union subjecting sovereign nations to its rule – a foreign rule. History has seen such systems before – Rome, the Soviet Union. Hit the books, read up on it and draw the lessons.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, arvoisa komissaari, on aika aikuistua. Putin käy rikollista hyökkäyssotaa ja sabotoi Eurooppaa aktiivisesti. Trump horjuttaa transatlanttista liittoa tietoisesti, eikä suhteeseen voi enää täysin luottaa. Kiina käy geoekonomista kamppailua ja vyöryttää meille tuotteitaan.
Eurooppa on näiden voimien puristuksessa, samoin meidän tulevaisuutemme, eikä meillä ole varaa jatkaa geopoliittista ja geoekonomista murrosikäämme liian pitkään.

EU:n strategista autonomiaa on vahvistettava nyt. Meidän on rakennettava uskottava pelote, vahva puolustusteollisuus ja oma taloudellinen selkäranka. Meidän on oltava innovatiivisia uusien käytäntöjen ja perussopimuksien tulkintojen kanssa. Eriytyvä integraatio, puolustus ja 42 artiklan 7 kohdan uudelleentulkinta ovat asioita, joihin me voimme ryhtyä.
Putinin julmuus ja Trumpin itsekeskeisyys pakottavat Eurooppaa kasvamaan. EU:n institutionaalinen vastaus globaaleihin haasteisiin on meidän kypsyyskokeemme, eikä tätä koetta voi enää lykätä.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Erich Kästner hat mal gesagt: Es gibt nichts Gutes, außer man tut es. Und ich glaube, die Bürgerinnen und Bürger spüren, dass die EU derzeit sehr schwach aufgestellt ist in der Welt gegenüber Trump, Putin und anderen. Aber sie spüren auch, dass Europa eigentlich die Kraft hätte, dass es eigentlich die Möglichkeit hätte zur Stärke und zu mehr Handlungsfähigkeit. Aber, und das ist ein dickes Aber, es fehlt an Mut. Und leider muss ich sagen, es fehlt Europa auch an Selbstbewusstsein. Dabei ist der europäische Moment jetzt. Der ist nicht morgen. Und er ist auch nicht übermorgen. Und wir diskutieren, sorry, Passerelle, Vertragsänderungen seit mehreren Legislaturperioden. Aber, um zurück zu Kästner zu kommen, wir tun nichts.

Und deshalb erwarten wir von der Kommission schon mehr Unterstützung, mehr Initiativen und hier nicht weiter so zu zaudern. Denn wir hören die Worte, aber wir sehen die Taten nicht. Wir erwarten vom Rat auch tatsächlich nicht einfach business as usual – denn was Sie beschrieben haben, ist ja nichts anderes –, sondern wirklich auch Schritte und Mut zu Reformen. Ich finde es gut, dass Sie die Erweiterung genannt haben. Aber dann auch mit Konzepten zu kommen. Und an all die, die sagen, ach, nur die Einstimmigkeit: Wir haben doch gesehen, zu welchen wirklichen Herausforderungen es kommt, wenn Einzelne alles blockieren können in einem Moment, wo Europa geeint handeln muss. Und deshalb ist es wichtig, diese Veto-Optionen für Blockierer und deren Trittbrettfahrer zu beenden.

Europa kann mehr und es kann seine Bürgerinnen zusammen besser schützen. Aber, um noch einmal mit Schuman zu reden, ohne schöpferische Anstrengungen, die der Größe der Bedrohungen entsprechen, kann Europa nicht aus seiner Dauerkrise kommen. Und deshalb – mehr Mut und mehr Selbstbewusstsein.

interventions.speaker_label: Damian Boeselager (Verts/ALE), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“.
interventions.speaker_process_in_transcript: Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“

paragraphs.text: Frau Bischoff, erst mal wollte ich mich bedanken, weil Sie sich im letzten Mandat und auch in diesem für die Veränderungen der europäischen Verträge so stark einsetzen.

Ich frage mich aber trotzdem: Wir haben als Europäisches Parlament schon Vertragsveränderungen verlangt. Wir haben Artikel 48 ausgelöst. Es ist eigentlich gar keine Wahl mehr, ob der Rat, ob die Regierungschefs sich zusammensetzen und tatsächlich darüber abstimmen, dass wir diese Verträge verändern oder eben nicht. Also, ist es nicht das große Versagen des Rates, dass er eigentlich gerade vertragsbrüchig ist, weil er eben nicht darüber abstimmt, ob wir die Verträge öffnen?
Und was muss in Deutschland noch passieren, damit die Bundesregierung das auch versteht?

paragraphs.text: Ich habe das ja beschrieben: Wir haben es mit einem Aussitzen zu tun im Rat. Deshalb ist es wirklich auch die Verantwortung des Rates, und zwar auch der Staats- und Regierungschefs, dass sie dafür, dass Europa im Moment nicht handlungsfähig ist, dass es so eine schwache Rolle abgibt, auch die Verantwortung übernehmen.

Wir plädieren ja seit Langem dafür, dass sie endlich die Vorschläge aufgreifen und zumindest mal diskutieren – selbst dazu ist es nicht gekommen. Wir hatten in Deutschland Initiativen – Deutschland und Frankreich zusammen – für Vertragsänderungen, und ich hoffe, dass es auch weiter neue Vorschläge der jetzigen Regierung gibt.

paragraphs.text: Elnök Úr! Itt ma már lassan sport lett abból, hogy hogyan lehet észrevétlenül újabb és újabb hatásköröket központosítani. Mindezt persze mindig a jól ismert és hangzatos jelszavakkal: több Európa, nagyobb hatékonyság az közös uniós érdek. A végeredmény azonban ugyanaz, kevesebb nemzeti mozgástér, több központi irányítás. Jean-Claude Juncker politikai Bizottsága után ma már geopolitikai Bizottságról beszélünk, de a lényeg nem változott. Egyre több hatalom koncentrálódik az európai intézményeknél, és a Biztos Úr pedig politikai iránymutatást emleget.

A szerződéseink szerint a Bizottság a szerződések őre, nem pedig kormány. A nemzeteknek van kormánya. A migráció és a szólásszabadság ügye is megmutatta, Európának józan észre, tiszteletre és erős nemzetállamokra van szüksége. Az együttműködés igen, a központosítás nem, csak ez lehet sikeres kormányzás menete.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'Europa deve smettere di dare l'impressione di essere forte solo nei documenti e debole nella realtà.

Mentre Stati Uniti e Cina decidono, investono e proteggono i propri cittadini, noi continuiamo a perderci tra burocrazia, vincoli e lentezze. E intanto le famiglie europee fanno i conti con bollette sempre più pesanti, imprese in difficoltà e stipendi che valgono sempre di meno.

Noi siamo favorevoli a una difesa europea più forte, perché il mondo di oggi è instabile e la sicurezza conta, ma non possiamo accettare che l'Europa trovi soldi e flessibilità solo per le armi, mentre per aiutare famiglie e imprese sull'energia risponde sempre di no. Perché, senza energia accessibile, non c'è lavoro, non c'è industria e non c'è futuro.
Il governo Meloni sta dicendo una cosa semplice e concreta: prima vengono i cittadini europei, prima vengono le famiglie, prima viene il diritto di vivere e lavorare con dignità.

L'Europa deve avere il coraggio di tornare dalla parte della sua gente, perché, se i cittadini iniziano a sentirsi soli, abbandonati e ascoltati solo quando devono fare sacrifici, allora il problema non sono gli europei, il problema è questa Europa.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, what a lively debate. I heard very good interventions. The first one, of course, from my colleague Sandro Gozi and then from Van Lanschot. Very good. I also heard some interventions which I didn't like. I don't know where to look, but it was more on that side.
(The speaker gestured to the right)

I think colleagues Sandro and Van Lanschot, you were right. It is the moment now. Europe has to deliver – and we're not delivering: we are always too little, too late, too slow, not big enough. The time has come to renew Europe. Renew Europe, reform Europe! And we know what we have to do. Because that is also what our citizens ask; our citizens said deliver.

So we have to abolish unanimity, make Europe strong and united again. And then last week we had the child born: we have the working group on a European army, here in this House. So for me, I just came back from Africa. There there is a lion, President, a lion. Let's have the political courage of a lion and decide on the European army.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, when we as Europeans last discussed how the European Union should function was 25 years ago. It was a very different world. It was a world where we could still entrust our lives to the Americans, where democracy, social market economy, freedoms were still spreading in this world.

Well, we live in a different world now. We have seen since, for example, a head of state offer his veto to our adversaries, to wield the veto at the negotiation table on behalf of Vladimir Putin. In this situation, citizens are realising that we need to change the European Union. We have never had such majorities for changing the European Union, for working closer together.

But also, we have never had such weak answers to that from the governments and from the heads of state. We have adopted Treaty change proposals and you don't even discuss it with us. You can dismiss these proposals, you can qualify them as bad ideas, but at least sit down and discuss these proposals with us – how to make Europe stronger.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, é preciso decidir regras fiscais por maioria qualificada para acabar com os Estados offshore? É preciso decidir mínimos sociais, laborais e ambientais para impedir a corrida para o fundo? É preciso projetos de cooperação entre os Estados-Membros? Vamos a isso.

Precisamos de uma União que dê mais valor aos direitos do que aos mercados, que proteja mais o planeta do que os lucros, que lute mais pela paz, em vez de ficar a ver guerras ou a querer criar mais exércitos. Mas, quando debatemos a governação da União Europeia, vamos falar do concreto, porque, para alguns, é sempre mais poder centralizado e, para os mais fortes, o argumento é que vai mudando.

Agora, são as emergências. As emergências são reais: custo de vida, habitação, saúde, clima, guerra. Mas é preciso agilizar processos de decisão para algum dos objetivos concretos da vida das pessoas, porque aquilo de que não precisamos de certeza é de uma espécie de estado de sítio, onde tudo se impõe, tudo se centraliza e nada se escrutina.
Responder às emergências? Sim. Usá-las para subtrair decisões à democracia? Não. A história já provou que esse é o pior dos caminhos.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, byla nabídnuta otázka: Co může dělat správa Evropské unie pod tlakem globálních výzev? Jak má reagovat? Je to projev bezradnosti. Půjdeme-li ke kořenu problému, pak je jasné, že ve struktuře řízení, nezmění-li se tato struktura – a ona se změnit nemůže, protože je zakódována ve Smlouvě o Evropské unii a ve Smlouvě o fungování Evropské unie –, nemůžeme očekávat náležitou reakci na globální výzvy.

V centru moci je Evropská komise, tedy sbor nikým nevolených úředníků, v jehož čele je druhé období předsedkyně, která již na začátku svého působení zvolila jako stěžejní projekt Green Deal, který hrubě poškozuje hospodářství, a tím sociální situaci občanů v Evropské unii. Dalšími klíčovými projekty jsou podpora imigrace, kontrola nad občany, korupce prostřednictvím dotací, které vedou k růstu byrokracie. Následuje sebedestruktivní zahraniční politika a podpora války na Ukrajině a militarizace směřující k vyvolání válečného konfliktu. Vraťme se k realitě!

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, dragi colegi, cred că este foarte posibil ca această discuție să rămână în istoria dezbaterilor din Parlamentul European, deoarece observ că în germene aici avem de-a face cu în sfârșit, devoalarea planurilor dumneavoastră.

Demult am spus că se dorește federalizarea Europei și renunțarea la principiul „Unitate în diversitate”, căci altfel cum să fie federalizarea dacă nu să renunțăm la tradițiile, la obiceiurile noastre, la religie și la tot ce înseamnă identitate națională.

Acum aud de reforme în tratate, aud de schimbarea tratatelor. Foarte bine, schimbați-le, dar schimbați-le pentru suveranitatea statelor care compun această Uniune Europeană. Pentru că, spunea colegul care a inițiat această întrebare orală, nicio țară nu poate fi independentă în vreun fel sau altul. Vă contrazic, domnule, România a fost independentă energetic și v-ați ocupat cu Green deal-ul să ne închideți minele, să ne închideți termocentralele, să ne plece oamenii în pribegie prin Uniunea Europeană sau în alte state, astfel încât să nu mai fim independenți energetic.
