paragraphs.text: Has the war that has been started helped the oppressed Iranians? Well, we can clearly see since the end of January, when it started, that the situation for the Iranian people has actually gotten worse because of the military action. So that's not helping either. We need to have a diplomatic solution. I mean, it's impossible to erase Iran from the ground, and it's not our intention, because the people of Iran, with their culture, deserve a chance. And we use the tools that are in our toolbox. So we are trying to have the diplomatic results. In the end, there has to be a diplomatic solution because the war is just bringing more chaos to not only the Iranians, but everybody because of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. We see the rise of the energy prices, that everybody is feeling. We see the fertilisers that are not coming through – 54 % of fertilisers going to Sudan, for example, are coming via the Strait of Hormuz. So if they don't have the fertilisers this year, there's going to be famine next year. Is it better because of this war, in the region? I will put the question mark there.

Ampak problem je, da imajo številni evropski državljanke in državljani občutek, da Bruselj postaja bolj utrujen od vprašanj o Gazi, kot pa od lastne politične nemoči. Zato vas sprašujem: če verjamete, da je treba politično vplivati celo na talibane, zakaj ta ista logika izgine pri Benjaminu Netanjahuju? Se pravi, kje je danes tista dejanska rdeča črta Evropske unije? Ali pa vaša? Zato, ker posledic tega, da imamo vse te črte nekako pomešane, ne čuti več samo Gaza, čuti jih vsa regija in v bistvu tudi vedno bolj Evropa.

paragraphs.text: When the Assad regime fell, we actually decided that we should give Syria a chance. We had meetings in Jordan; we had meetings in Saudi Arabia with all the regional partners, as well as the international actors, like the European Union, like the United States, to really give Syria a chance, because this means also more stability for the region.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Калас, в Европейския съюз има държави, които казват „да“ още преди да са чули какво ги питат от Вашингтон. Този факт бе потвърден от Марко Рубио, който за съжаление посочи и моята държава България сред тези страни. Пак със съжаление трябва да допълня, че в Европа има и други правителства, подчинени на Вашингтон, а ръководството на Европейския съюз също не показва, че е склонно да води независима от Съединените щати политика. Да, в момента Вие демонстрирате някакво недоволство срещу Доналд Тръмп, но това е недоволство срещу сегашния президент. Ако във Вашингтон управлява друг президент, например Камала Харис, то тогава брюкселският елит отново ще се превърне в „пудела“ на Съединените щати.

paragraphs.text: I understand all the points you have made about trade and the Member States, and I think everybody will continue to campaign for a suspension of the association. But in the meantime, we can actually implement the existing law.

As you know, settlement goods are treated differently to goods that are made in Israel. They are subject of a tariff. I asked the EU delegation in Palestine to estimate the value of trade between the settlements and the European Union, and he told me it was EUR 50 million.

However, we are all very aware of a widespread practice of mislabelling, so that what is presented as settlement goods is in fact made in Israel. The extent of this mislabelling is estimated to be up to 90 % in certain goods.

Therefore, what I am asking you to do, HR/VP, is to look at this whole question, find out what the real volume of trade is, look at the rules of origin, and explore the question of whether or not we can properly stand over the labelling of goods that are said to be from Israel, but are most likely to be from the settlements.

paragraphs.text: Thank you for your question and sorry for all those who did not get to have a question. I tried to answer shortly so you all have the possibility, but an hour is an hour.

On the trade with settlements, we have really looked into this and, of course, it is not entirely my remit, but our trade people have also looked into this. We have the numbers that, since 2015, the percentage of the trade from the settlements is around 0.5 %.

Also the point that you made on the labelling, this has been raised by the Member States. The problem is – and we looked into this – that it is very hard to actually see how we could prevent this because the circumvention via exports from Israel is difficult to prevent if we do not have the suspension of the trade with Israel as a whole, because we do not have mechanisms to really go after.

Yes, it is true that if we start to read the labels and see the addresses where it is coming from, but it is a lot of work considering that it does not have that impact. That is the assessment currently on the table.

interventions.speaker_label: Kaja Kallas, Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Europe faces the most dangerous security environment since the end of the Cold War. I see the main challenges for European security today in the deterioration of the threat environment and our capability to act on that.

First, on the threat environment. Russia is gearing up for long-term confrontation with the West. Whether Putin dares to test European defences is really dependent on us. Deterrence only works when it is credible. Showing weakness only invites aggression. Moscow spends around 8 % of its GDP on military. It has shifted to a war economy – basically, tanks, missiles, artillery are pretty much everything that Russia is producing right now.

European intelligence services and military officials are clear eyed when it comes to Russia – that Russia's endgame is not only Ukraine; it is a threat to whole of Europe. We all know that Russia wants to achieve this. Many of our national intelligence agencies believe that Russia could test the EU's defence readiness within the next three to five years. Already today we see an increase of airspace violations, cyberattacks, sabotage against critical infrastructure and widespread disinformation campaigns. It is clear that Russia will remain a long-term threat. And Russia is not acting alone – countries like Iran and North Korea are actively undermining European security.

The second challenge concerns transatlantic relations. Since the end of the Second World War, the United States has been the guarantor of European security. Tens of thousands of American troops are currently stationed in Europe. The US military footprint in Europe is the major contributor to NATO's deterrence and defence.

But Washington's geopolitical priorities are shifting. We have known this already for a while. It was anticipated that the US might withdraw troops from Europe, because Washington is increasingly shifting its focus towards the Indo-Pacific and the Western Hemisphere. The Pentagon has now halted planned deployments of American troops to Poland and Germany. These announcements are part of this broader trend, but NATO deterrence remains intact. And NATO will continue to maintain a strong presence on its eastern flank, because now is not the time to look weak. The presence of American soldiers in Europe is in our interest, but it's also in the US's interest.

The message is clear: Europe must take greater responsibility for its own defence. To keep our countries safe, we must continue to strengthen European defence readiness, and this means increasing defence spending, closing capability gaps and scaling up European defence production. All this comes with costs, but deterring aggression is cheaper than fighting a war.
Honourable Members, these challenges are not temporary shocks. They are likely here to stay and they will shape Europe's security for decades to come. So what must Europe do?

First, we must continue to support Ukraine. Ukraine is the first line of European defence. Ukrainians are not only defending their own country, they are also defending Europe and buying Europe time to strengthen its own defences. We need to increase our economic, military and political support to Ukraine. Europe already provides the largest share of assistance, but we need to do more. The European Union is doing the heavy lifting, including the EUR 90 billion loan.

Second, we must strengthen Europe's own military capabilities. Defence spending is increasing across Europe – that is necessary and welcome. But Europe still lacks a number of capabilities, which are often too costly or complex for any single Member State to procure alone. That is what we have to focus on – not only about how much we spend, but whether we spend it wisely. We need to think more European.

Third, Europe must strengthen its defence industry. Money alone does not create security if production cannot keep up. If increased defence spending only leads to longer waiting times and order backlogs, it doesn't work.

Fourth, Europe must deepen and build partnerships with like-minded countries. The more reliable partners Europe has, the stronger and safer Europe becomes. We need stronger cooperation with partners such as the United Kingdom, Canada, Norway and Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

Finally, we must improve Europe's decision-making. Today's security environment moves fast; too often, Europe does not. Europe's reliance on unanimity often prevents action at the speed required. So we need to move on that.

Madam President, honourable Members, the assumptions that have shaped our security for decades no longer hold. Europe must take greater responsibility for its own security, and not sometime in the future – now. We need to be really at this point.
The good news is that Europe has faced historic turning points before, and each time we have emerged stronger and there is no reason we cannot do it again.

interventions.speaker_label: Nicolás Pascual de la Parte, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I think that the point here that is bringing us together is – regardless of what the Americans are deciding in the eastern part of Europe – that the European Union has to accelerate our preparedness 2030. Regardless of what the Americans do, we have to accelerate and speed up. Time is of the essence. And I think that we have no time to lose.

First, we have to decide at what pace we have to develop our technological and industrial base with a European preference. And at the same time, we have to start thinking European and not national. We cannot have 27 national fragmented markets. We need an integrated market for defence. And the European Union for defence means also to have common command and control structures, and that means also an integrated change of command. We need also shared capabilities, and that means joint procurement. And we need, as well, to have the possibility to develop a political will in a unified manner. And that means determination and clear ideas.

We have the instruments there – the political and legal instruments approved last year – whether the new White Paper for defence, the roadmap, and now the Commission is preparing the European strategy for security 2026. Here, we need as well our fast reaction forces with a new level of ambition – a 5 000-strong contingent is not enough. We need much more to beef up this rapid reaction force. And at the end of the day, we have to act united and quickly – again, regardless of what the Americans are deciding concerning their presence in Europe.

interventions.speaker_label: Thijs Reuten, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, dear High Representative, thank you for what you just said, because I agree with what you said.

But to the Member States, I would ask: how much proof do we need that Europe needs to strengthen its own defence and deterrence? Now is the time for bold action: no more incremental improvements. Now is the time for European solutions: we are stronger than the sum of our parts. Now is the time for European confidence: our deterrence gap is not just a matter of capabilities; it is also mentality and doctrine.

Many will say this is a wake-up call. It's not! We have been woken up many times before, but we dozed off again, hitting the snooze button like a complacent teenager relying on daddy to wake him up. Enough of that. Enough!

But I'm talking to the wrong person, because the High Representative and Mr Kubilius are not the problem. We urgently need real progress on the European defence union, including an operational Article 42(7) and a real autonomous European pillar of NATO. Mostly, we need to realise that Ukraine's European integration is a security necessity. Member States, stop holding us back and endangering us all!

But to the Member States, I would ask: how much proof do we need that Europe needs to strengthen its own defence and deterrence? Now is the time for bold action: no more incremental improvements. Now is the time for European solutions: we are stronger than the sum of our parts. Now is the time for European confidence: our deterrence gap is not just a matter of capabilities; it is also mentality and doctrine.

Many will say this is a wake-up call. It's not! We have been woken up many times before, but we dozed off again, hitting the snooze button like a complacent teenager relying on daddy to wake him up. Enough of that. Enough!

But I'm talking to the wrong person, because the High Representative and Mr Kubilius are not the problem. We urgently need real progress on the European defence union, including an operational Article 42(7) and a real autonomous European pillar of NATO. Mostly, we need to realise that Ukraine's European integration is a security necessity. Member States, stop holding us back and endangering us all!

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Haute Représentante, vous l'avez dit, le désengagement américain de l'Europe se poursuivra après le mandat de M. Trump, car l'orientation profonde de Washington est claire: l'Europe n'est plus un théâtre prioritaire pour les États-Unis et les forces armées européennes doivent garantir elles-mêmes la dissuasion conventionnelle sur le continent. À cette redirection de long terme viennent s’ajouter une crise de confiance et une une incertitude dans la relation transatlantique. Or l'incertitude est peut-être le pire ennemi des états-majors et des stratèges.

Dans cette situation, nous avons deux impératifs. D'abord, les États européens doivent être capables de garantir une dissuasion conventionnelle sur le continent, donc accélérer sur la voie de l'autonomie. Mais surtout, la confiance entre alliés du Vieux Continent doit être totale et durable.

C'est pourquoi, alors que l'élection présidentielle française aura lieu dans un an et que mon parti est bien placé pour l'emporter, je souhaite réaffirmer dans cet hémicycle notre position: la France garantira ses engagements sur le flanc est l'Europe, de la Baltique à la mer Noire, en Roumanie comme nation-cadre, en Estonie dans le cadre du bataillon multinational, ou encore dans l'espace aérien des pays baltes.

Chers collègues, le contexte n'invite ni à la panique ni à la dispersion. Donnons-nous les moyens de dissuader quiconque nous menacerait, et cela même si nous devions être seuls. Ce n'est pas un plan B, c'est une question de vie ou de mort.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Pani Komisarz! Pytacie, dlaczego Ameryka wycofuje swoje wojska z Europy? Prezydent Nawrocki prawie rok temu zapewnił obecność amerykańskich żołnierzy w Polsce. Od tego czasu jednak prawie na każdej sesji tego Parlamentu słyszę wulgarną krytykę Ameryki. Wasi politycy dają upust najniższym emocjom codziennie i nawet zorganizowaliście tutaj w Parlamencie wulgarną wystawę obrażającą prezydenta Stanów Zjednoczonych. A premier Tusk pozwolił sobie nawet zakwestionować USA jako sojusznika. No i macie co chcieliście. I co, jesteście z siebie dumni?

Czy to przypadkiem nie wy jako pierwsi proponowaliście, że użyję waszego sformułowania, głodzić finansowo państwa, które was krytykują? Przypomnę: jesteśmy silniejsi, więc zablokujemy Polsce, Węgrom pieniądze, bo nas krytykują, i co? I dzisiaj Ameryka zastosowała wobec was dokładnie te same narzędzia, które wy stosowaliście już od dawna. I jesteście zdziwieni? I teraz tak, tylko, że teraz koszty mogą być znacznie większe, ponieważ możemy stracić konieczną nam pomoc w zdolnościach, których po prostu nie mamy. Wymienię tylko niezależne odstraszanie nuklearne, bombowce strategiczne dalekiego zasięgu, których nie mamy, wywiad strategiczny i rozpoznanie, broń precyzyjna dalekiego zasięgu, to samo jeżeli chodzi o duże lotniskowce czy wielowarstwową obronę przeciwrakietową – to możemy stracić.

A co zyskaliście, pytam? Co? Daliście swój prymitywny upust swoim emocjom, jakieś lajki, bo pokrytykowaliście prezydenta Trumpa w mediach społecznościowych? A co z odpowiedzialnością za bezpieczeństwo 450 mln obywateli Europy? Od lat marnowaliście europejskie pieniądze na politykę gender, nielegalną migrację czy ideologiczną politykę klimatyczną, więc tak naprawdę to was trzeba przerotować, a nie amerykańskich żołnierzy.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Madam Vice-President, colleagues, it is in the interest of Poland, Europe and also the United States itself that American troops remain in Europe and continue to train alongside us. It is also important to note that Poland has for years contributed financially to hosting American soldiers. Dear American Friends, do you really want to send such a signal at a moment when Russia and Belarus are demonstrating their readiness and, since yesterday, are conducting nuclear military exercises? Today's blame game in Europe – we heard an example just a while ago – over who offended or provoked the Americans is a waste of time and energy. All democratic and non‑pro‑Russian forces should stand together. Poland has proven that it is a loyal and reliable ally. Loyal allies expect partnership, predictability and mutual respect. Sadly, I must say today to our American friends, your European ally is disappointed. Let's work together to overcome this crisis.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, I serve as a volunteer in the Latvian armed forces, my wife also serves and our son has joined as well. In Latvia and in our region, this is normal. But Europe as a whole faces one problem that too many politicians avoid saying out loud: we simply do not have enough military personnel.

Our 'plan A' remains NATO and Article 5 and it must stay that way. Every day we train side by side with our allies from Europe and across the Atlantic, and I hope that never changes. But the truth is that Europe simply does not have enough soldiers, enough officers, enough instructors or enough people capable of leading operations independently. Our armies are too small. Without people, there will be no European command centres, no rapid reaction units, no credible European defence union.

The Baltic states, Finland, Germany and others are already showing the way. Military service must return in one form or another: conscription, voluntary systems or a randomised model like we have in Latvia. The form can differ; the principle cannot. Europe needs more people in uniform. And this is not the job of the armed forces – this is the job of politicians.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Wenn die USA ihre Truppenpräsenz in Europa reduzieren wollen, dann müsste die Antwort doch eigentlich lauten: Ja, bitte schön! Ja, Yankee go home! Das hätte man übrigens auch schon vor Jahrzehnten sagen müssen. Doch statt eine eigenständige europäische Sicherheitsarchitektur des Friedens, der Abrüstung und der gemeinsamen Sicherheit mit allen Staaten dieses Kontinents aufzubauen, hielt man fest an dem Militärbündnis NATO. Selbst wenn man dafür sicherheitspolitisch von den USA abhängig war, war man schließlich Nutznießer dieser Ordnung.

Heute reagieren dieselben Kräfte nervös auf die Trump-Administration, die auf der Münchner Sicherheitskonferenz noch Beifall geklatscht haben für Rubios unsägliche Rede von der Verteidigung der westlichen Zivilisation. Doch ihre transatlantische Partnerschaft hat keine Zivilisation gefördert, sondern ihren Machtanspruch mit Gewalt in die Welt getragen. Selbst wenn die europäischen Staaten manchmal nicht Teil der NATO-Kriege waren, waren europäische Basen dafür entscheidend, wie jetzt im Iran.

Deshalb heißt es: Ja, Yankee go home! Und deshalb heißt es: Schließt die US-Militärbasen in Europa und in Deutschland! Wir brauchen nicht die EU-Militärunion, sondern wir brauchen endlich Frieden auf diesem Kontinent, und dafür müssen Sie sich auch einsetzen, Frau Kallas!

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Angela Merkel hat heute hier einen Verdienstorden bekommen. Sie hat fast alles falsch gemacht, aber in einer Sache hatte sie recht: Friedrich Merz kann es nicht.

Deutschland kommt nicht aus der Krise: Die Industrie wandert ab, die Arbeitslosigkeit steigt, die Infrastruktur bröckelt, die Krankenkassen sind pleite, die innere Sicherheit ist verloren und das Sondervermögen für die deutsche Bundeswehr ist wirkungslos verpufft. Aber statt sich um diese Probleme zu kümmern, spielt der Kanzler lieber den Weltpolitiker: Vor Schülern im Sauerland erklärte er, dass die USA im Iran gedemütigt würden. Trump war daraufhin so sauer, dass er den Abzug von 5 000 amerikanischen Soldaten aus der Oberpfalz angekündigt hat.

Deutschland ist nicht verteidigungsfähig – wir wollen das ändern! Das erreichen wir aber nicht, indem wir die eigenen Probleme ignorieren und stattdessen den Amerikanern die Welt erklären. Wir müssen zuerst vor der eigenen Haustür kehren. Wir müssen illegale Migranten abschieben, um unsere Sozialsysteme zu retten. Wir müssen unsere Kernkraftwerke reaktivieren, damit wir unsere Industrie nicht verlieren. Und wir müssen die Bundeswehr besser ausrüsten, damit wir uns auch ohne amerikanische Hilfe verteidigen können. Das wären die Aufgaben für Friedrich Merz. Er will das ja auch, aber wir sehen: Er kann es nicht.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Alta Representante, há políticas que se fazem por palavras e há políticas que se confessam por gestos. E, em matéria de defesa, os gestos não mentem.

A redução da presença militar americana no nosso continente, particularmente da Alemanha ao flanco leste, é prova de uma tendência e não de um acaso. Não cabe, por isso, à Europa lamentar. Temos de respeitar, mas, essencialmente, temos de assumir as nossas responsabilidades.

A Aliança Transatlântica da NATO continua a ser a pedra angular da nossa segurança e defesa, e queremos continuar a sê-lo em pé de igualdade dos dois lados do Atlântico. Mas a parte que nos cabe, essa, ninguém fará por nós. Por isso, investir em capacidades é necessário e é urgente. Investir em pessoas, em recursos humanos, é indispensável. Recrutar, formar, reter e dignificar quem veste a farda — eis o verdadeiro teste de prontidão europeia.

Por isso, vejamos esta decisão como uma grande oportunidade, uma oportunidade de aumentar as nossas capacidades, mas também, essencialmente, de aumentar a nossa soberania em matéria de segurança e defesa. Eu vejo esta proposta como positiva.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, are the Americans still prepared to defend Europe? We keep asking that question, but colleagues, it is the wrong one. The real question is not whether America is ready to defend Europe, but whether Europe is actually ready to defend Europe. Because, let's be honest, American troop reductions should not come as a surprise.

For years, we have known that if NATO is to remain transatlantic, it must first become more European, and that makes sense. We are the second‑biggest economy in the world. We have the strongest social model on the planet, and we should be ready and honestly proud to defend our European values against outside threats.

That is why, together with a cross‑party group of MEPs, we are now calling for a genuine single market of defence at the heart of a real European Defence Union, not as a replacement for NATO, but as the necessary European pillar for a stronger and more equal transatlantic alliance.

So, colleagues, for the love of God, let's stop hyperventilating about every tweet that comes out of the White House and focus instead on our strength, on building our capabilities and on defending our continent – not because of anything Donald Trump says or does, but because the Europeans deserve it.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, vážená paní vysoká představitelko, stažení amerických jednotek z Evropy je studenou sprchou. Buďme ale naprosto upřímní ohledně toho, proč jsme se do této situace dostali. Je to přímý důsledek hluboké diplomatické neschopnosti Bruselu. Po mnoho let se evropská byrokracie nechovala k našemu nejdůležitějšímu bezpečnostnímu partnerovi s respektem, ale s ideologickou arogancí a malicherným moralizováním. Místo budování spolupráce se Brusel posedle soustředil na politické rozdíly, a tím úspěšně odcizil našeho hlavního spojence. Řekněme si nepopiratelnou pravdu – evropská bezpečnost, NATO a Spojené státy jsou zcela neoddělitelné. Skutečná bezpečnost nespočívá ve fantazii o evropské armádě, kterou prosazuje elita, která není schopná ochránit ani naše vnější hranice, ale vyžaduje tvrdý a chladný pragmatismus. Přestaňme s arogantním ukazováním prstem, opusťme federalistické iluze a sjednoťme se s Washingtonem. Je čas na zdravý rozum.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Konkurencja w Europie również na tej sali o to, kto bardziej obrazi Stany Zjednoczone i jej demokratycznie wybranego prezydenta, jest bardzo silna. Ale w tej szkodliwej rywalizacji niewątpliwie w całej Europie wygrywa premier Donald Tusk. Przypomnę, że Tusk bez żadnych dowodów oskarżył prezydenta Trumpa o zdradę stanu. Tak, oskarżył go o wieloletnią współpracę z wrogim wywiadem. Przypomnę, że w USA jest to zbrodnia zagrożona karą śmierci. I nigdy się z tych słów nie wycofał.

Tusk jest premierem Polski, kraju, któremu jak żadnemu innemu w Unii Europejskiej powinno zależeć na jak najlepszych relacjach z naszym najpotężniejszym sojusznikiem. Szczególnie, że jak twierdzi sam Tusk, w tej chwili grozi nam agresja ze strony Rosji. Nic więc dziwnego, że gdy teraz decydują się losy amerykańskiego kontyngentu w Europie, Tusk nie jest w stanie pojechać na negocjacje do Waszyngtonu, on nie jest w stanie nawet zadzwonić do amerykańskiego przywódcy. Lenin nazywał takich jak Tusk pożytecznymi idiotami. Ja w głupotę Tuska po prostu nie wierzę. On robi to z pełną premedytacją. Prawo i Sprawiedliwość udowodniło, że potrafi budować relacje z USA, niezależnie od tego, kto urzęduje w Białym Domu. Czas na powrót do skutecznej dyplomacji.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kallas! Ich komme gerade aus dem Trilog „Defence Omnibus“ und, meine Damen und Herren, ich kann nur sagen – ich kann eigentlich gar nichts sagen, denn von den drei Paketen, die wir verhandelt haben seit gestern, haben wir eins auf den Weg gebracht, weil der Rat sich nach wie vor hinter nationalen Vorrechten versteckt.

Und das steht im Widerspruch zu der Erklärung der Mitgliedstaaten, als sie die Mitgesetzgeber aufforderten, die europäische Verteidigung voranzutreiben. Das ist ein gefährlicher Vorgang, nämlich eine Kluft zwischen den historischen Worten unserer Regierungschefs und ihrer Fähigkeit, diese mit konkreten Maßnahmen umzusetzen.

Das Omnibus-Paket zur Verteidigungsbereitschaft wurde nämlich genau deswegen konzipiert, damit Bürokratie abgebaut wird, Genehmigungsverfahren beschleunigt werden, der Rüstungsindustrie Vorrang eingeräumt wird und Europa dabei geholfen wird, seine Produktionskapazitäten auszubauen.

Meine Damen und Herren, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, wir können uns das Gequatsche zu Hause nicht weiter erlauben! Hier haben wir die Chance, etwas zu ändern, und der Rat muss sich bewegen! Wir als Europäisches Parlament sind bereit dazu! Alles andere ist scheinheilig.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Mr Bielan, Mr Jaki, one cannot build reliable security on unreliable partners. And by now it should be obvious Donald Trump is not reliable. You can flatter him, you can appease him and he will still hit you with tariffs, annexation threats or troop drawdowns. And none of that will make us safer. The alternative, on the other hand, is clear and simple: strengthen our European defence industry; close our capability gaps; support the eastern flank; and finally act as Europeans and not as 27 nervous clients waiting for Trump's mood of the day.

Let us also not forget that America needs Europe too, and US senators know it. There is no credible US deterrence without bases in Europe. There is no American defence industry without European buyers, and there is no American global power without European support. Despite all of this, the Council still shies away, and is blocking every step towards a truly European Defence Union. They are too slow, too national, too late.
Dear colleagues, let us finally unite our efforts to prevent war, not wait for war to unite us.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Haute Représentante, j’entends ici des gens qui pleurnichent un peu parce que les États-Unis retirent quelques milliers de soldats. Pourtant, en réalité, disons-le, ce qu’on voit, c’est que ce sont des gangsters qui partent. Parce que c’était quoi le deal? Soit vous venez me soutenir en Iran en menant une guerre illégale – je sais bien que vous n’avez pas été capable de condamner la guerre illégale des États-Unis et d’Israël contre l’Iran, mais ça reste une violation de la charte des Nations unies –, soit je m’en vais. En gros, il disait: ce sont les Européens qui doivent tuer les écolières en Iran. Eh bien, heureusement qu’on a dit non à cela et qu’ils dégagent.

Deuxièmement, on a des champions qui disent: ben, comme ils partent, alors nous, on doit massivement militariser; on doit suivre le modèle américain. Plus d’armes, moins de pensions, moins d’écoles, moins d’hôpitaux. Mais c’est du n’importe quoi. On a déjà beaucoup plus d’armes que les Russes. Et en plus, on lit tous les jours dans les journaux que les Russes sont en difficulté, qu’ils n’ont plus de chars. Ils n’arrivent même plus à faire le défilé à Moscou. Alors, on n’est pas obligés de choisir. Choisissons une autre voie, la voie de la paix, de la diplomatie. Et pour cela, il y aura une grosse mobilisation à Bruxelles le 14 juin. Je vous invite tous, chers collègues, comme ça vous sortez un peu et vous vous mettez du côté des gens qui se mobilisent pour le welfare, not warfare.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Die Vereinigten Staaten ziehen Truppen ab, die sie im Zuge der Ukrainekrise nach Europa verlegt hatten. Das war politisch angekündigt und daher absehbar.

Wer sich nun sorgt, die USA würden Europa bald ganz im Stich lassen, kann sich beruhigt auf die andere Seite drehen: Großmächte pflegen, ihre Vasallen gelegentlich zittern zu lassen. Aufgeben werden die USA ihren Brückenkopf nach Eurasien aber bestimmt nicht. Der wahre Feind Europas ist nicht die Russische Föderation, sondern der islamische Totalitarismus. Er bedroht die offenen Gesellschaften nicht nur von außen, sondern auch von innen – unterstützt von den linksgrünen Zeloten dieses Parlaments.

Die eigentliche Frage lautet daher nicht, ob Amerika bleibt. Die Frage lautet, ob Europa erwachsen wird. Wer strategische Autonomie predigt, darf nicht zugleich seine sicherheitspolitische Mündigkeit in Washington bestellen. Es passt nicht zusammen, sich rhetorisch von den USA zu emanzipieren, praktisch aber immer neue Waffen bei ihnen zu kaufen.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Man hat den Eindruck, manche in Europa haben mit dem Krieg in der Ukraine vollkommen den Verstand verloren. Sie, Frau Kallas, möchten Russland zerschlagen. Der deutsche CDU-Abgeordnete Kiesewetter will, dass Europa auf die Kapitulation Russlands hinarbeitet. Und Nico Lange von der Münchner Sicherheitskonferenz frohlockt: Ja, man kann Russland besiegen.

Fast scheint es, als wollten einige in Europa den Feldzug ihrer Großväter gen Osten fortsetzen, der durch die deutsche Kapitulation 1945 unterbrochen wurde. Nach ihrem Willen soll der Stellvertreterkrieg der NATO in der Ukraine zum europäischen Krieg gegen Russland werden. Es sind diese Maulhelden, die Europas Sicherheit gefährden und die sich selbst sofort aus dem Staub machen, wenn ihre verbale Saat aufgeht.

Der berühmte Schriftsteller Remarque hat es treffend formuliert: Ich dachte immer, jeder Mensch sei gegen den Krieg, bis ich herausfand, dass es welche gibt, die dafür sind, besonders die, die nicht hingehen müssen.
Hören Sie endlich auf damit, einen Krieg herbeizureden! Die Menschen in Europa wollen Frieden.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, stimați colegi, timp de decenii, parteneriatul dintre SUA și Europa a fost coloana vertebrală a lumii libere. Generații întregi au crescut fără frica războiului, deoarece au știut că dincolo de ocean există un aliat care nu abandonează libertatea atunci când aceasta este amenințată.

Astăzi însă, lumea se schimbă. Dislocarea trupelor americane de pe flancul estic nu este doar o problemă a Europei. Istoria ne-a învățat un adevăr dureros: atunci când democrațiile ezită, agresorii capătă curaj, atunci când aliații se îndoiesc unii de alții, pacea devine fragilă.

Flancul estic nu apără doar România, Polonia sau statele baltice, ci și stabilitatea întregii lumi libere. Prezența americanilor nu este doar o desfășurare strategică de trupe, este dovada că articolul 5 din tratatul NATO nu este doar un text într-un tratat, ci o promisiune vie între națiuni, o necesitate a zilei de astăzi.

Iar în același timp, Europa trebuie să înțeleagă un adevăr: o Europă puternică are obligația de a deveni și o Europă capabilă să se apere într-un parteneriat strâns cu Statele Unite ale Americii. Împreună putem garanta pacea și securitatea lumii.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Nasz największy sojusznik przestał być przewidywalny, a jego pochopne decyzje narażają nasze bezpieczeństwo. Prawica chce przed nim klękać i błagać. My, my musimy być odpowiedzialni i budować własną siłę. Musimy być odważni, a nie tchórzyć tak jak prawica, także ta polska. Chcemy wielkiej, zjednoczonej Europy, nie rozbitego na kawałki kontynentu. Żądamy Europy Wielkiej od Lizbony, przez Berlin, przez Warszawę, aż po niepodległy Kijów. Jako Europa musimy mówić nie tylko siłą argumentów, ale także argumentem siły. Nadszedł czas, abyśmy przestali się bać. To my jesteśmy ojczyzną demokratycznych narodów całego świata.

Dzisiaj rano słuchaliśmy ludzi, którzy mieli odwagę marzyć o zjednoczonym kontynencie i którzy potrafili tę wizję urzeczywistnić. To dzięki takim liderom jak Lech Wałęsa czy Aleksander Kwaśniewski, mój kraj, Polska, mogła dołączyć do Unii Europejskiej i NATO, filarów naszego bezpieczeństwa, wolności i rozwoju.

Apeluję do amerykańskich sojuszników: miejcie odwagę kontynuować partnerstwo, które przez dekady było fundamentem bezpieczeństwa naszego i waszego. Wiedzcie, że my, Europejczycy, jesteśmy lojalni, ale wiedzcie też, że z pewnością nie przestaniemy walczyć o bezpieczny kontynent, Nie będziemy brać wolności za pewnik. Wy, amerykańscy sojusznicy, też nie powinniście.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, the latest US decision to reduce military development and deployments in Europe, including the cancelled troop rotation to Poland and Romania, should be viewed as an opportunity, not a crisis. Since the Obama years, Washington has signalled its strategic shift away from Europe, yet most European countries fail to strengthen their own defence.

It was President Trump's first term that finally forced Europe to take defence seriously and move towards higher spending commitments. While Poland and other countries on the eastern flank have dramatically increased their military capabilities and budgets, too many Western European countries continue to underinvest and delay meaningful defence action.

We must stay committed to NATO and the transatlantic alliance. But friendship with America cannot mean dependency, as the Americans also said. To be strong again, Europe needs to rebuild its own industry, increase ammunition and air defence production, secure its border and achieve energy independence. The message must be clear: to Moscow, that Europe will not be intimidated; to Washington, that we will carry our own fair share; and to our citizens, that peace is protected by strength. Europe must and can stand on its own feet and protect itself.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Donald Trump a raison. Oui, vous avez bien entendu: Donald Trump a raison. Il est temps que l’Europe prenne en charge et assure sa propre défense. C’est bien le moins que nous devons à nos concitoyens: être capables de dissuader une agression extérieure et les défendre si nécessaire. C’est le choix qu’a fait la France depuis 60 ans, celui de l’autonomie stratégique; et c’est celui qu’elle propose à l’Europe depuis près de dix ans.

Malgré tout, Donald Trump se trompe. Au lieu d’aider à la mise en place de la défense européenne, il s’acharne à l’entraver. Pire, il fragilise l’OTAN au moment même où la menace russe n’a jamais été aussi flagrante, et alors même qu’il n’existe à ce jour aucune alliance militaire aussi robuste ni aussi respectée. Mais assez parlé de Donald Trump. Mettons-nous sérieusement au travail pour faire du pilier européen de l’OTAN le cœur du réacteur de l’Alliance et pour arrimer l’Ukraine à la défense de notre continent. C’est notre intérêt, c’est notre urgence. Il n’y a plus une minute à perdre.
Nous avons perdu la certitude que nous pouvons compter demain sur les États-Unis pour nous défendre. Alors, faisons en sorte qu’on doive compter avec l’Europe.

C’est le choix qu’a fait la France depuis 60 ans, celui de l’autonomie stratégique; et c’est celui qu’elle propose à l’Europe depuis près de dix ans.

Malgré tout, Donald Trump se trompe. Au lieu d’aider à la mise en place de la défense européenne, il s’acharne à l’entraver. Pire, il fragilise l’OTAN au moment même où la menace russe n’a jamais été aussi flagrante, et alors même qu’il n’existe à ce jour aucune alliance militaire aussi robuste ni aussi respectée. Mais assez parlé de Donald Trump. Mettons-nous sérieusement au travail pour faire du pilier européen de l’OTAN le cœur du réacteur de l’Alliance et pour arrimer l’Ukraine à la défense de notre continent. C’est notre intérêt, c’est notre urgence. Il n’y a plus une minute à perdre.

Nous avons perdu la certitude que nous pouvons compter demain sur les États-Unis pour nous défendre. Alors, faisons en sorte qu’on doive compter avec l’Europe.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Europe has been blindsided by Trump many times – threatening Greenland, betraying Ukraine. But for once, Trump is just doing what he said he would. The withdrawal of American soldiers from Germany and Poland should not come as a surprise to anyone who has listened to the US in the past years. At this point, I don't even blame Trump. I blame European leaders who are shocked – shocked! – when they should have seen this coming from miles away.

European leaders, when it comes to our security, hope is a bad strategy. Instead, join our network of 40 MEPs acting across party lines to take our security out of American hands and into our own. Let's build the European defence union together. For every 5 000 troops Trump withdraws from Europe, we should replace them with 5 000 of our own.
Bottom line: we need our own European defence, regardless of the latest clown show coming out of Washington. And that, by the way, is also the best way to strengthen the North Atlantic Alliance.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisară, reducerea graduală a prezenței americane trebuie să însemne pentru noi începutul unei noi ere în securitatea noastră. Ce ne spunea înainte doamna Strack-Zimmermann este într-adevăr îngrijorător. Trebuie să facem programele noastre de apărare, propriile programe să le facem ca lumea.

Să luăm câteva exemple: programul SAFE. Programul SAFE deja este plin de controverse în multe țări din Europa. Riscă să devină un mecanism de îndatorare fără integrare industrială reală. A doua problemă: tensiunea dintre urgența militară și transparența democratică. Procedurile accelerate din SAFE țin să elimine controlul parlamentar în acest moment. A treia controversă: dezechilibre industriale între statele membre. Statele mari se vor dezvolta mai mult, statele mai mici vor rămâne dependente. A patra problemă este lipsa coordonării europene și este cea mai mare problemă. Fiecare stat cumpără separat, negociază separat și stabilește priorități diferite.
Și, în fine, avem și dependența de furnizorii externi, care se va vedea foarte bine. Ne trebuie o arhitectură strategică suficient de clară și pentru SAFE.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowni Państwo! Symboliczne że w piątym roku wojny w Ukrainie europejskie odznaczenie za zasługi przyznano kanclerz Angeli Merkel, promotorce Nord Stream i współpracy z Władimirem Putinem. Jak widać Unia Europejska wciąż nie potrafi wyciągać wniosków z historii najnowszej. Na szczęście państwa nordyckie, bałtyckie czy Polska już dekadę temu miały trzeźwą ocenę sytuacji. Jako wiceminister obrony w rządzie Prawa i Sprawiedliwości aktywnie uczestniczyłem w rozwoju współpracy strategicznej z USA. Nadaliśmy nowy impuls relacjom transatlantyckim. Przyjęliśmy tysiące amerykańskich żołnierzy. Utworzyliśmy nowe struktury. Zainwestowaliśmy setki milionów euro w infrastrukturę.

Dzisiaj trzeba podkreślić: wzmacniając wschodnią flankę NATO i obecność amerykańską w regionie, zabezpieczaliśmy trwałość całego europejskiego projektu. Dlatego w ostatnim czasie z rosnącym niepokojem przysłuchuję się europejskiej debacie o budowie bezpieczeństwa w kontrze do USA, której praktycznym wyrazem jest ograniczenie współpracy z naszym najważniejszym militarnym partnerem. Skutkuje to rosnącym negatywnym nastawieniem Waszyngtonu do współpracy z Europą. Biorąc powyższe pod uwagę, proponuję, by kolejna debata dotyczyła odbudowy współpracy transatlantyckiej z udziałem sekretarza generalnego NATO.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiama posėdžio Pirmininke, gerbiama aukštoji atstove užsienio politikai ir saugumui, gerbiami kolegos. Nors Europa jau prisiėmė ilgalaikius įsipareigojimus didinti savo investicijas į saugumą ir gynybą, JAV karinis buvimas Europoje netapo ir tikrai netaps perteklinis. Teroristinis Kremliaus režimas pripažįsta ir supranta tik vieną kalbą, t. y. jėgą ir stiprumą. Todėl Europos Sąjungos teritorijoje, ypač Europos Sąjungos rytiniame flange, karinių pajėgų ir karinės technikos tiesiog negali mažėti.

Pastaruoju metu Rusija stiprina informacinių atakų, vykdomų prieš ypač Baltijos valstybes, frontą, taip, tikėtina, ruošdama dirvą naujoms ir labai pavojingoms provokacijoms. Europos Sąjunga gali ir turi dėti maksimalias pastangas, siekdama išlaikyti strateginį JAV karinį buvimą Europoje, ypač ties rytinėmis sienomis, kur dronų, kibernetinių atakų ir nelegalios migracijos grėsmės pačios didžiausios. Kviečiu Europos Sąjungą ir valstybes nares rasti būdus Europos Sąjungai ir JAV lygiavertei partnerystei stiprinti.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Madam High Representative, dear colleagues, the US decision to stop the rotation of US army brigade to Poland became a surprise. Typically for the Trump administration, it seemed to be a surprise even to the US army and the Congress. However, we have been warned about the reduction of the US forces in Europe ever since President Obama's time. So we had ample time to prepare, but failed to do so.

So what to do now? Well, let's not cry over the spilt milk. Let's finally accept the fact of the US forces' withdrawal from Europe. This trend will most probably continue even after Trump leaves office. European military forces of NATO and EU countries number around 1.5 million soldiers, with around 1 million in reserves. US combat forces represent only around 5 % of the European combat power. Europe can defend itself without the United States.

Let us concentrate on getting our forces combat ready, reinforce them, and build independent European joint capabilities to enable our defence. It will take years, but the sooner and faster we act, the sooner it will be ready. Meanwhile, let's integrate the strongest army in Europe – the Ukrainian armed forces – into European defence through EU and NATO membership as soon as possible. Slava Ukraini!

Granice na Wschodzie są tak samo ważne jak granice na południu. Każdy kilometr europejskiej granicy wymaga absolutnej ochrony i solidarności całej Unii. Dlatego informacje o możliwej redukcji wojsk amerykańskich w Polsce nie są wyłącznie problemem Polski. To sprawa bezpieczeństwa całej Europy.

Ale kiedy słyszę o wczorajszych ćwiczeniach wojskowych z użyciem broni jądrowej na Białorusi, zadaję sobie pytanie: czy my jako Europa mamy się temu tylko przyglądać? Czy po prostu powinniśmy zacząć działać?

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Vice-President, Americans need Europeans; Europeans need Americans. So it's both ways. Americans are not only here to defend Europe, but also for US power in Europe, in the Middle East and in North Africa. Europe is the largest market for American weapons. That should change.

I recently visited Ramstein and the FBI in Washington, and I found out that American officials say that we need each other and we should keep on working together. The problem is the US President, because he doesn't like an independent, strong Europe. So that means we have to get even stronger.

Regardless of what the Americans decide, we Europeans should take full responsibility for our own defence. A unified European army is the only right way in the medium term. In the short term, we need to coordinate within the EU and cooperate with like-minded countries around the world. All European governments should understand that.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, Vice-President of the Commission, for decades, the transatlantic alliance has been the foundation of Europe's security. The presence of the United States in Europe, especially on NATO's eastern flank, has been essential for our protection.

Recent Washington decisions shows the shift in American strategic priorities. Europe must take responsibility for its own defence. We need higher defence spending, stronger European defence industry. This is vital because Russia continues its war against Ukraine, carries out cyberattacks and uses hybrid tools to destabilise our societies.

The eastern border is the front line of the European and transatlantic security. Any reduction in American presence of the eastern flank must be matched by stronger European capability. Europe's message is clear: transatlantic unity remains our strength and Europe is ready to carry more weight to protect it.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Vice‑President of the Commission, colleagues, for over 70 years the Transatlantic Alliance was the backbone of global security. The U.S. decision to reduce troop deployment in Europe is regretful and irresponsible. The EU is strong in our soft power globally, but in defence not. However, we cannot outsource our security forever. Europe must now take responsibility for its own defence. That means real budgetary capabilities, real EU industry, real joint procurement mechanisms, personal equipment and also our solidarity in our eastern European Union flank. And it means our unwavering support to Ukraine. In a world this interconnected, any invasion will affect everyone. In the Union of 27, all 27 will suffer and bear the consequences. Every one would be affected. It is naive to think that being far from the eastern flank protects you from aggression. We want a strong EU defence and security union. We want a strong transatlantic partnership, but we cannot be held hostage to the mood of any single president. Europe will not be abandoned. Europe will defend itself.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, viime viikonloppuna Suomessa vietettiin kaatuneiden muistopäivää. Me tiedämme, mikä on vapauden ja itsenäisyyden hinta. Se on mittaamaton.

Jokainen EU:n jäsenmaa on vastuussa unionin tulevaisuudesta ja turvallisuudesta. Itäiset rajamaat ja jokainen, joka näkee, mitä tapahtuu Venäjän hyökkäyssodan myötä Ukrainassa, tietävät, että pyrkimys eroon strategisista riippuvuuksista on perusta vakaalle tulevaisuudelle. Olipa kyse kiinalaisista komponenteista tai yhdysvaltalaisista joukoista, emme voi olla tämän mantereen turvallisuuden osalta riippuvaisia muista kuin itsestämme. Samalla on löydyttävä tahtoa siihen, että jokainen jäsenmaa tekee osansa.
Tietysti on hyvä pyrkiä ylläpitämään transatlanttista yhteistyötä, mutta ei sellaisella hinnalla, joka vie turvallisuutemme ja itsenäisyytemme avaimet pois omista käsistämme.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Zawrócenie czterech tysięcy żołnierzy. Przyjęcie przestępcy ściganego przez polskie sądy. Polska nie zasłużyła na takie traktowanie, panie Trump. Obywatele Polski walczyli w Iraku i w Afganistanie i ginęli tam. Wydajemy ponad 5% na zbrojenia. Kupujemy waszą broń i budujemy na waszej technologii elektrownię atomową w Polsce. Wierzę, że nastąpi refleksja, bo zjednoczona Europa potrzebuje silnych Stanów Zjednoczonych. Jednak polityka to nie jest kwestia wiary tylko działań. Europa musi się głęboko zreformować. Europa musi być jeszcze silniejsza. To nie jest kwestia wyboru. To jest konieczność.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora Kallas, para que la Unión Europea responda ante la retirada de efectivos militares por parte de los Estados Unidos en el este de Europa, la condición necesaria es que la Unión Europea tenga una voz propia, digna de ser escuchada y respetada.

Y eso es muy difícil cuando afronta la crítica del doble rasero: enfrentada con Rusia por su agresión contra Ucrania, pero incapaz de decir una palabra audible sobre el genocidio perpetrado por Israel en Gaza, o su agresión contra el Líbano, o la acción militar, ilegal también, de los Estados Unidos en Irán —régimen execrable, pero al que no se puede bombardear ilegalmente sin más—.
Y, por supuesto, el doble rasero se exaspera cuando la Comisión Europea invita a los talibanes a negociar retornos de personas refugiadas procedentes de Afganistán en territorio europeo.
Por tanto, lo principal es que la Unión Europea madure deprisa, tenga voluntad de ser y disponga de los recursos necesarios para ser globalmente relevante, también en defensa y seguridad.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, dio Trumpove politike je kratkotrajan, proći će nakon njegovog odlaska, ali dio je strukturne naravi i ostat će nakon njegovog odlaska.

Što će proći? Proći će retorika koja, i određene mjere kao ove koje tretiraju Europu više kao neprijatelja nego kao saveznika, ali šta će ostati, ostat će da fokus SAD-a više nije na Europu, više, sada je fokus na Indo-pacifik i stoga Europa mora preuzeti sama odgovornost za vlastitu sigurnost. To ne znači odustati od NATO-a, ali to znači unutar NATO-a izgraditi europski stup. To znači da na taj način, s europskom obrambenom politikom, NATO će biti jači i moći će i dalje biti uvjerljiva snaga za odvraćanje ne samo ruske prijetnje, nego bilo koje druge prijetnje i na taj način osigurati mir u Europi.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária Kaja Kallas, a presença militar norte-americana em alguns países europeus não corresponde a nenhuma preocupação com a segurança e a defesa desses países — corresponde aos interesses norte-americanos e à forma como cada administração norte-americana interpreta em cada momento os interesses económicos, políticos e geoestratégicos que justificam essa presença militar.

E, portanto, a saída de militares americanos de países europeus não deve servir nem para disputas de outros países por essa presença militar, nem como pretexto para a militarização da União Europeia, para a acentuação da política de confrontação e de guerra a partir das orientações da União Europeia contra a sua tradução nacional.

Pelo contrário, essa saída de militares norte-americanos dos países europeus onde estão deve significar uma oportunidade para a desmilitarização das relações internacionais, para a promoção de uma política de paz, de segurança coletiva, de cooperação, de exigência de respeito pelo direito internacional e pela Carta das Nações Unidas. Esse deve ser o sentido em que devemos caminhar.

paragraphs.text: Thank you, honourable Members, for this debate. I think that the majority view is that we need to do more for our defence. We have heard U.S. pleas, loud and clear, that Europe should take up European security. So we are working on that. It is also clear that the U.S. military footprint in Europe is the major contribution to NATO's deterrence and defence. But Washington's geopolitical priorities are different. They have been very open about this. So what we can do about this is make ourselves stronger so that we can also stand up for ourselves.

paragraphs.text: Mariusz Kamiński (ECR), na piśmiePrezydent Lech Kaczyński ostrzegał przed nową falą rosyjskiego imperializmu już w 2008 roku podczas rosyjskiej agresji na Gruzję. Świat nie chciał wtedy słuchać. Wolał żyć w naiwności, robić interesy z Rosją, podczas gdy Kreml poprzez korupcję i służby konsekwentnie osłabiał kolektywny Zachód.Wysoka Przedstawiciel ma rację mówiąc, że odstraszanie działa tylko wtedy, gdy jest wiarygodne. Spójrzmy więc na liczby: do obrony własnego kraju gotowa jest ponad połowa społeczeństwa jedynie w państwach mojego regionu oraz w Skandynawii. Jeżeli jedynie co piąty Niemiec deklaruje gotowość do obrony własnego kraju, to dziwi mnie naiwność Litwinów wierzących, że z trudem rozmieszczana tam niemiecka brygada będzie gotowa bronić ich państwa. Czy Berlin był wiarygodny w pierwszych tygodniach wojny, gdy Ukrainie oferował stare hełmy?Ironicznie, kilka godzin przed tą debatą, europejski establishment postanowił uhonorować Angelę Merkel, polityk, która świadomie, wbrew ostrzeżeniom Polski, uzależniała Europę od rosyjskiego gazu, traktowała Moskwę jako strategicznego partnera, a poprzez format normandzki, wykluczający mój region oraz Stany Zjednoczone, próbowała decydować o bezpieczeństwie Europy.Dlatego przestrzegam przed wykorzystywaniem kwestii obronności do prób federalizacji Unii i wypychania Stanów Zjednoczonych z Europy. Dzisiejsza debata jest tego najlepszym przykładem. Nie wiemy jeszcze dokładnie, co oznacza wstrzymanie rotacji amerykańskiej brygady w Polsce. Pozwólmy działać prezydentowi Karolowi Nawrockiemu.

paragraphs.text: Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), in writingAmerican soldiers, American weapons, American budgets, American political will to defend Europe.For decades Europe has enjoyed of privileged status under the protection of greatest military power in human history.And now as Washington reduces parts of its military presence in Europe, the response from many across this continent has been irritation, denial and blame.The ”socialist Spanish flu” afflicting Europe has led many here to forget a fundamental truth:Ultimately, the defence of Europe is Europe’s own responsibility.If the US steps back, Europe must step up.Defense cannot be outsourced indefinitely.The gap left by the US must be filled by European investment, European forces and European political will.The time for free riders is over.

paragraphs.text: Yvan Verougstraete (Renew), par écritRécemment, nous avons été témoins d’une réduction significative de la présence militaire américaine sur le sol Européen. Cette tendance avait déjà commencé l’année dernière, mais elle se confirme désormais mois après mois, semaine après semaine. Que ce soit en Roumanie ou en Pologne, ce désengagement est remarqué, avec des conséquences importantes pour ces régions. Ce retrait d’une partie des troupes américaines et des missiles de notre continent doit servir d'électrochoc stratégique. Notre dépendance sur la protection américaine est devenue un point de faiblesse pour notre Union. Nous entrons maintenant dans une nouvelle ère, où le free riding sur les Etats Unis ne peut plus être le status quo. Il est devenu dangereux pour l’Europe de croiser les doigts et espérer que l’humeur politique à la Maison Blanche soit pro européenne. Il est temps que nous reprenions notre destin en main et que nous allions de l'avant pour une souveraineté et défense européenne.

interventions.speaker_label: Kaja Kallas, Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, the situation in Cuba is getting more serious by the day. After decades of decisions of harming the country and its own population, Cuba urgently needs to make fundamental changes. The status quo is not admissible anymore.

These changes should include the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms of the Cuban people, releasing all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained, meaningful political and economic reforms. But more than ever, Cuba needs to open up to democracy. This message is crystal clear and an absolute consensus between our Member States. Of course, Cuba must also distance itself from those who undermine international law and the UN Charter.

But before speaking about geopolitics and diplomacy, let me start with the Cuban people. Today, millions of Cubans face daily power outages, shortage of medicines and food, collapsing public services and growing difficulties in accessing even the most basic healthcare. Hospitals struggle to function; families spent hours searching for fuel, transport and essential products. The country's energy crisis is a result of decades of structural economic failures, poor policies and the impact of ongoing external restrictions and measures. To make a bad situation even worse, the economic crisis is growing. Humanitarian access and humanitarian support must remain protected under all circumstances.

The European Union will continue to support the Cuban population with humanitarian assistance, including an additional EUR 6 million recently mobilised to address the urgent needs. Our financial support is implemented through international organisations, Member States, agencies and European partners. It supports Cuban people. The European Union does not finance the Cuban state.

Honourable Members, the resilience of the Cuban people is extraordinary. But resilience cannot replace reform. It cannot compensate for economic failure and growing isolation. Humanitarian support will not solve Cuba's crisis, but will merely alleviate immediate human suffering. Cubans deserve a better life. They deserve greater freedom and opportunity. The choice to stabilise the situation and thereby open a credible path forward can only come from the inside. Havana should not postpone important decisions any longer.

Along with ending political repression, Havana should also end the uncompromising grip on the economy that is holding the country back. Openness to private initiative, investment, entrepreneurship and economic modernisation is essential. Havana needs to find the courage to take decisions in order to avoid collapse and improve the situation for its people.

The European Union has played an important role in accompanying reforms, particularly through support to small businesses and entrepreneurs. But it can only work and have the proper impact together with reforms' clear opening for the economy. Sustainable economic reform cannot happen without legal certainty, independent economic actors and freedom, including for the citizens to express themselves. This is why the European Union consistently raises the situation of political prisoners, restrictions on fundamental freedoms, and the need for meaningful reforms. Our political and cooperation agreement establishes the framework and channels to systematically raise these divergences. It's not a way to ignore our differences; it's an instrument to address them. But this agreement is also not a silver bullet. We all want to improve the way this agreement delivers.

Honourable Members, with regards to current developments, the EU's position is clear: Havana should end the political repression and its uncompromising grip on the economy that is holding the country back. The decisions need to stabilise the situation and a credible path forward can only be made by Cubans themselves. Further instability in Cuba only risks greater humanitarian, migratory and security consequences for the Cuban people, but also for the wider region. Negotiated reform today is preferable to collapse tomorrow.

interventions.speaker_label: David McAllister, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Madam High Representative, dear colleagues, more than six decades the people of Cuba are suffering under the continuous repression of the authoritarian regime, and I would like to underline many things High Representative / Vice-President Kallas just mentioned.

In light of this worrying situation on the island, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, jointly with our Subcommittee on Human Rights, held an exchange of views on the developments in Cuba two weeks ago and welcomed Mr José Ferrer. He is, above all, a staunch human rights activist and one of the leading voices of the Cuban opposition. Since 2003, Mr Ferrer has been continuously persecuted and several times been imprisoned. During his captivity, he was inadequately supplied with food, he was refused medical treatment and he had to endure solitary confinement. That's why his detention was subject to a resolution of our House, of this Parliament, in September 2024.

Now, although Mr Ferrer had the opportunity to leave his country in 2025, today, more than 700 political prisoners are still unable to. They are still held captive by the regime. Like Mr Ferrer, these prisoners are denied a fair and impartial trials. They are frequently subjected to overcrowded and unsanitary conditions, and they have only inadequate access to food, water and medical supplies. What I'm saying is, as they are being silenced, the European Parliament must raise its voice for the brave women and men in Cuba who are suffering under this repression, but who refuse to give up their legitimate fight. I call for their immediate and unconditional release.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: en nombre del Grupo S&D

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señora vicepresidenta Kallas, no es la primera vez ni seguramente la última que hablamos en esta Cámara del pueblo de Cuba, pero me gustaría que, por primera vez —al menos por esta vez—, realmente hagamos un debate pensando en el pueblo de Cuba y no en otros intereses, y que defendamos una posición coherente y clara de la Unión Europea basada en los valores que veíamos esta mañana en el vídeo.

Hablemos, pues, del pueblo cubano, de las personas que están sufriendo una crisis humanitaria insoportable desde hace muchos años, desde el bloqueo estadounidense y, especialmente, desde las sanciones que han adoptado en el último tiempo. Ha habido apagones, escasez de alimentos y medicamentos y dificultades de acceso a servicios básicos como el agua, la educación o la sanidad; llevamos décadas denunciándolo. Señorías, la ciudadanía nunca debe ser ni debe pagar el precio de las diferencias políticas ni de las causas, por muy justas que estas parezcan. ¿Hay alguien que realmente crea que esta es la forma de avanzar en la agenda de derechos humanos o en reformas políticas? ¿El sufrimiento de la población programado y deliberado?

Señorías, somos muy claros: los Estados Unidos deben poner fin a todo tipo de coerción en Cuba. La Unión Europea debe seguir enviando efectivamente y sosteniendo la ayuda humanitaria y blindando el Derecho internacional. Y con la misma claridad digo que el Gobierno de Cuba debe avanzar de una vez por todas en las reformas democráticas. La liberación de presos es bienvenida, pero para nada es suficiente. Todos los presos políticos deben ser liberados. Se debe garantizar la libertad de expresión y el espacio cívico.

Por eso, señora Kallas, hoy más que nunca, el Acuerdo de Diálogo Político y de Cooperación entre la UE y Cuba es un buen instrumento. No es un cheque en blanco, efectivamente; sirve para empujar y para avanzar. La Unión Europea debe estar más presente que nunca, desde la profunda solidaridad con el pueblo cubano, denunciando las injerencias extranjeras y con un firme compromiso con los derechos humanos y la agenda democrática.

interventions.speaker_label: Hermann Tertsch, en nombre del Grupo PfE.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: en nombre del Grupo PfE

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, señora Kallas, resulta realmente desesperante: 67 años de dictadura, un régimen comunista asesino, que tiene encarcelados a sus hijos, que ha hecho la cárcel más grande del mundo desde hace más de seis décadas. Y aquí estamos hablando de que hay que hacer unas reformas, de que no se intervenga.

¿Saben lo que pasa? Esta dictadura está ahora más cerca que nunca del colapso, por su brutal y abismal fracaso general, que no genera más que miseria, miedo, hambre y muerte, y gracias también a la acción de la política norteamericana. Sí, aquí ha estado —se ha citado ahora— José Daniel Ferrer y aquí ha estado Zoé Valdés. ¿Y qué han pedido los dos? Intervención norteamericana para acabar con la dictadura miserable de los Castro y de la mafia comunista. Eso es lo que se pide. Y eso es lo que pide cualquiera que tenga sentido común y que tenga un poco de compasión y piedad por el pueblo cubano, torturado desde hace 67 años.

¿Y qué hace la Unión Europea? Mantiene desde hace una década un vergonzoso Acuerdo de Diálogo Político y de Cooperación con la dictadura, que la dictadura no cumple en ningún punto. Este Acuerdo ha proporcionado a la dictadura una supuesta legitimidad y millones de euros del contribuyente europeo. Me dice la alta representante que va a la sociedad civil, que no va a la dictadura. Pero ¿qué conoce usted de Cuba realmente para pensar que algún dinero de esos va realmente a la sociedad civil, sino que va a las organizaciones del partido que aterrorizan al pueblo y va a los grupos mafiosos de la cúpula de la dictadura?

Ha proporcionado, además, un precioso oxígeno a un régimen en agonía para que continuara extendiendo sus tentáculos de violencia, crimen y subversión por toda Iberoamérica, vertiendo su veneno por todas partes allí.
Por eso, hay que acabar con este Acuerdo y hay que ayudar a derribar la dictadura de una vez por todas. Todo lo demás es complicidad con el crimen.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca, Pani Wysoka Przedstawiciel! Komunizm na Kubie jest w agonii. Jedynie brutalna siła podtrzymuje reżim przy władzy. Nie ma on żadnej demokratycznej ani moralnej legitymacji do rządzenia narodem kubańskim. Podstawowe prawa człowieka i obywatela na Kubie nie istnieją. Wszelkie przejawy oporu społecznego są tłumione, a w więzieniach w tragicznych warunkach przetrzymywana jest rekordowa liczba ponad 1200 więźniów politycznych.

Pani Wysoka Przedstawiciel, czy widziała Pani zdjęcia Aleksandra Diaz Rodrigueza, który po wyjściu z więzienia wyglądał jak więzień Auschwitz? Czy wysłuchała Pani wstrząsających świadectw byłych więźniarek o torturach, gwałtach, niewolniczej pracy i odbieraniu im ludzkiej godności? Czy dotarły do Pani nowe fakty dotyczące skrytobójczych mordów dokonywanych przez Komunistyczną Służbę Bezpieczeństwa na niezależnych działaczach, takich jak Oswaldo Payá?

Pytam Panią Wysoką Przedstawiciel, bo wbrew jasno wyrażonej woli Parlamentu Europejskiego umowa o dialogu i współpracy między Unią a Kubą jest kontynuowana. Przecież warunkiem jej podpisania była zgoda reżimu w Hawanie na respektowanie praw człowieka. Niedawno gościem Parlamentu Europejskiego był legendarny bojownik o wolność Kuby Daniel Ferrer. W komunistycznych więzieniach spędził kilkanaście lat. On też w imieniu zwykłych Kubańczyków apelował o zawieszenie tej umowy. Jej dalsze utrzymanie jest legitymizowaniem zbrodniczego reżimu. Komunistyczna dyktatura na Kubie musi upaść. I właśnie to jest ten moment.

Przecież warunkiem jej podpisania była zgoda reżimu w Hawanie na respektowanie praw człowieka. Niedawno gościem Parlamentu Europejskiego był legendarny bojownik o wolność Kuby Daniel Ferrer. W komunistycznych więzieniach spędził kilkanaście lat. On też w imieniu zwykłych Kubańczyków apelował o zawieszenie tej umowy. Jej dalsze utrzymanie jest legitymizowaniem zbrodniczego reżimu. Komunistyczna dyktatura na Kubie musi upaść. I właśnie to jest ten moment.

interventions.speaker_label: João Cotrim De Figueiredo, em nome do Grupo Renew.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: em nome do Grupo Renew

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Alta Representante, a fome, a miséria, o medo, o desespero e a repressão política em Cuba não são um acaso. A crise humanitária é, sobretudo, o resultado deliberado de um regime comunista brutal que há mais de seis décadas oprime sem piedade o seu próprio povo em benefício de uma elite corrupta.

O regime ameaça, prende, tortura e deixa apodrecer nas masmorras todos os que se lhe opõem. Um desses, que foi torturado selvaticamente e resistiu sempre, foi José Daniel Ferrer, líder da UNPACO (União Patriótica de Cuba), o movimento mais representativo da oposição cubana.

José Daniel esteve recentemente no Parlamento Europeu a apresentar um plano de transição para a democracia em Cuba. Nas nossas conversas, José Daniel não pediu dinheiro, não pediu armas, não pediu intervenções externas — pediu apoio político. Pediu, por exemplo, que a União Europeia suspendesse de imediato o acordo de diálogo político de cooperação com Cuba, porque ele confirmou o que todos já suspeitávamos, Senhora Alta Representante: o dinheiro, ao abrigo deste acordo, não chega ao povo cubano; financia o aparelho repressivo do regime e enche os bolsos da elite comunista, enquanto o povo cubano morre à fome. É uma vergonha que a Europa continue a dar oxigénio a esta tirania torcionária, prolongando a crise humanitária.

E José Daniel Ferrer pediu outra coisa: que a inação da União Europeia não faça Cuba passar de uma ditadura comunista para uma dependência de Washington. É uma posição lúcida e corajosa que a Europa tem de apoiar. Basta de cumplicidade com o comunismo. Só há uma escolha: ou a União Europeia suspende este acordo de cooperação pondo-se ao lado dos que lutam pela liberdade em Cuba, ou será cúmplice da opressão continuada do povo cubano.
Como dizem os valentes democratas em Cuba: «Pátria ou vida, vencerá.»

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: en nombre del Grupo Verts/ALE

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, cuando las hienas huelen sangre, se ríen. Es lo que les pasa aquí a muchos, no les preocupa nada el pueblo cubano y se ríen. La situación de Cuba no puede analizarse ignorando el contexto de bloqueo, la agresión permanente a la que ha sido sometida durante años y las décadas de embargo por parte de los Estados Unidos.

Todos los países del mundo han votado en contra, menos Estados Unidos y sus lacayos. Es profundamente irresponsable hablar de un Estado fallido cuando, en realidad, Cuba se enfrenta a un escenario forzado e inducido externamente. ¿Me pueden decir qué país del mundo podrá resistir sesenta y cuatro años de bloqueo ilegal? Déjense de propaganda yanqui y tengan decencia por una vez.

Ningún pueblo puede aguantar una situación así y menos en las condiciones de dignidad como lo hace el pueblo cubano. Y Europa debe seguir, señora Kallas, haciendo esa solidaridad con Cuba, que es merecida porque estamos hablando de las consecuencias para un pueblo.

Cuba ha ayudado con vacunas y médicos a la humanidad. Pero lo que está pasando es un castigo colectivo por parte de Trump que está asfixiando a los cubanos. No permitamos que las hienas del imperialismo permitan una invasión a Cuba. Como decimos en el BNG, «¡Cuba sí, yanquis fóra!».

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, oggi parliamo di Cuba e con la solita, magistrale ipocrisia di questo Parlamento, riusciamo a parlare di diritti umani senza citare l'elefante nella stanza: l'embargo statunitense che va avanti da 66 anni.

Quello che nascondete sotto al tappeto è ciò che tutto questo vuol dire: assenza di energia e beni di prima necessità a danno dei più fragili: donne incinte, anziani, disabili, bambini e soprattutto malati oncologici.

E l'Europa cosa fa? Mentre Trump parla di dottrina Monroe 2.0, questo dibattito serve solo a coprire l'ennesima azione neocoloniale. E non raccontate che il problema sono i diritti umani, perché dovreste spiegarci come mai non interrompete l'accordo di associazione con Israele o non intervenite a difendere gli attivisti della Flotilla.
L'Europa dovrebbe tutelare l'accordo di cooperazione con Cuba per mettere fine all'illegale blocco economico che strangola l'isola da troppo tempo.

Da italiano, non dimenticherò mai le brigate cubane accorse a sostenere la nostra sanità, messa in ginocchio da anni di vostre politiche liberiste, durante i mesi difficili della pandemia o ancora oggi, in Calabria, dove senza l'apporto dei medici cubani non si potrebbe garantire il diritto alla salute. Cuba esporta medici e solidarietà, voi armi e guerre.

Voglio concludere questo intervento citando uno dei più grandi giornalisti della storia italiana, Gianni Minà, che scrisse: "Il blocco economico contro Cuba non è una semplice sanzione commerciale, è un atto di guerra in tempo di pace. La guerra più lunga e spietata della storia moderna, un tentativo sistematico di prendere per fame e per malattia un intero popolo, colpevole unicamente di non essersi voluto piegare al padrone di turno".

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: im Namen der ESN-Fraktion

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Kuba ist heute der billigste Puff der Karibik. Die extreme Armut zwingt junge Kubaner in die Prostitution. Organisiert wird der Sextourismus von Armeechef Raúl Castro, dem Bruder von Fidel Castro.

Linke Parteien sehen Kuba als Vorbild. Erst vor vier Wochen fand in Barcelona eine Konferenz der Sozialisten statt. Auch der deutsche Vizekanzler Lars Klingbeil war da. In der Abschlusserklärung zeigten sich die Teilnehmer besorgt über die humanitäre Lage auf Kuba. Sie fordern ein klares Bekenntnis zu Menschenrechten und Demokratie.

Man sollte meinen, dass sich die Forderungen an die Machthaber in Havanna richten. Doch weit gefehlt: Europas Sozialdemokraten haben mit der sozialistischen Diktatur auf Kuba kein Problem – aber mit Donald Trump. Kuba sei nämlich nur deshalb so arm, weil Washington ein Embargo verhängt habe. Die Wahrheit ist: Trotz fruchtbarer Böden und tropischem Klima muss Kuba 80 % seiner Lebensmittel importieren. Warum? Weil Armut, Hunger und Repression immer die Folgen sozialistischer Misswirtschaft sind. Deshalb müssen wir den Freunden der kubanischen Diktatur das Handwerk legen!
Die Zeit der Sozialdemokraten ist abgelaufen. So wie die Zeit von Raúl Castro auf Kuba.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, una isla sumida en la oscuridad con apagones que alcanzan hasta veinte horas diarias es un buen ejemplo de aquello en lo que el régimen ha convertido a Cuba. Pero esa oscuridad va mucho más allá: durante demasiado tiempo, el miedo a la represión —a acabar en prisión y engrosar la lista de los más de 1 200 presos políticos que hoy siguen encarcelados— y la ausencia de libertad han obligado a la población cubana a soportar en silencio condiciones de vida deplorables.

Y algunos lograron escapar. Otros resisten desde dentro, pero todos comparten una única esperanza, la esperanza de recuperar todo aquello que les ha sido arrebatado. Hoy es hora de reiterar que el Acuerdo de Diálogo Político y Cooperación no ha servido en absoluto para avanzar en la democracia en Cuba. La represión y la violencia contra los disidentes y los activistas de derechos humanos siguen siendo una realidad. La libertad de expresión y de asociación siguen viéndose restringidas y las cárceles están llenas de presos políticos. La Unión Europea debería sentir vergüenza por mantener un acuerdo en estas condiciones.

Dicho esto, me atrevo a decir que mantenemos una visión optimista sobre el destino final de un pueblo al que queremos: una transición hacia una democracia robusta y pluralista. Señora alta representante: dialogue con el régimen, convénzale de que tiene que cambiar, de que la Unión Europea quiere ayudarles. Nuestra confianza no reside en absoluto en las estructuras actuales, sino en el extraordinario potencial del pueblo cubano. La meta es clara: una Cuba donde la democracia no sea un anhelo, sino una realidad.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la crisi umanitaria a Cuba ha radici diverse e profonde, ma bisogna essere chiari, signora Alta rappresentante: la tenaglia stretta dall'amministrazione USA non libera i cubani, li condanna a fame e insicurezza con l'inasprimento dell'embargo sino al blocco delle forniture petrolifere, le sanzioni secondarie, che colpiscono anche imprese europee, e la minaccia costante di un'azione militare.
Trump non vuole la democrazia a Cuba, vuole Cuba. Non possiamo essere suoi complici.
È invece il dialogo con governo e società civile cubani che produce risultati concreti, come confermano le recenti liberazioni di oppositori politici mediate dalla Santa Sede.

Chiediamo perciò fermamente all'Avana di garantire il rispetto dei diritti umani e il libero accesso degli osservatori internazionali e chiediamo all'Unione – a noi stessi – di mantenere aperto il dialogo con Cuba nell'interesse del suo popolo.
Il dialogo non è debolezza: è il vero metodo dell'Europa.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la tragedia di Cuba non è un incidente della storia, ma il risultato prevedibile di 67 anni di dittatura comunista: i blackout prolungati, gli ospedali senza corrente, la fuga di migliaia di giovani, le centinaia di prigionieri politici, le repressioni e le torture sono il frutto di un sistema che ha distrutto l'economia, ha soppresso le libertà e mantenuto il potere con la forza e la propaganda.
Il comunismo ha fallito a Cuba, come ovunque abbia governato: produce sempre miseria, censura, gulag e corruzione dell'élite al potere.

L'Europa e l'Occidente non possono più fingere di non vedere che la gente muore di fame, vive al buio e finisce in prigione per aver chiesto libertà e pane. I cubani non chiedono un socialismo dal volto umano, chiedono libertà, democrazia e la fine di un sistema che li ha imprigionati per generazioni. Meritavano di riprendersi il loro paese. È tempo di smettere di sostenere i carnefici e iniziare a sostenere il popolo.
La Storia ha già emesso il suo verdetto sul comunismo reale: un fallimento totale.
